fix(arbitrator): resolve startup failure with missing config backup directory (#1309) (#1313)

* fix(arbitrator): resolve startup failure with missing config backup directory (#1309)

The arbitrator service was failing to start with error "Monitoring config
backup directory not defined" due to multiple issues:

1. Duplicate flag parsing: Go's flag package conflicted with Cobra, causing
   --user flag value to be lost when using --user=value syntax
2. Empty ConfDirBackup: User lookup failed with empty username, resulting in
   empty backup directory path
3. Inappropriate fatal error: Arbitrator never saves config, doesn't need
   backup directory

Changes:
- Remove duplicate flag.Parse() that conflicted with Cobra flag handling
- Add WithArbitration compile-time flag to identify arbitrator binary
- Skip ConfDirBackup requirement when WithArbitration="ON"
- Fix systemd service files to use correct Cobra flag syntax (--user repman)

The fix maintains all safety checks for server deployments while allowing
the arbitrator to start without requiring a config backup directory.

* fix(arbitrator): address code review findings

Fixes identified during code review:

CRITICAL:
- Remove unused "flag" import that broke build

HIGH:
- Guard os.MkdirAll(ConfDirBackup) to skip when arbitrator mode
- Add WithArbitration check to PushConfigToBackupDir() early return

MEDIUM:
- Add Restart=on-failure to arbitrator systemd service for consistency
- Also removed trailing space from Description line

These changes prevent the arbitrator from attempting filesystem operations
on empty ConfDirBackup paths while maintaining full functionality for
server builds.

* fix(arbitrator): add missing --user flag and restore WithArbitration setting

The --user flag was not registered in arbitrator's command flags after
removing duplicate flag.Parse(). This caused "unknown flag: --user" error.

Changes:
- Add --user flag as PersistentFlag on rootCmd
- Add server package import to access WithArbitration variable
- Use local withArbitration constant and assign to server.WithArbitration

This restores the --user flag functionality for the arbitrator command
while maintaining the cleaner flag handling approach.

bytes variable comparison

The staged content adds intelligent value comparison logic for database variables to handle three different types of values:

Key Features Added:
Size Unit Normalization (parseSizeToBytes)

Converts size units (K, M, G, T, KB, MB, GB, TB) to bytes using BigInt
Handles values larger than JavaScript's MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (>9 petabytes)
Supports decimal values like 1.5G
Parses plain numeric strings as bytes
Size Variable Detection (isSizeVariable)

Identifies size-related variables by name patterns
Detects variables ending with: _size, _buffer, _memory, _cache, _length, _limit
Detects variables starting with: max_, min_
Detects InnoDB and buffer/cache related variables
Unified Comparison Logic (areValuesEqual)

Smart comparison that handles:
Boolean variables: ON/OFF, 1/0, TRUE/FALSE are treated as equivalent
Size variables: 4G equals 4294967296 bytes
Regular variables: Standard string comparison
Prevents false positives when comparing different representations of the same value
Impact:
Replaced all manual comparison logic throughout the component (7 locations)
Variables like innodb_buffer_pool_size with value 4G in configurator now correctly matches 4294967296 in runtime
Eliminates incorrect "difference" alerts for semantically equal values
Supports extremely large database configurations (terabyte-scale) without precision loss

fix: use correct TLS config name in mysql.RegisterTLSConfig

The Go MySQL driver's RegisterTLSConfig expects a plain name (e.g.
"tlsconfig") that matches the value after "tls=" in the DSN. The
constants ConstTLSCurrentConfig and ConstTLSOldConfig contain the
full DSN fragment ("&tls=tlsconfig"), which was incorrectly passed
as the registration name. The driver then looks up "tlsconfig" but
finds nothing registered under that name, silently falling back to
no TLS.

Split the constants into DSN fragments (unchanged) and registration
names (new), and use the registration names in RegisterTLSConfig.

This fixes TLS connections to MySQL 8.4 with caching_sha2_password,
which requires TLS for initial authentication.

fix(app): debounce transient APPERR flapping

Only emit APPERR after three consecutive app check failures to reduce intermittent timeout noise, and map TCP connectivity failures to APPERR001 to keep connection diagnostics consistent.

fix(app): correct app monitoring debounce semantics

- Per-route debounce: AppErrConsecutiveMap replaces single shared counter.
  Failures are now tracked per route-key per GetMonitoringStatus call,
  preventing counter inflation when multiple routes fail in one tick.
- Isolated counter reset: success on one route no longer clears failure
  history on other routes.
- Immediate config-error emission: no-routes and unsupported protocol
  now emit APPERR immediately without debouncing.
- Temporary TCP dual emission: TCP failures emit both APPERR003 (canonical)
  and APPERR001 (compatibility) after threshold, for migration window.
- Configurable threshold: new cluster-level
  app-error-debounce-threshold (default 3) replaces hardcoded constant.

fix(app): remove incoherent AppErrConsecutiveCnt scalar counter

- Drop AppErrConsecutiveCnt in favour of AppErrConsecutiveMap as the
  single source of truth for per-route debounce state. The scalar
  was last-writer-wins and misleading in multi-route scenarios.
- Add targeted comment on APPERR004 formatting confirming argument
  order matches the format string; test now asserts exact ErrDesc.
- Add test for no-routes global counter reset and for per-route map
  isolation under mixed success/failure.

fix(app): remove dead bool return and eliminate port-race in tests

- Drop the unused bool return from debouncedRecordAppErr closure; it was
  purely side-effect based and the return value was discarded everywhere.
- Replace ephemeral-port-bind-then-close pattern in two TCP failure tests
  with a stable closed endpoint (127.0.0.1:1) to prevent spurious success
  if the OS reuses the freed port before the dial completes.

change credentials through the API, rather than waiting for the
next monitor tick.

add manual secret-store pruning utility

Add reusable secret-store pruning helpers in cluster package and a
manual server command to prune per-cluster secret history by keeping
only the last N versions per key.

The command supports dry-run output and reuses the same core logic so
future scheduled pruning can call the same implementation safely.

Tests added for prune behavior, dry-run semantics, and cluster lookup
error handling.

add manual secret-store copy utility with hash dedupe

secret history to {monitoring-confdir}/cluster.d/{cluster}_secret_store.json.

Use raw-byte SHA256 comparison to avoid redundant copies, support dry-run
and overwrite controls, and keep copy/write logic reusable for future
scheduled invocation without duplicating behavior.

Also add tests for copy, dedupe, overwrite gate, dry-run semantics,
and server-side cluster/confdir path resolution.

add secret-store restore utility for cluster config

for a safe runtime subset, and add resolver/listing helpers with tests.

feat(logplugin): add binlog security plugins for cleartext-password and credit-card leak detection

Introduces incremental binlog QUERY event scanning via a persistent
replication.BinlogSyncer kept open on each ServerMonitor.  On every
CheckLogPlugins tick, newly-arrived events are drained (50 ms budget)
into a BinlogEventLog ring buffer and passed to external plugins
through the existing wire protocol.

No double-fetch: reuses server.BinaryLogFile (already refreshed by
CheckBinaryLogs) — no extra GetMasterStatus query.  On binlog
rotation or server failure the syncer is closed and reopened cleanly
via CloseBinlogEventSyncer(), called from SetFailed() and Close().

New config flags:
  log-plugin-binlog-scan              (bool, default false)
  monitoring-binlog-event-log-length  (int,  default 200)

New external plugins:
  plugin-binlog-cleartext-password  WARN0310 — detects IDENTIFIED BY /
    SET PASSWORD literals in binlog QUERY events
  plugin-binlog-creditcard-leak     WARN0311 — detects Luhn-valid PAN
    candidates in binlog QUERY events

Wire protocol (wire.Request / StdioRequest / LogSource) extended with
BinlogEvents []BinlogEvent field; backwards-compatible (empty slice
when scan is disabled).

causing locked accounts (e.g. mariadb.sys) to appear unlocked and raise

unlocked. Using = 'true' for explicit string comparison fixes the false
positive for locked accounts like mariadb.sys.

fix(plugins): fix mutex-copy deadlock in snapshotHttpLog/snapshotSlowLog

snapshotHttpLog(s18log.HttpLog) and snapshotSlowLog(s18log.SlowLog) took
their arguments BY VALUE.  Both structs embed sync.Mutex.  Copying a mutex
is forbidden by the Go memory model: if ErrorLogWatcher (or SlowLogWatcher)
holds server.ErrorLog.L at the exact moment the monitoring loop copies the
struct for the argument, the copy has mutex.state=1 (locked).  The subsequent
log.L.Lock() inside the snapshot function then sleeps on a semaphore that
nobody will ever signal → permanent deadlock in the monitoring goroutine.
This is why cluster.StateMachine.heartbeats stays at 1 on clusters with
plugins enabled: CheckLogPlugins() blocks forever after the first tick.

Fix: change both functions to take *s18log.HttpLog and *s18log.SlowLog
(pointer parameters) and update the three call sites accordingly.

fix(plugins): set WaitDelay on external plugin subprocesses to prevent monitoring loop hang

When a plugin subprocess spawns children that inherit the stdout/stderr
pipes, cmd.Output() blocks forever waiting for pipe EOF even after the
5-second context timeout kills the plugin binary.  This caused the
monitoring loop to freeze at heartbeats=1 on clusters with external plugins.

Set cmd.WaitDelay = 2s so that Go forcibly closes the I/O goroutines 2
seconds after the context fires, guaranteeing cmd.Output() returns within
p.timeout + 2s regardless of orphaned subprocesses.

Also treat exec.ErrWaitDelay the same as DeadlineExceeded so the finding
correctly reports "plugin timed out" in both cases.

fix(plugins): isolate external plugin registry per-cluster to prevent cross-cluster hang

GlobalRegistry was a process-wide singleton shared across all clusters.
When cluster A (belair) loaded 23 external plugins into GlobalRegistry,
every other cluster's CheckLogPlugins() also iterated over those 23
plugins and spawned subprocesses for each of its servers — even clusters
configured with log-plugin=false or with no plugins installed.

Any subprocess that hung (pipe leak, slow binary) froze ALL cluster
monitoring loops, causing heartbeats to stall for every cluster.

Fix: introduce NewRegistry() that clones GlobalRegistry's built-in
plugins into a fresh Registry.  Each cluster now owns a pluginRegistry
populated only with its own external plugins.  ReloadLogPlugins resets
the cluster registry to a fresh built-in clone before scanning the
cluster-specific plugin dir, so removed binaries also disappear on
hot-reload.

fix: change RelayLogSpace from sql.NullInt64 to sql.Null[uint64]

Percona/MySQL 8.4 can return Relay_Log_Space as a large uint64 that exceeds
int64 range, causing SHOW REPLICA STATUS parsing to fail with:
  sql: Scan error on column index 22, name \"Relay_Log_Space\":
  converting driver.Value type uint64 to a int64: value out of range

This scan failure causes the replica to disappear from topology detection,
leading to cascading failures:
- slave seen as StandAlone
- no failover candidates available
- automatic failover can create split-brain

The fix changes the field type to sql.Null[uint64] which safely handles
large unsigned values and preserves NULL semantics.

Also adds comprehensive tests covering:
- NULL, uint64, int64, MaxUint64, negative rejection
- []byte and string numeric inputs
- overflow and non-numeric rejection

fix: stable findings for SEC0101/SEC0107/SEC0108/SEC0118 — sort user lists, single finding

Each of these checks was emitting one finding per affected user, and since
DatabaseUsers arrives in non-deterministic order the description changed every
monitoring tick, causing spurious state-machine transitions.

Fix: collect all affected accounts, sort them alphabetically, then emit a
single finding with the full sorted list. The description is now identical
across ticks as long as the set of affected accounts doesn't change.

- SEC0101 (weak-auth): one finding listing all weak-plugin accounts sorted
- SEC0107 (anon users): one finding listing all anonymous hosts sorted
- SEC0108 (wildcard host): one finding listing all '%'-host accounts sorted
- SEC0118 (hostname grants): one finding listing all DNS-hostname accounts sorted

fix: AND semantics for SecurityScore — all servers must pass for cluster to pass

Root cause of HasAuditPlugins (and other per-server checks) flapping between
PASS/FAIL: ApplyCheck was a plain assignment, so the last server to run in the
monitoring loop overwrote all previous results. With a 2-server cluster where
master has no audit and replica does, the score toggled every tick depending on
iteration order.

Fix: SecurityScore.ApplyCheck now uses AND semantics. The first server to report
a tag sets its value; subsequent servers AND with the accumulated result. A replica
that passes a check cannot mask a master that fails it.

- Add `applied map[string]struct{}` to SecurityScore (unexported, reset each tick
  when SecurityScore{} is assigned)
- Split ApplyCheck into getCheck/setCheck helpers
- Add TestSecurityScore_ApplyCheck_ANDSemantics covering the exact 2-server
  flapping scenario (master-fail/replica-pass, master-pass/replica-fail, both-pass)

Also: stable SEC0101/SEC0107/SEC0108/SEC0118 findings (sorted user lists,
single finding per check) — already committed separately.

fix: eliminate SecurityScore flash-to-all-FAIL by using local accumulator

Root cause: CheckLogPlugins reset cluster.SecurityScore = SecurityScore{} at the
start of each tick, making all 19 check fields false until ApplyCheck/Compute
repopulated them. Any concurrent HTTP read (dashboard polling) during that window
saw all checks as FAIL.

Fix:
- Accumulate score checks into a local SecurityScore (newScore) across all servers
- Call Compute() once after all servers have run
- Assign cluster.SecurityScore = newScore as a single atomic swap at the end

Side effects fixed:
- RunLogPlugins now takes *SecurityScore instead of modifying cluster.SecurityScore
  directly, making the data flow explicit
- Per-server Compute() calls removed; score is only computed once per tick with
  the full cluster-wide AND result

Portal's inject_plugins.sh delivers plugin binaries into {cluster}/plugins/
inside the -pull GitLab repo.  PullCloud18Configs clones that repo to
WorkingDir/.pull but nothing moved the files to WorkingDir/{cluster}/plugins/
where ReloadLogPlugins looks for them.

Add syncPluginsFromPull: called after each successful pull, it MD5-compares
each binary in .pull/{cluster}/plugins/ against the destination and only
copies files that have actually changed, then triggers ReloadLogPlugins once
per cluster that had updates — avoiding unnecessary reloads every cycle.

- WARN0313: no plugin binaries in cluster/plugins/ → not registered, sign up

WARN0314 includes a direct API link to the switch endpoint so the operator
can enable log-plugin with one click from the dashboard:

Fix plugin-signing.pub being executed as a plugin binary

plugin-signing.pub starts with plugin- so LoadPluginsFromDir passed the name
check; syncPluginsFromPull also chmod'd all copied files 0755 unconditionally,
making it executable, causing fork/exec format errors at runtime.

Fix 1 (external.go): skip any file with a non-empty extension in
LoadPluginsFromDir — plugin binaries are always extension-less.

Fix 2 (server_git.go): only chmod 0755 files with no extension in
syncPluginsFromPull so .pub and .sig files are never made executable.

Fix WARN0314 not visible: flush state machines before early return

When log-plugin=false, WARN0314 was correctly added to SecurityStateMachine
and WorkloadStateMachine but the GetOpenStates() calls that populate
cluster.SecurityStates / cluster.WorkloadStates (what the dashboard reads)
were only reachable after the early return, so the state was never exposed.

Flush both slices before returning in the disabled branch.

Split WARN0313: security warning vs INFO0315 workload nudge

Built-in workload plugins (error-log 24h, slow-query 24h) run as soon as
log-plugin=true so a WARNING on the workload machine when no external
plugins are loaded is misleading.

- INFO0315 fires on the WorkloadStateMachine: built-in analysis is active,

Both states are cleared when external plugins are loaded.

Fix cloud18 connect blocking HTTP server by running InitGitConfig async

InitGitConfig makes 5+ sequential HTTP calls to GitLab (OAuth token,
user lookup, group access, PAT rotation/creation). Running it synchronously
in the HTTP handler blocked all other browser requests for 5+ seconds.

Set Cloud18=true optimistically and launch InitGitConfig in a goroutine.
The handler returns 200 immediately. If InitGitConfig fails in the
background, Cloud18 is reverted to false and the UI reflects that on the
next monitor poll. The goroutine calls SaveConfig when done to persist
the final state (PAT + GitUrl on success, Cloud18=false on failure).

This also correctly handles the reconnect-after-days scenario where the
PAT has expired: InitGitConfig always runs and re-authenticates with the
stored email+password credentials.

Force monitor refresh after connect/disconnect so UI updates immediately

After setGlobalSetting returns, config?.cloud18 only updates on the next
getMonitoredData polling cycle, which could be many seconds away. Dispatch
getMonitoredData immediately after connect/disconnect so the button state
(Connect ↔ Disconnect) transitions without waiting for the interval.

Lock URI fields when credentials exist, not just when connected

Disconnect is a temporary deactivation — the CRM is not notified of URI
changes. Editing domain/subdomain/zone after disconnect without going
through Unregister would orphan the old GitLab projects on the server.

URI fields are now read-only whenever hasCredentials is true (connected
or disconnected with stored creds). Only Unregister clears credentials,
which is the correct gate for URI changes.

Track uriUnlocked state after Unregister to gate URI field editing

URI fields (domain/subdomain/zone) must only be editable after an explicit
Unregister call, which is the CRM call that drops both the GitLab projects
and the subscription DB record for the old URI. Disconnect alone is not
enough — the CRM still holds the URI record.

After successful Unregister: uriUnlocked=true, URI fields become editable,
and hasCredentials is forced false so the UI shows Register (not Connect)
since the CRM subscription row is gone and must be recreated.

uriUnlocked resets automatically when isConnected becomes true (new
registration completed).

generation.

plugin-push fails during Docker builds because multiple concurrent
builds try to git push to the signer repo simultaneously. Docker
builds only need plugin-sigs (to embed .sig files in the image),
not plugin-push.

Default PLUGIN_PUSH=OFF. Pass PLUGIN_PUSH=ON explicitly when you
want to update the signer repo (e.g. release pipeline).

fix(ci): auto-push plugins only when wire version is new

When PLUGIN_PUSH is OFF (default), check if the signer repo already
has a wire-vN directory for the current wire version. If not, this
is a new wire version — auto-push to create it. If the directory
exists, the signer repo is already up to date — skip push.

This prevents concurrent push failures during parallel Docker builds
while still ensuring new wire versions are published automatically.

feat(plugins): auto-push to signer repo only when binaries change

Restore semantic wire version (from wire.go, not release tag).
Auto-push logic now compares SHA-256 checksums of locally built
plugin binaries against the signer repo's wire-vN directory:

- New wire version (dir missing) → push
- Existing wire version + binaries changed → push
- Existing wire version + binaries identical → skip

This ensures the signer repo stays in sync with plugin code changes
without pushing on every build or growing with duplicate binaries.

fix(configurator): prevent empty config overwrite on repman shutdown

When repman shuts down while dbjobs is fetching the config tarball,
the TCP receiver's defer cleanup fires JobFinishReceiveFile with an
empty .tmp file. This unconditionally renamed the good dummy.cnf to
.old and overwrote it with empty content. On restart, every deployed
variable appeared as "Deprecated (loose)" because the diff saw no
expected config values.

Three layers of protection:

1. Root cause: hasPrintDefaultsContent() guard in JobFinishReceiveFile
   checks that .tmp has actual --prefixed lines before overwriting
   dummy.cnf or current.cnf. Empty .tmp is skipped with a warning.

2. Delta guard: WriteDeltaVariables skips when server IsDown() or when
   VariablesMap lacks config/deployed data (HasConfigValues/HasDeployedValues).

3. GUI: ConfigFilesPanel dropdown shows host:port instead of server IDs,
   file panels stacked vertically inside Using Tags section.

registered an intentional stop.

after ShutdownClean, so the orchestrator transitions to a clean
"stopped" state. The SQL shutdown with innodb_fast_shutdown=0 still
runs first for the InnoDB full purge, then the orchestrator stop
ensures a clean state for the subsequent start.

test(regtest): add testOpenSVCUpgradeWarnRecovery

Reproduces the flacq May 2026 incident: a failed rolling upgrade
leaves OpenSVC in warn state, blocking subsequent starts with 409.

Scenario:
1. Stop slave cleanly
2. Inject broken config.tar.gz (invalid tarball)
3. Start slave — container fails, OpenSVC enters warn state
4. Verify slave is down
5. Restore good config
6. Clear instance state (per-node instance API)
7. Start slave — should succeed
8. Wait for replication sync

Requires OpenSVC orchestrator and at least one slave.

feat(monitoring): implement monitoring-schema-change-script hook

Call the configured script when a table schema change is detected
during MonitorMasterTableSchema(). The script receives:
  $1 cluster name
  $2 server URL (host:port)
  $3 schema name
  $4 table name
  $5 change type ("new" for new tables, "altered" for CRC change)

First-time cache population ("init") is skipped to avoid flooding
the script on startup when the table dictionary is empty.

The config key monitoring-schema-change-script was already registered
but never called — this wires it into the monitoring loop.

feat(monitoring): pass column diff to schema change script via stdin

The monitoring-schema-change-script now receives a unified diff of
column definitions piped to stdin:

  --- schema.table (before)
  +++ schema.table (after)
  - old_col varchar(50) NOT NULL
  + old_col varchar(100) NOT NULL
  + new_col int DEFAULT 0
  - dropped_col text

Covers all change types:
  - "new": all columns shown as additions (old is empty)
  - "altered": before/after diff of changed columns
  - "dropped": would show all columns as removals (if table tracking added)

Args unchanged: $1=cluster $2=server $3=schema $4=table $5=change_type

feat(monitoring): detect dropped tables and call schema change script

After scanning current tables, compare with cached DictTables to find
tables that no longer exist. Call the schema change script with
changeType="dropped" and all old columns as removals in the diff.

All three DDL types now covered:
  - new: table created (all cols as + additions)
  - altered: table changed (before/after column diff)
  - dropped: table removed (all cols as - removals)

fix(pr-review): address schema change script review findings

1. Explicit nil for oldCols when changeType == "new" — avoids relying
   on GetTableFromDict returning an empty-but-non-nil Table.

2. Script timeout: 30s via context.WithTimeout to prevent stalling
   the monitoring loop during active schema migrations.

3. Log output only when len(out) > 0 (avoid noisy empty log lines).

4. Unit tests for columnDiff and formatColumn covering:
   - New table (all additions, no removals)
   - Dropped table (all removals, no additions)
   - Altered table (before/after for changed, new/dropped columns)
   - Empty old and new
   - Identical columns (no diff lines)

config side of VariablesMap. They appear in the delta as variables that
exist in compliance but are rejected by the DB, allowing the user to
click Drop to remove them.

fix(backup): run jobsCheckRunningFromMemory when scheduler is off

JobsCheckRunning was only called when MonitorScheduler=true, so
backup state machine states (WARN0073, WARN0175) were never set
when the scheduler was disabled. Now calls jobsCheckRunningFromMemory
in the else branch to track backup lifecycle via flags.

fix(backup): check backup flags unconditionally each tick

Move backup state checks (InPhysicalBackup, InLogicalBackup, restic
flags) into a dedicated jobsCheckBackupStates() called every tick
regardless of MonitorScheduler or server connection state.

Previously the flag checks were inside JobsCheckRunning which could
return early on server down/no connection, never setting WARN0073
or WARN0175.

fix(backup): move backup state check to top of Ping()

jobsCheckBackupStates was unreachable inside Refresh() because it
required successful DB connection and variable fetching. Move it to
the very start of Ping() so backup states (WARN0073/WARN0175) are
always set regardless of connection state.

fix(backup): move backup state checks to cluster-level Run() loop

The backup state machine checks (WARN0073/WARN0175) were inside
per-server Refresh()/Ping() which depend on DB connectivity. When
the connection fails, the flag checks are never reached and backup
states don't appear in the state machine.

Move the check to CheckBackupStates() called from Run() before
StateProcessing(), so it runs every tick at the cluster level
regardless of per-server DB connection status.

Also fix jobsCheckRunningFromMemory() which was only checking
InResticPhysicalBackup/InResticLogicalBackup but missing
InPhysicalBackup/InLogicalBackup.

debug: add logging to trace logical backup slot acquisition and state check

fix(backup): per-server backup state for state machine tracking

The state machine is per-server but backup was tracked as a cluster-level
boolean (InLogicalBackup/InPhysicalBackup). This caused the state to be
invisible when JobsCheckRunning couldn't find the task.

Add per-server flags (IsInBackupLogical, IsInBackupPhysical) on
ServerMonitor, set alongside the backup lifecycle. CheckBackupStates()
now iterates servers to set WARN0073/WARN0175 with the correct
ServerUrl. PreserveState keeps the WARN alive during restic phase
after the main backup completes.

fix(backup): don't clear physical backup state on task insert failure

JobInsertTask can fail (leftover task, connection issue) but the SST
receiver is already running at that point. Clearing IsInBackupPhysical
makes the backup invisible to the state machine even though it's
still executing. Log the error but keep the flags set.

fix(backup): remove cluster-level backup state broadcast, show free slots

Remove InPhysicalBackup/InLogicalBackup cluster-level checks from
JobsCheckRunning and jobsCheckRunningFromMemory that were emitting
WARN0073/WARN0175 on every server in the cluster. Per-server task-based
detection remains intact. GUI shows free backup slots as single number.

fix(backup): re-set WARN0174 every poll cycle so ClearState cannot kill it

WARN0174 was set once then disappeared on the next monitoring tick
because ClearState moved it to OldState and nothing re-set it in
CurState, causing immediate resolution. Now re-set every 2s poll
iteration. State resolves naturally when slot is acquired.

feat(workload): add PFS digest plugin with covering ratio tag

New workload-pfs plugin (WTAG0200) computes PFS digest coverage:
sum(exec_count) from PFS digests vs total queries from Graphite
over the same window (since last PFS truncate). This shows what
percentage of the workload is captured by digest monitoring.

Exposes PFSLastTruncate on LogSource so the plugin can query
Graphite for the exact delta since the last TRUNCATE.
refactor(workload): rename PFS plugin to workload-pfs-digest

feat(workload): add PFS digest explain coverage tag (WTAG0201)

WTAG0201 reports what percentage of PFS digests have a cached
EXPLAIN plan. Exposes PFSExplainCount on LogSource from the
server's explain cache. Count/Total set for cluster aggregation.

feat(workload): add EXPLAIN-based full scan detection (WTAG0210)

Expose PFSExplainPlans on LogSource with plan rows (type, key, etc.).
WTAG0210 scans all cached EXPLAIN plans for type=ALL at any position,
weighted by exec_count. The percentage shows what fraction of executed
queries involve a full table scan based on actual query plans, not
just the PFS PlanFullScan flag.

feat(workload): WTAG0210 computes full scan row cost from EXPLAIN plans

Instead of counting queries, WTAG0210 now computes the row-operation
cost: sum(rows × exec_count) for type=ALL steps vs total row work
across all EXPLAIN plan steps. This shows the actual cost of full
scans as a fraction of total row operations in the workload.

Exposes PFSExplainPlans on LogSource with plan rows from the
server's cached EXPLAIN results.

feat(workload): WTAG0210 shows effective workload coverage

Chain the three metrics: digestCoverage (WTAG0200) × explainCoverage
(WTAG0201) = effective coverage. WTAG0210 now shows both the full
scan row cost percentage AND what fraction of the total workload
that observation represents.

Example: "Full scan row cost 80% (3/12 digests) observed 24% of workload"
means 80% of row ops are full scans in the 24% of workload we can see.

feat(workload): add range and ref row cost tags (WTAG0211, WTAG0212)

Generalize EXPLAIN access type analysis into three tags:
- WTAG0210: Full scan (type=ALL) row cost
- WTAG0211: Range scan (type=range/index) row cost
- WTAG0212: Index lookup (type=ref/eq_ref/const) row cost

Each shows percentage of total row operations, digest count, and
effective workload coverage. Together they show the row-operation
breakdown of the observed workload.

feat(workload): add disk tmp table tag from PFS digests (WTAG0220)

WTAG0220 computes the percentage of query executions that create
on-disk temp tables, using PlanTmpDisk from PFS digest stats
weighted by exec_count. Only needs digest coverage (not EXPLAIN).

cluster.Status was ConstMonitorStandby (arbitration mode). This caused
scheduled jobs (backups, optimize, etc.) to run briefly on the passive
node until the first arbitration tick resolved the active/passive state.

fix: guard cron.Stop() against deadlock when Start() was never called

cron.Stop() sends on an unbuffered channel only drained by run(),
which is spawned by Start(). Calling Stop() on a never-started cron
blocks forever. This was exposed by the scheduler standby fix where
initScheduler() no longer calls Start() on passive nodes — any
subsequent Stop() (cluster shutdown, scheduler toggle, re-init) would
deadlock.

Add a running check mirroring the existing pattern in Schedule/Entries/
Remove. Add tests for Stop-before-Start and double-Stop scenarios.

fix(arbitration): prevent election race and heartbeat reset

Two bugs caused both repman instances to end up standby:

1. RequestArbitration() used a transaction but SELECT queries lacked
   FOR UPDATE, allowing concurrent elections to both read count==0
   and both lose. Add FOR UPDATE suffix for MySQL/InnoDB to serialize
   concurrent election attempts.

2. WriteHeartbeat() reset elected status 'E' back to 'U' every tick
   when count(distinct master)==1. That condition means both instances
   agree on the same master (split-brain resolved), not that the
   election should be undone. Invert the logic: only reset when
   count>1 (masters diverge, true split-brain).

fix: self-heal missing per-cluster plugins symlink in ReloadLogPlugins

The <cluster>/plugins → ../plugins symlink is created only at startup
and by the git pull sync. When the cluster working dir does not exist
yet at startup (or was wiped by a config restore), symlink creation
fails and is never retried: plugins stay unloaded, or stale registry
entries fork/exec dangling paths producing a WARN0203 storm on every
tick (seen on dev image with belair cluster).

ReloadLogPlugins now recreates the symlink to the shared plugin dir
when the per-cluster path is missing, so plugin loading no longer
depends on startup/pull-sync ordering.

fix: stable secret ciphertext across config saves to stop git churn

Every periodic SaveConfig re-encrypted all secrets from memory with a
fresh random IV (GetEncryptedString -> crypto Encrypt), so saved config
files always differed even when nothing changed. With git config sync
this meant a commit+push every save cycle (~2min), phantom 'config
changed' on every peer/standby pull, and cluster reloads flooding the
state machine (OPENED/RESOLV churn, cookies recreated).

Secret gains a Crypted ciphertext cache, seeded at load from the config
file's own hash_ value. New Config.GetStableEncryptedValue reuses the
existing ciphertext while it still decrypts to the current value and
only re-encrypts (fresh IV, unchanged crypto) when the secret really
changed. EncryptSecretValue mirrors DecryptSecretValue composite
handling (user:hash_..., comma lists). Both GetEncryptedValueFromMemory
implementations (server + cluster) now use it, including credential
composites; empty secrets are no longer encrypted into junk.

per run) and detail logging + file persistence happen only when the set
actually changes; WARN0084 is still re-asserted every run so the state
stays open.

Split brain: elections run every tick per cluster while the condition
persists (required to keep the winner's arbitrator row fresh — see
dbhelper.WriteHeartbeat REPLACE demoting status), which re-logged
'election won/lost, switching to ...' every tick on every cluster.
Outcome is now logged only on an actual active/standby transition and

feat: role-free standby config sync via isolated .config clone

Per-cluster arbitration elections are incompatible with role-based git
sync (active pushes / standby pulls): with a mixed active/standby
cluster set there is no server-level role to gate on, and the old
PullActiveConfig ran git checkout --force + pull --force directly on
the LIVE working dir — destructive for locally saved state of clusters
active on that node — gated by HasStandbyClusterWithGitSync (any single
standby cluster made a node pull, so after a failover both peers
pulled).

New model, change-driven and role-free:
- pull lands in an isolated clone WorkingDir/.config/ (same principle
  as .pull/), gitignored; the live tree is never force-reset
- files (<name>.toml, overwrite.toml) are copied into the live tree
  only for clusters where this node is standby with
  git-config-sync-standby, and only when bytes actually differ (real
  change detection before the reload)
- PullActiveConfig now runs on both peers whenever arbitration is on;
  HasStandbyClusterWithGitSync removed
- GitPush stays ungated: with stable secret ciphertext, nodes with no
  real edits push nothing

Also documents the per-cluster-election design decision (server-level
election considered and rejected: arbitration protects each cluster's
master, and masters legitimately sit on different sides of a
partition) in HEARTBEAT_AND_ARBITRATION.md.

fix: main loop must never block on network I/O — detach periodic tasks

The %60 block launched git sync (PullActiveConfig + GitPush wait=true),
cloud18 pull-repo sync and peer health polls as goroutines and then
wg.Wait()ed on them inside the main loop. go-git has no timeout: one
hung pull froze the entire loop — observed 2h frozen on dbaas-fr-2-dr
(last log 10:30:38, empty state machine, no heartbeat states, Monitor
0/0) while HTTP kept serving, so supervision died silently.

Tasks now run detached, each guarded by an atomic busy flag: if a round
is still running at the next cycle it is skipped and GWARN013@<task>
opens (git config sync / cloud18 pull-repo sync / peer health poll), so
a hang degrades into a visible Monitor warning instead of killing every
state producer.

fix: bound all go-git network calls, never wait on manager queue in loop

Second freeze found after the detach fix: the git-sync goroutine takes
the ConfigManager gitMutex (WithGitLock) and hangs in a go-git call
(go-git has no network timeout); next %60 cycle the loop's
SaveConfig(wait=true) queues behind the wedged worker and freezes every
state producer BEFORE the GWARN013 guard can fire. Observed on
dbaas-fr-2 five minutes after a fresh boot (last log 10:41:59), empty
state machine, no OPENED/RESOLV lines.

- main loop periodic SaveConfig no longer waits on the manager queue
- CloneConfigFromGit and PushConfigToGit use PlainCloneContext /
  PullContext / PushContext with a 120s gitNetworkTimeout, so a hung
  remote turns into a logged error surfaced by the GWARN002/003 git
  health states instead of a permanent mutex hold

feat: monitor loop ticker exposed and watched by the GUI

A frozen main loop cannot report itself through states — only an
external observer can catch it. The loop now publishes its tick
counter (loopTick in /api/monitor) and the navbar shows a live
'Tick N' pill (global view) that turns into a red blinking
'Monitor Stalled' when the tick stops advancing for ~5 monitoring

fix: RepMan init race left global state machine nil — no state ever published

Three files' init() guarded RepMan creation with bare
'if RepMan == nil { RepMan = new(ReplicationManager) }'. Go runs file
inits in file-name order, so server_decrypt.go's minimal init won and
server_monitor.go's full block was skipped: MessageChan stayed nil
(send would block forever) and InitAlertStateMachine never ran. Every
repman.SetState was a silent no-op — GWARN/GERR/GINF states never
existed in monitor mode: empty /api/global/alerts, zero OPENED/RESOLV
log lines, Monitor button permanently 0/0, regardless of split brain,
registration or supervision producers running.

Single ensureRepMan() constructor now builds the singleton with all
runtime dependencies; all three inits call it.

fix: preserve slow-cadence global states across lifecycle ticks

The lifecycle clears the global state machine every tick but the

fix: raise heartbeat supervision stall threshold to stop GWARN001 flapping

outage), so GWARN001 flapped STALLED/RESUME on every cluster tick
(40 open/close in 4.5min observed on fr-2). A truly stalled cluster
loop stays stalled for minutes: default is now 30 ticks (~60s),
critical at 3x (~3min); still tunable via

doc: config event log design — peer-symmetric config change replication

Approved design for event-changed.<RRBid>.log: per-instance append-only
log of locally-born config mutations in the shared config git repo,
per-peer cursors persisted with the save and advanced on the SaveConfig
cycle (apply the diff between two saves). Echo suppression, hash_
ciphertext for secrets, timestamp LWW conflicts, rotation with
full-pull fallback, log-everything / apply-allowlist scoping.
Solves mutations stranded on the standby peer (belair external user
case). Doc only — no code.

doc: config event log — drop apply-allowlist, peers re-apply every event

Every logged event is a dynamic cluster-scope setting peers must
converge on (server-scope flags never enter the log); LWW resolves
concurrent writes. Doc only.

doc: config event log — server-scope settings also logged and re-applied

Runtime changes to immutable scope:server settings are lost on restart
anyway, so replaying them on a peer carries no extra risk and peers
converging on the same runtime value is the desired behaviour. Doc only.

doc: config event log — save-diff authoring with provenance subtraction

Events derived from the SaveConfig cycle, not setter hooks (rejected:
call-site churn, future setters could forget to log): replay peer
events first recording provenance, key-diff the new toml against the
previous save, subtract keys whose value came from a replay, append
the rest as own events. Cursors + provenance persist with the save.
Ping-pong impossible by construction: applied events are subtracted
from the diff, cursors are forward-only, per-key LWW with author-id
tie-break gives all peers the same winner. Trade-offs recorded
(save-coarse timestamps, no transient audit, thin attribution). Doc
only.

feat: config event log — peer-symmetric config change replication

Implements doc/implementation/config/CONFIG_EVENT_LOG.md.

Authoring (save-diff, no setter hooks): SaveConfigFile,
SaveImmutableConfig and Overwrite() now build content in memory, write
crash-safe (<file>.new + rename — a kill mid-save can no longer leave
a truncated toml) and key-diff against the previous save. Locally-born
changes append to event-changed.<RRBid>.log (RRBid =
arbitration-external-unique-id); values just replayed from a peer are
subtracted via the provenance table, making ping-pong structurally
impossible. Secrets travel as hash_ ciphertext only. First save is a
baseline and emits nothing. Identical content no longer rewrites the
file (real change detection replaces the md5-at-wrong-offset check).

Transport: config.FetchRemoteRootFiles — bounded fetch + blob read
from the remote-tracking ref; the working tree is never merged into.

Replay (server_eventlog.go): fetch peer logs on the detached git-sync
cycle before the push, apply events past per-log cursors in (ts,
author) order under per-key LWW with author-id tie-break, seed peer
ciphertext into the Secret cache so both peers' saved configs converge
byte-identical, persist cursors+provenance in event-log-state.json
(gitignored, atomic). Unknown-setter keys apply through the same
viper/mapstructure path the config loader uses. A rotated (shrunk)
peer log replays from the start — LWW skips stale events.

Removed: the .config/ isolated clone and ReloadStandbyConfigsFromDisk
(one-directional active→standby sync stranded standby-born mutations,
e.g. marketplace signups); leftovers deleted at push time.

Unit tests: diff+echo subtraction, crash-safe artifact semantics,
provenance import rules.

fix: event log transport + phantom event sources

Three issues surfaced by the first live event log run:

- PushConfigToGit never staged event-changed.<id>.log (explicit
  whitelist of <cluster>/*.toml + agents.json + default.toml), so
  events were authored but never committed or pushed — peers fetched a
  remote with no logs. The event log now travels with the config push.
- SaveUserRoles built the role list from map iteration: random order
  made the ACL string flap ('sysops dbops' <-> 'dbops sysops') and emit
  phantom acl-allow-external events on every save. Roles are sorted.
- SetAgentsCpuCoreMem removed: it min()'d agent capacity into
  ImmuableFlagMap — write-only (no reader anywhere, incl. dbaas-portal),
  absent at boot (empty agent list -> unset event) and 0 when agents
  had not reported capacity (set '0' event). Per-agent capacity already
  reaches the BO through agents.json, which the push stages; free-
  capacity publication, if wanted, will be a proper computed field
  there.

fix: event log compares secrets by decrypted value, not ciphertext

Encryption uses a random IV: the same secret re-encrypted (e.g. after
a restart when the ciphertext cache did not seed) produces different
bytes — not a config change, must not emit an event. The save diff now
decrypts both sides for secret keys and skips equal plaintexts, making
the event log immune to ciphertext instability regardless of cause.

Adds boot-seed reproduction tests (config_secret_seed_test.go): the
DecryptSecretsFromConfig -> GetStableEncryptedValue cycle is proven
stable across simulated restarts when the raw hash_ value is present
in the flag maps — so the every-boot re-encryption observed live means
the maps lack the raw values at seed time (boot wiring, under
investigation); the git-churn side of that remains to fix.

fix: instance-local secrets never replicate; config saves gated on init

- Instance-local keys (git-acces-token, vault-role-id/secret-id,
  api-oauth-client-id/secret) are excluded from the config event log:
  never authored, never applied. Each instance derives its own GitLab
  PAT from its own OAuth session (rotated at boot and daily) — a peer
  replaying it would clobber the local credential, and both peers
  rotating the same named PAT would invalidate each other.
- Cluster.Save() refuses to run until InitFromConf completes
  (initConfigDone flag): config saves go through an async queue, and a
  save executing mid-init captured a half-loaded config (missing
  external users, restic paths, ACLs) — emitting transient unset/set
  event pairs (seen on mixr-dev, two saves 100ms apart) that then
  replayed on peers.
doc: config event log — instance-local keys and authoring hygiene

fix: dynamically-created clusters load their saved config at boot

GetClusterConfig gated the saved-<cluster> section load on the STATIC
cluster section existing (cf2 != nil). Clusters created dynamically
(API, marketplace) have no static section — they exist only through
saved-<name>.toml — so every restart discarded their entire persisted
config: api-credentials-external regenerated (AddCloud18GitUser saw no
sysops user and rolled a fresh random password each boot — the
per-boot mixr-dev events), backup-restic-local-repository and ACLs
rebuilt from defaults. Discovery already knew these clusters (it
strips the saved- prefix); only the loader refused their section.
The block only uses cf3 (own nil-check) and the immutable map, so
dropping the cf2 condition is safe for static clusters.

fix: per-instance GitLab PAT name — peers no longer invalidate each other

Both peers authenticate as the same GitLab account and built the same
PAT name (domain-subdomain-zone), and GetGitLabTokenOAuth rotates the
token by name: every boot (and daily ticker) of either instance minted
a new token under the shared name, invalidating the other instance's
copy — its git fetch/push then failed 401 until its own next restart.
Pre-existing bug; the event log's every-cycle fetch made it visible in
minutes (DR could not fetch peer events after main's restarts).

Token name now carries the instance unique id
(GetInstancePATName: <domain>-<subdomain>-<zone>-<RRBid>) in all three
sites (InitGitConfig, daily rotation ticker, SSO login flow). Each
instance owns and rotates its own PAT; the shared-name token falls out
of use.

fix: stage event log in the push implementation actually used

There are two push implementations: repman.PushConfigToGit (legacy,
stages event logs since 4f213c12b, also writes the gitignore lines)
and config.PushConfigToGit used by the ConfigManager queue — the one
every periodic push goes through, staging only <cluster>/*.toml,
agents.json and queryrules.json. The event log staging went into the
wrong one, so event-changed.<id>.log was authored, committed nowhere,
and never reached the remote (diagnosed live: pushes green, file
absent from HEAD, gitignore missing the legacy path's lines proving
that path never runs). Both implementations now stage the logs.

fix: stage event log in the ConfigManager push worker — the real live path

Third push implementation found the hard way: the ConfigManager's own
commit worker (config/manager/manager.go, GitAddTask queue) is what
every periodic push actually runs — proven live by its distinct error
format in the logs and by the instance .gitignore lacking every line
the legacy paths write. The two previous staging fixes (repman and
config package PushConfigToGit) patched dormant code. The worker now
queues event-changed.<id>.log like default.toml.

Push 'object not found' failures observed alongside are the shallow
clone racing the peer's pushes; the worker's existing
classifyRecoverablePushError -> RefreshGitMetadata -> retry already
covers that.

fix: rebase-on-remote before commit in the live push worker

Fetch (bounded 120s) and mixed-reset the local branch onto the
remote-tracking head before staging: working files are kept (local
content wins), only the branch pointer and index move, so every push
is a fast-forward built from objects we hold. Kills the shallow
two-writer race for good: previously the worker committed on top of a
stale graft, the push died with 'object not found' once the peer had
advanced the remote, and the refresh-restage retry (~2min at ~1s per
go-git Add across ~80 files) reliably lost the next race too —
trapping local commits, including the config event log, forever.

fix: checksum repair DELETE fails on MariaDB < 11.6 (alias syntax)

RepairTableChecksum emitted 'DELETE FROM db.tbl A WHERE <A.-qualified
chunk condition>' — single-table DELETE with a table alias, which
MariaDB only accepts since 11.6.1 (MDEV-33988) and refused to backport
to any LTS line (MDEV-37227 Won't Fix). Checksum repair was therefore
broken with error 1064 on 10.5/10.6/10.11/11.4. The alias cannot be
dropped (the stored chunkRangeCondition references A.), so use the
multi-table form 'DELETE A FROM db.tbl A WHERE ...' which every MySQL
and MariaDB version accepts.

fix(arbitration): restore peace-time election semantics and true heartbeat upsert

Two regressions from late June made peer pairs flap active/passive
(ERR00022 open/resolve every ~2min with 'Arbitrator says: winner'):

1. The election reset was inverted on 2026-06-30 from the original
   2017 semantics. Restored: count(distinct master)==1 — every fresh
   heartbeat reports the identical master, no split brain — clears the
   election, because in peace time the arbitrator must not impose an
   authority: who is active is decided by the peer protocol (an
   instance seeing its peer active with the same master sets itself
   passive, an authority already exists). The Elected flag only takes
   over when the peers disagree on the master (two different masters
   after a partition, or one side seeing none), and is then preserved
   so the first winner holds for the whole partition. The inversion
   made the arbitrator keep a persistent winner in peace time,
   fighting the peer protocol.

2. WriteHeartbeat used REPLACE / INSERT OR REPLACE, which deletes and
   reinserts the row — status falls back to its default 'U', so the
   winner wiped its own Elected flag on its own next heartbeat.
   Restored the original 2016 MySQL semantics (ON DUPLICATE KEY
   UPDATE; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on SQLite): the heartbeat reports
   uuid/master/date/hosts/failed and never touches status.

Also updates TestRequestArbitration_Winner_MySQL_SQL to the SQL shape
introduced by the 2026-06-30 stale-row filter (failing since then).

Arbitrator-side only: rebuild (make arb) and redeploy the arbitrator
service; no repman client changes.

feat(arbitrator): /version endpoint

Reports the running build ({version, fullVersion} JSON). Election

fix(client): consult the arbitrator only when the master has failed

The /arbitrator endpoint runs an election. The client probed it in
peace time — every tick on active clusters through the false-positive
check chain, plus a periodic ERR00022 status probe — so the arbitrator
minted a transient Elected row on every check; the peer probing
seconds later read it, answered looser, and every cluster flapped
active/passive (ERR00022 blockers) at probe frequency.

The check chain now evaluates ActiveArbitration lazily: pass without
probing while the master is healthy, ask the arbitrator only when
isMasterFailed() and a failover is actually being evaluated — the one
moment the answer is decisive. The peace-time status probe block is
removed; a lingering ERR00022 resolves naturally once no longer
re-asserted, and the split-brain election path (cluster_split) is
unchanged.

Client-side fix on purpose: upgraded repman instances must behave on
OLD arbitrators, which keep the probe-elects behavior forever.

fix(arbitrator): status probes no longer run elections — read-mostly /arbitrator

Companion to 859989b5e (client stops idle probing): protects fleets of
OLD repman clients, which probe /arbitrator in peace time forever.
Decision order in handlerArbitrator:
1. A fresh Elected row exists: answer winner/looser by uid, no write.
2. No Elected row and no fresh heartbeat disagrees with the caller's
   master: peace — every asker is a winner (the arbitrator imposes no
   authority; the peer protocol decides who is active), no write.
3. Masters diverge: real split brain — run the election; the flag
   sticks for the whole partition (heartbeats no longer wipe it) and
   dissolves when agreement returns.

New read-only helpers GetFreshElected and IsMasterAgreed in dbhelper.
Takes effect on arbitrator redeploy; no client changes required.

feat: chaos isolation — per-cluster split-brain simulation + regtest

Simulates, for one cluster on this instance only, the scenario
arbitration protects against: the monitor loses the data plane (every
database connection fails at GetNewDBConn, driving servers to failed
exactly like a real cut) and peer visibility (IsSplitBrain forced in
ArbitratorHandler, engaging the existing election machinery) while the
arbitrator stays reachable.

- Runtime state only, NEVER a config key: config would replicate to
  the peer through the config event log and isolate both sides.
- API: /api/clusters/{name}/actions/chaos-isolate-start
  (?duration=seconds, 120s default, 15min max) and chaos-isolate-stop;
  requires the cluster-test grant. Always auto-restores; WARN0181
  warns every tick while armed with the remaining seconds.

Regtest testChaosIsolationArbitration, three phases (failover mode
forced auto and restored — phases 1-2 alone would pass in manual mode
too and prove nothing):
1. Armed: the isolated side must lose the election, go standby, and
   the failover counter must NOT move.
2. Lifted: split brain resolves, same master, still no failover.
3. The hard part: a REAL master stop under active arbitration must
   still fail over automatically (protection must never block the
   legitimate authority) and the old master must rejoin as a slave.
Skips as passed when arbitration is not configured.

and arbitrator, 1 of 3), so the master it sees is not authoritative —
the majority (peer + arbitrator) holds the truth. A minority node must

check failed (IsSplitBrain); cluster: cannot join the arbitrator
(arbitrator link cut) — and asserts status and failover counter never

('goes standby') was wrong: a minority node holds its status, it does

fix(chaos): arbitrator cut also stops the arbitrator report

A minority node (arbitrator link cut) must stop refreshing its
arbitrator heartbeat row, not just skip the election — otherwise its
row stays fresh and the majority never wins. SetArbitratorReport now
bails on the arbitrator cut too, so the minority's row goes stale
(~10s) and the majority wins the next per-tick election, exactly as a
real isolated node behaves (it can reach neither the peer nor the
arbitrator, so it reports to neither).

test: rename to testSetMinority with two virtual scenarios

testSetMinority puts a repman into the minority condition (peer +

- setMinorityLostMaster: master on the majority side (unreachable) —
  enters CheckFailed/isMasterFailed; guards against promoting a slave
  -> second failover.

Same assertion (status held, no failover), two distinct code paths.

~*6s, capped at 60s, and honors request cancellation) so the polling
peer experiences a genuine network timeout with its real delay.

cut armed on both peers, each side's outbound request times out on its
own against the other's sleeping handler — exercising the real
network-timeout code path (client.Do error -> split brain) instead of a
synthetic instant answer. Arm the cut on both peers for a bidirectional
partition.

Restore the outbound timeout in HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain: an isolated
node cannot reach its peer either, so its own request must hang and
time out too — sleeping the full timeout reproduces the real
network-timeout delay from this side. Combined with the sleeping
/api/heartbeat (peer's inbound times out), arming the peer cut on the
single isolated node now reproduces what BOTH sides see in a real
partition, without arming both or cross-instance coordination.

fix(splitbrain): force server split-brain when heartbeat failure simulated

The inbound-only heartbeat cut made the split brain invisible on the node
where it was armed: SimulateHeartbeatFailure only darkens this node's inbound
/api/heartbeat, so its own outbound heartbeat still succeeded and
HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain returned false — repman.SplitBrain never flipped and
nothing propagated to the clusters. Only the peer could detect it, and only if
a remote call landed.

Now, when IsHeartbeatFailureSimulated() is armed, Heartbeat() forces
repman.SplitBrain = true directly (a real cable cut means THIS node cannot
reach its peer). The existing block then fires GWARN006 and pushes IsSplitBrain
down to every cluster — the first observable step — with no peer dependency.
On expiry/restore the next tick recomputes via the real peer heartbeat and
clears it. This also lets the minority tests detect the split locally.

feat(arbitration): log the per-tick arbitrator verdict at debug

The winner/looser reply from the arbitrator was only logged on a status
transition, so while a node holds a stable active state the per-tick verdict
was invisible — making it impossible to see from the node's own log whether the
arbitrator's *answer* flaps or only its /stats display does.

Add a DEBUG line on the receive side of both arbitrator calls:
- arbitratorElection (split-brain election): "reply arbitration=%s winner-master=%s (my status=%s)"
- isActiveArbitration (peace-time probe):    "reply arbitration=%s (my status=%s)"

cluster (e.g. belair) without touching others.

fix(arbitration): bound isActiveArbitration HTTP call with a timeout

isActiveArbitration used a bare http.Client{} with no deadline, so a cut
arbitrator link (real split brain or the split-brain simulator's blackhole)
would hang the monitor tick — and shutdown — indefinitely instead of failing
fast. Bound it with ArbitrationReadTimout (default 800ms), matching the intent
already present in SetArbitratorReport (context deadline) and arbitratorElection
(client Timeout). This is also required for split-brain detection to work: the
probe must FAIL on a severed link, not block.

fix(arbitration): minority fail-safe — set master read-only + yield to standby

When a node is in split brain but cannot reach the arbitrator to confirm
authority, it is (or must assume it is) the minority. Previously arbitratorElection
just returned on arbitrator loss, so a node that was Active with a writable master
FROZE Active and kept accepting writes — risking dual-active and, worse, writes on
the minority master that diverge and block its rejoin once the partition heals.

The 2020 fail-safe (SetReadWrite blocked while IsFailedArbitrator, still present)
only refuses to *enable* writes; it does not demote an already-writable master.

Add arbitratorMinorityFailSafe(), called from both arbitrator-unreachable paths
(simulated cut and real HTTP error):
  1. force the master READ-ONLY so it rejoins the majority's newly-elected master
     as a slave (no divergence), and
  2. yield status to standby so this repman stops driving the cluster.
Idempotent per tick. This is the behavior expected by design; git history confirms
the original fail-safe was read-only-based, never a status yield that was removed.

test(splitbrain): minority must fail-safe (yield to standby), not freeze

minorityDoesNothing asserted the minority's status stays UNCHANGED — but the
correct, data-safe behavior is that the minority yields: drops to standby and
sets its master read-only so it can rejoin the majority. The old assertion would
flag the correct fix as a "FLIPPED" failure.

Rewrite the assertion: for the whole window require no failover (FailoverCtr
unchanged), and require the node to reach standby (yield). Log the master's
read-only state. "does nothing" was really "does nothing destructive" — it must
still fail safe.

fix(splitbrain-sim): master/db cut must fail the Ping health check, not just new conns

simulate-master-failure / simulate-database-failure only hooked GetNewDBConn, but
that is NOT the path that detects a down server: ServerMonitor.Ping() only calls
GetNewDBConn when CheckType == "tcp", and monitoring otherwise reuses the existing
pooled connection. So the simulated master kept pinging fine, was never marked
failed, and the majority never detected a master loss or promoted — "still see the
master as master."

Inject the simulated failure directly in Ping(), after the CheckType switch, so the
server is driven down through the real detection path (FailCount -> stateFailed ->
failover) regardless of CheckType or connection reuse. Covers both the whole-cluster
db cut and the master-only cut.

fix(splitbrain-sim): also fail Refresh() ping so a cut master stays down

Hooking Ping() alone wasn't enough: the health is delegated to the Go driver's
pooled connection, and Refresh() (server.Conn.Ping()) auto-reconnects and keeps
succeeding, flapping the master Suspect->Master so it never reaches MaxFail and
never triggers failover. Gate Refresh()'s ping with the same simulation check so
the cut server stays consistently down and failover fires.

Simulation-only (fires solely when IsMasterFailureSimulated / IsDatabaseFailureSimulated
is armed) — no effect on normal operation. NOTE for after release: the deeper
question is why Refresh() runs at all after Ping() has already failed for a server
in the same tick — that flap could mask real half-broken-master failures too.

fix(splitbrain-sim): simulated master death must defeat false-positive guards

A simulated master failure only cuts repman's view — db->db replication stays
live — so the false-positive guards (isOneSlaveHeartbeatIncreasing sees the slave
still replicating; isExternalOk may still reach the DB) concluded "master not
really dead" and vetoed failover on every tick. FailCount climbed past MaxFail
(observed 21/5) but MasterFailover never fired.

Short-circuit both guards to the "dead" answer when IsMasterFailureSimulated /
IsDatabaseFailureSimulated is armed, so a simulated death is treated as real and
failover triggers at MaxFail (5/5) as expected. Simulation-only; no effect on
real operation.

fix(splitbrain-sim): stop the topology-role heal from resetting a simulated-dead master

The real reason a simulated master death never triggered failover: the ping/refresh
error was fine, but srv.go's active-passive state reconciliation re-marks the master
stateMaster purely from its topology role (PrevState==Suspect + "it's the master"),
ignoring the connection. That heal reset FailCount every tick, so it flapped
Suspect<->Master and never held Failed long enough for CheckFailed to promote.

Skip that re-heal while IsMasterFailureSimulated is armed for this server, so the
death sticks -> FailCount reaches MaxFail -> failover fires. Sim-gated only.

NOTE after release: this same heal ignores the connection for REAL deaths too — worth
verifying against the failover regtest whether it can mask a real active-passive
master failure.

fix(splitbrain-sim): guard the real reheal path (SetMaster) for master-slave

a0f8da31a guarded the ActivePassive branch (srv.go:789), but belair is master-slave,
so that branch never runs — the reheal actually goes through SetMaster() (srv_set.go),
which topology discovery calls every tick to re-designate db1 as master, re-marking it
stateMaster and resetting FailCount -> the flap, no failover.

Revert the wrong-branch guard and instead guard SetMaster(): while a server's failure is
simulated, don't re-mark it stateMaster, so the death sticks -> FailCount holds at MaxFail
-> failover fires. Sim-gated only.

feat(arbitration): authority lease + contest window — fix the coordination root cause

The dual-active relapses observed live today (a standby self-promoting off
a single lost peer poll, twice) are a COORDINATION flaw, not a client bug:
the arbitrator had no memory of who holds authority. Elected rows went
stale 10s after a split ended, so the next asker — whoever, whenever — won
a fresh election against nobody. Blips merely walked through that open
door. Per Stephane: fix the coordination, do not hide the blip.

The Elected row becomes a persistent LEASE, enforced by the arbitrator:

- Lease maintenance (handlerHeartbeat): an instance reporting status
  Active CLAIMS its lease; reporting Standby RELEASES it. Fed by new
  event-driven transition reports from repman (server.go): every
  server-level transition (Active<->Standby, split enter/leave, boot)
  posts one report per arbitrated cluster — steady peacetime stays
  completely silent. Old clients omit status: nothing changes for them.
- decideArbitration (handlerArbitrator): I hold the lease -> winner;
  another holds it FRESH -> looser (base-cut: incumbent keeps driving);
  another holds it STALE -> the challenger must persist through a 10s
  CONTEST WINDOW before the election runs and the lease transfers
  (in-memory contest map, single-instance arbitrator, no protocol or
  schema change). A blip heals long before the window closes; split brain
  stays fully visible (WARN0079) but can no longer steal authority.

feat(arbitration): true minority-master freeze via held FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK (opt-in)

FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK is the only server-side lock that blocks even
SUPER — so it is the only way to truly stop a minority/old master from
diverging during a split.

- ServerMonitor.FreezeWithReadLock: opens a DEDICATED single-session conn
  (SetMaxOpenConns(1)) and holds FTWRL on it. The lock lives exactly as
  long as that conn stays open, so a repman crash releases it — a client
  master can never be left frozen forever. UnfreezeReadLock closes it;
  IsFrozen reports state. Idempotent.
- Wired into arbitratorMinorityFailSafe (gated on new opt-in flag
  arbitration-minority-freeze, default false), released when the split
  resolves (ArbitratorHandler) and defensively at rejoin start (recovery
  must write). Pairs with the authority gate: the gate stops repman's own
  writes, the freeze blocks everyone else's.

fix(inject): dml marker table created once via the proxy — no state machine

The dml traffic marker broke replication because I created the marker table
OUT-OF-BAND (directly and empty on each node): the master's in-place REPLACE
(a ROW update of id=1) then had no matching before-image on the slaves ->
1032 HA_ERR_KEY_NOT_FOUND.

The fix is simply to create the table the SAME way the marker is written —
via the PROXY, once, when traffic starts. That CREATE lands on the master,
is binlogged, and flows to every slave in the SAME binlog stream BEFORE any
REPLACE that follows it. Binlog ordering guarantees a slave applies the
CREATE before the REPLACE (no 1032), and a reseeded node gets the table in
its snapshot. So there is NOTHING to check — no CanInjectTraffic state, no
per-node presence probe, no DictTables/SHOW CREATE lookup, no new-node
tracking. One idempotent create-once guard (injectTrafficTableReady).

- Default is ddl (self-contained view, battle-tested); dml experimental.
- injectTrafficMarker creates DB+table+seed+view via the proxy db on first
  call, then REPLACEs — all on the same connection.
- Removed refreshInjectTrafficState, CanInjectTraffic, WARN0186.

topology: re-designate stale master after a minority sat out split-brain

Regression from the 2026-07-08 minority fail-safe (ca0da65a5/3630064574): a node
that sat out a split-brain as the minority froze its last-known master pointer.
When it goes Active/calm again it lands in the extra-master branch (Case A) whose
reconcile has been commented out since 2023, so it forever holds cluster.master =
the old master even though that node is now a slave of the real (majority-elected)
master. Symptom: node shows db1=Master while db1 is actually a wedged slave of db2,
ERR00063 open every tick, proxies never follow.

Fix: in the master-slave extra-master case, if our own cluster.master pointer is
itself a slave now (IsSlave), it is stale — re-designate to the real master
(the non-slave others follow) rather than treating the live master as an extra to
demote (which would enslave it). Guarded to TopoMasterSlave and IsActive only, so
the minority never re-designates from an untrusted view and multi-master is
untouched. Repair of the stale old master (standalone->slave) is a separate step.

leave the caller in arbitratorMinorityFailSafe COMMENTED OUT: it must be

acl: fix missing rejoin ACL rule (was 403 for everyone)

The /actions/rejoin/{server}/{method} endpoint had no entry in clusterACLRules,
so matchACLRules denied it for every user (403 No valid ACL) and the operator
rejoin buttons never reached RearmRejoin.

- add base rule: /actions/rejoin requires cluster-failover
- add cluster-rejoin-unsafe grant; ignore-delta-force (the only destructive
  method, discards the divergent tail) additionally requires it, enforced
  per-method in the handler (a URL rule cannot express it safely because
  matchACLRules' hierarchical fallback would grant reset-master-reslave via the
  existing actions/reset-master rule)

rejoin: safe/unsafe verbs, cluster-scoped, + bootstrap-ftwrl & rejoin-script methods

Restructure the operator rejoin into two cluster-level verbs keyed by the method
(server dropped from the path — resolved from crash history, optional ?server=):
  POST /actions/rejoin/{method}         -> cluster-failover
  POST /actions/unsafe-rejoin/{method}  -> cluster-failover + cluster-rejoin-unsafe
The two verbs are non-overlapping ACL anchors; the handler also enforces the
method<->verb match so a safe-verb caller cannot run a destructive method.

New methods:
- bootstrap-repli-ftwrl (unsafe): BootstrapReplication(clean, ftwrl=true) takes a
  short FTWRL on the master before RESET MASTER, all on ONE pinned connection with a
  session wait_timeout so the lock self-releases if repman dies/hangs.
- rejoin-script (safe): runs the custom autorejoin-script (now returns an error).

GUI: classify methods (safety x duration) and group the delta-viewer buttons
(safe-fast / safe-full-reseed / unsafe-fast); header crash badge now blinks on a

rejoin: cluster-level, no server param — backend resolves target from crash history

A cluster-level action must not carry a db server name. Dropped the ?server= query
(and the GUI passing it): the backend resolves the diverged master from its own crash

target is now a crash URL by construction, so RearmRejoin always matches, instead of a

gui(delta viewer): themed buttons + preserve scroll on refresh

- Rejoin method buttons: raw Chakra Button (ad-hoc blue/red, not theme-aware) ->

rejoin: actually EXECUTE an operator-armed rejoin (was armed but never run)

RearmRejoin only copied the crash into the working set; nothing ran it. RejoinMaster
(which dispatches the chosen method) is called only from the Failed->up edge (srv.go)
and the extra-master topology path (cluster_topo.go), BOTH gated on Conf.Autorejoin.
So a manual rejoin of a healthy attached slave with auto-rejoin off — the whole point
of the operator action — armed the crash and then sat there: nothing happened.

Two fixes, keeping the armed-crash design intact:
- rejoinAlreadyAttempted: an armed working-set crash (method set, no result) overrides
  the one-shot, so a finished automatic attempt no longer blocks the manual retry.
- ProcessArmedRejoins: new per-tick pass (wired after CheckFailed) that runs any armed
  crash via RejoinMaster, INDEPENDENT of Conf.Autorejoin and the Failed->up edge. One-
  shot as always (finishRejoin records the result).

rejoin: WARN0188 blocker — disable reset-master-reslave when old master diverged (1236)

reset-master-reslave (RESET MASTER + reslave) does NOT clear gtid_slave_pos, so a slave
that EXECUTED extra transactions and got IO error 1236 (requested GTID not in master's
binlog) still asks for the missing GTID after the reset — it fails anyway. It only works
when the SQL thread was blocked by strict mode (diverged txns unapplied in the relay log).

- WARN0188: cluster-level rejoin blocker, raised in checkStoppedReplication when the IO
  thread stops with 1236 (keyed on the diverged server = the old master).
- RejoinMethodsStatus disables reset-master-reslave while WARN0188 is open, steering the
  operator to flashback or reseed.

rejoin: fix bootstrap-repli-ftwrl (menu bootstrap worked, method did not)

Root cause: rejoinWithMethod is built for single-server methods and ALWAYS runs
attachAsReadOnlySlave(master) after the method. bootstrap-repli-ftwrl calls
BootstrapReplication, which rebuilds the WHOLE topology and re-slaves this server
itself — the trailing single-server CHANGE MASTER then fought the setup the bootstrap
had just built. That is why the menu bootstrap (a clean single call) worked and the
rejoin method did not. Now the bootstrap case finishRejoin's and returns, skipping the
trailing attach — same shape as the menu action.

Also: only reset-master-reslave stays blocked by WARN0188 (it 1236s). bootstrap-ftwrl
works (its cleanup clears gtid_slave_pos) so it is NOT blocked; ignore-delta-force left
enabled pending confirmation.

rejoin: manual methods delegate to the auto-rejoin code, attach only on failure

The point of manual rejoin is to EXERCISE the same code auto-rejoin uses, so a client
can trust turning auto-rejoin on. Re-coding it was a double mistake: reinvention bugs +
it validates nothing about auto. Aligning rejoinWithMethod to the auto path:

- Remove the blanket trailing attachAsReadOnlySlave. It duplicated (and conflicted with)
  every self-attaching method — flashback does its own slave_pos CHANGE MASTER, my attach
  re-issued current_pos, and the naive attach dropped SSL/delay/channel/multi-source.
  Now attach runs ONLY on the failure branch, exactly like the auto path (its line 214).
- flashback/logical-dump/logical-backup/physical-backup: call the real auto functions,
  which self-attach with the full-config CHANGE MASTER. No second attach.
- reset-master-reslave: = the server menu, ResetMaster + StartSlave (resumes the existing
  replication, so multi-source / named channels / MASTER_DELAY are preserved).
- ignore-delta-force: RESET MASTER + SetReplicationGTIDSlavePosFromServer (full config) +
  StartSlave — its own proper re-attach (RESET MASTER alone does not re-slave).
- WARN0188 informational-gate: reset-master-reslave disabled when the old master diverged
  (IO 1236) — replication would point to an invalid position on the new master.

Auto-rejoin function bodies untouched; only RejoinScript (returns error, auto ignores) and
rejoinAlreadyAttempted (armed-crash override, no-op for auto) are shared-and-preserved.

acl: rejoin rules were in the WRONG table (403 for everyone), + reset-reslave unsafe

THE BUG: /actions/rejoin & /actions/unsafe-rejoin are CLUSTER-level URLs, so IsURLPassACL
routes them to clusterACLRules — but the rules were placed in databaseACLRules (only
reached for /servers/... URLs). So matchACLRules found no rule and denied: 403 for every
user regardless of grants (admin HAS cluster-failover + cluster-rejoin-unsafe, still 403).
Moved the two rules into clusterACLRules next to /actions/failover, dropped the gratuitous
trailing slash (nothing else in the table has one), unsafe verb keeps RequiredGrants AND
(like /actions/restart). Verify: POST /actions/rejoin/<x> should go 403 -> 400/404.

Also:
- reset-master-reslave reclassed UNSAFE (group + verb + cluster-rejoin-unsafe grant): it is
  the 'unsafe method' in WARN0188, and it re-slaves from a possibly-invalid position.
- bootstrap-repli-ftwrl: use the PROVEN FreezeWithReadLock (dedicated-session FTWRL) +
  dbhelper.ResetMaster instead of the hand-rolled freezeResetMasterFTWRL (removed).

fix(cluster): non-blocking ReleaseBackupSlot to prevent monitor-loop deadlock

Release was a blocking receive on the backup semaphore channel; a receive on
an empty channel blocks forever. Release is driven by WARN0073/WARN0175 state
resolution in StateProcessing, which is not guaranteed to be paired with a held
slot, so an unpaired release froze the whole Cluster.Run monitor loop for hours
(no CheckFailed, no failover, frozen workLoad). Make release a select/default
no-op when no slot is held.

fix(regtest): track and auto-restore split-brain simulator io_thread stop

op 5/6 issued a real STOP SLAVE IO_THREAD but left it untracked and un-restored,
stranding slaves in SlaveErr with no marker. Route it through SimulateSlaveIOThreadStop:
keep the real stop, but record it so it auto-restarts (START SLAVE) on timer expiry
and cleanup, and surface it as simulation-induced via VSPLIT0007.

fix(rejoin): pin failed-over master to Failed at crash materialization

A minority-side failover left the old master stranded StandAlone with no auto-rejoin.
Root cause (proven from logs): the only auto-rejoin trigger is a Failed->up edge, but
the winning repman yields active (calm-yield) before that edge lands, and the new
active never witnessed the failure (its DB link to the master survived), so neither
auto path fires — DR log showed 'Rejoin ... not triggered (active=false)'.

Fix: when the active node fetches/materializes the peer's crash for the old master
(fetchMasterFromPeer — runs only on the active node), set that server to Failed. The
node that drives the rejoin is then guaranteed to hold the Failed->up edge; the server
is reachable so it recovers to StandAlone next tick with PrevState=Failed and the
existing RejoinMaster fires. Guarded !IsMaster so the elected new master is never demoted.

fix(rejoin): keep operator-armed crash out of the DBs-up purge

The manual rejoin API returned {"rejoin":"armed"} (ACL OK, crash queued with the
chosen method) but never executed: hasUnresolvedCrash only protected a crash whose
server was SlaveErr/Failed, so for a StandAlone old master the DBs-up purge
(cluster_topo.go) deleted the armed crash before ProcessArmedRejoins could run it.
Treat an armed crash (RejoinMethod set, RejoinResult empty) as unresolved so it
survives the purge and the queued rejoin actually runs.
