fix(config-sync): dirty-gated config push, decoupled from the agents feed

The periodic git push gated config sync on GitMonitoringTicker, the same timer
that throttles the agents.json runtime feed — so slowing agents to hourly (to
stop reclone churn) also slowed DR/peer config sync to hourly.

Split into two decoupled triggers on one push path (server.go serve loop):
- configDirty: any cluster's IsNeedGitPush (set only by a real config diff in
  cluster.Save, which in the same pass appended the peer event-changed.<id>.log)
  -> push within ~60s so DR and peers converge promptly.
- safetyDue (GitMonitoringTicker): periodic full push + safety net, and the
  cadence on which the throttled agents.json is staged for the BO.

Flags cleared on dispatch; a failed push is recovered by the safety timer.
agents.json stays in git on its throttle (the BO's only channel) but no longer
gates config latency. Design: doc/implementation/config/CONFIG_SYNC.md.

docs(config-sync): mark the dead duplicate git-push paths

Three PushConfigToGit implementations exist; only ConfigManager's is live.
Comment config.Config.PushConfigToGit and repman.PushAllConfigsToGit/
PushConfigToGit as dead (no callers) so nobody wires back a path that stages
agents.json unthrottled outside the ConfigManager queue.

refactor(config-sync): remove the per-cluster save queue, single server-level gate

Config save was driven by a per-cluster queue (ClusterManager/processClusterQueue
+ per-cluster worker goroutines + cond vars) and, redundantly, by each cluster's
monitor loop. In a single-writer model that machinery is unnecessary.

- cluster.Save() is now the event (set IsNeedConfigSave, no I/O); the heavy
  persist moves to cluster.SaveCallBack(). Same split for repman: Save() = event,
  SaveCallBack() = SaveGlobalConfigs().
- SaveConfig is a queue-less dispatcher: wait=false -> event, wait=true -> sync
  SaveCallBack. Deleted ClusterManager, ConfigSaveTask, processClusterQueue,
  getOrCreateClusterManager, getClusterManager, CountTasksForCluster, clusterData,
  and the 6 obsolete queue tests.
- Single config-sync gate in the serve loop (active-only, gitSyncBusy-guarded):
  SAVE phase (every cluster's SaveCallBack + global) then dirty-gated PUSH, in
  order on one goroutine — no gitMutex/configWg needed for save/push ordering.
- Active/standby authority for config-sync moved to the server level: gate on
  repman.Status (the arbitration-driven anchor) instead of per-cluster
  cl.IsActive(). During split-brain cluster.Status flaps per cluster but
  repman.Status is stable, so the active repman keeps persisting all clusters'
  config through the incident.
- Removed the redundant cluster-loop periodic save (cluster.go).

Git push/pull worker and the BO->cluster .pull channel are untouched. The
ConfigManager->GitManager rename + git-queue-to-direct-call are a follow-up.
Builds clean; manager tests pass.

docs(config-sync): rewrite CONFIG_SYNC.md as-built

fix(rejoin): stop ALL slaves before flashback reseed replay (ERROR 1198)

The flashback reseed-from-backup path (JobFlashbackLogicalBackup) called
server.StopSlave(), which stops only the cluster.Conf.MasterConn channel —
empty by default, so plain STOP SLAVE on the unnamed default connection. A
server replicating on a NAMED connection (e.g. 'curepipe') kept running, so the
dump's embedded position statement failed with ERROR 1198 'you have a running
slave ... run STOP SLAVE <name> first'. Use StopAllSlaves(), which iterates
server.Replications and stops each by its real ConnectionName.

Latent because this rejoin-from-backup path was newly reached via the restore
selector; the widely-used client paths (direct master dump, manual
JobReseedMysqldump onto a fresh server) don't have a running named slave, so
they are left untouched.

feat(rejoin): catalog-based rejoin availability + multi-source-safe reseed

So a rejoin works after a failover when the freshly-promoted master has no
backup yet — the backup is on the old master (or restic/S3), not the new master.

Catalog-based rejoin availability (was master-cookie-scoped):
- Per-method selectors autorejoin-backup-selector-{logical,physical}
  (Origin/Repo:"any" — dig any node/repo/location); getAutorejoinBackupSelector(method).
- New catalog states IsValidRejoinBackup{Logical,Physical} + WARN0190/0191
  (ErrFrom "JOIN"), recomputed every 30 heartbeats from buildBackupCatalog().
- RejoinMethodsStatus() gates the crash-recovery logical/physical-backup buttons
  on those catalog states instead of master.HasBackupLogicalCookie(), so they
  enable when the OLD master holds a backup. WARN0111/0112 stay master-scoped for
  the external orchestrator contract (relabeled '... for current master').
- GUI: LostEventsModal 'Logical dump' -> 'Direct master dump'.

Multi-source-safe reseed:
- StopAllSlaves() before RESET MASTER (StopSlave only stopped the default
  MasterConn channel, so a named connection e.g. 'curepipe' survived and RESET
  MASTER failed with ERROR 1198) + symmetric StartSlaveChannel restart, on the
  direct-dump and flashback paths. Document the RESET MASTER Debian-bootstrap reason.

Restic/remote fetch into the rejoin ACTION remains unwired (catalog lists remote
backups, action is local-only) — tracked separately.

perf(config-sync): fan out the per-cluster save phase concurrently

The server-level config-sync gate saved clusters sequentially; restore the
drafted design (CONFIG_SYNC.md decision #3). Each cluster's SaveCallBack writes
only its own files (no shared state), so fan them out — plus the global config —
into goroutines and wg.Wait() before the push. Save-before-push ordering (which
lets the single-writer push run lock-free) is preserved by the barrier. Matters
when many clusters run per repman.

fix(dev): wait.sh must match the monitor process, not any substring

run.sh's wait.sh loop counted every ps line containing the AppName
(replication-manager-pro/-osc) — a concurrent run.sh/wait.sh, the start command,
etc. — not just the actual monitor process. So it spun 5s/loop on a phantom
while repman was already gone from ps, which read as a ~20-minute 'graceful stop'
during deploys. Add the 'monitor' qualifier, matching stop.sh's
(grep replication | grep monitor).

chore(dev): instrument wait.sh — print matched ps lines + elapsed, poll 1s

Diagnostic for the deploy stop time: each poll prints [+Ns] count and the actual
ps lines it matched (so we can see any phantom), and on exit reports how many
seconds the monitor process really took to leave ps. Poll every 1s instead of 5s.

fix(dev): stop.sh must signal each monitor pid individually

pid="$(ps ... | awk '{print $2}')"; kill -SIGINT "$pid" broke when the grep
matched more than one monitor (e.g. a leftover from a double start): "$pid"
became a multi-line string and the quoted kill got an invalid target, so SIGINT
was NEVER delivered. repman kept running (handler parked on <-sigs) and it read
as a multi-minute 'graceful stop' — a stop that silently never happened. Loop
over each pid and signal individually; report the count (0 or >1 is the bug).

chore(shutdown): time every shutdown phase so a slow stop pinpoints itself

Instrument the shutdown so the log says exactly where the seconds go, instead of
guessing:
- cluster.Stop(): per-phase durations (scheduler / templateMD5Worker /
  resticUnmount / resticWorkerShutdown / saveConfig) + per-cluster total.
- SIGINT handler: S3 unmount duration, per-cluster stop duration, and the
  all-clusters barrier + total-since-signal.
- final block: in-flight-save wait, global save, final git push,
  ConfigManager.Stop, PushConfigToBackupDir — each timed.

Clusters stop concurrently, so the overall stop time is the slowest cluster's
slowest phase; the log now shows which one.

fix(hang): bound the git push and peer HTTP client with timeouts

Two unbounded network connections that could block forever (a family the
shutdown-timing hunt surfaced):
- ConfigManager.PushConfigToGit: r.Push had no context (the FetchContext above
  it did) — the final git push on SIGINT could stall the whole stop. Use
  r.PushContext with a 120s deadline.
- server_peer.go PeerRequest/RequestForwarder: client := &http.Client{} had no
  Timeout — an unreachable peer hangs the forward (and the O(N^2) peer poll).
  Add a 30s Timeout.

Restic exec/FUSE-unmount are also unbounded but NOT touched here: a blanket
timeout would kill legitimately long backups — that waits on the shutdown
instrumentation to confirm restic is the phase before choosing a safe bound.

fix(hang): bound the Mattermost meet HTTP clients with timeouts

The support-chat/meet integration talks to an (embedded, already-slow) Mattermost
with unbounded clients:
- model.NewAPIv4Client defaults HTTPClient to no timeout -> a slow/hung meet
  server blocks the caller forever. Set HTTPClient.Timeout = 30s.
- the GitLab-SSO login client (&http.Client{Jar: jar}) had no Timeout. Add 30s.
Same timeout-less-connection family as the peer and git-push fixes.

chore(shutdown): fast-fail the final git push at 5s (safety net)

Git push time is always seconds in practice (tracked in the log), so this is not
the slow-stop cause — it's a guard: if gitlab is unreachable during a stop, the
unbounded PushContext(120s) would drag the shutdown. Bound the shutdown push to
5s and abandon on overrun (config is already synced by the dirty-gated push).

fix(shutdown): force/lazy restic unmount on stop — kills the 40-68s stall

UnmountRepo waits up to 5 MINUTES for CanUnmount() (all mount refs released) —
correct in normal operation, but on SHUTDOWN it holds the whole stop hostage to a
lingering mount reference. That wait (not git, not peers, not the worker) was the
observed 40s/68s graceful-stop (peers+marketplace disabled made it 68s, proving
it's the unmount).

Add ForceUnmountRepo: SIGTERM the mount process, lazy-unmount the path
(fusermount -uz / umount -l detaches a busy mount immediately, no user-wait),
short grace then SIGKILL, clear state. cluster.Stop() now calls it; the restic-job
callers keep the safe UnmountRepo with the 5-min wait.

fix(restic): plug the mount-ref leak on physical reseed early-returns

Root cause of the 'fast before, slow now' stop: the guarded ReleaseMountRef defer
was registered ONLY for non-physical reseeds, so the physical path's early-return
errors (ctx.Done, no candidates, no source paths, invalid/escaping path, snapshot
verification) returned WITHOUT releasing the mount ref. The leaked ref then made
UnmountRepo wait its full 5-minute CanUnmount() timeout for a phantom user — the
40-68s (up to 5min) graceful stop.

Register the defer for ALL methods. The physical success path already sets
refOwned=false when it hands the ref to the async cleanup
(registerResticReseedCleanup), so the defer skips it there; the refOwned guard
also prevents double-release with the existing manual releases. Logical was
already safe. Complements ForceUnmountRepo (which protects the stop regardless).

fix(rejoin): reconcile a stale FAILED crash to 'recovered' once the node is healthy again

A failed rejoin stamps a terminal one-shot RejoinResult (failed/no-method/...),
moved into durable FailoverHistory. When the node later recovers by OTHER means
(manual start-slave, save+start, a re-attach the one-shot guard blocked), the
backend already stops raising WARN0186 (assertRejoinResultStates 'resolved'
branch) — but the raw rejoinResult in history still says 'failed', so the GUI
crash button blinks forever on a clean topology and the record lies.

At that same resolved point — node is a healthy slave of the elected master —
rewrite the durable record to RejoinResultRecovered and re-persist (crash.json +
LoadFailoverHistory). History becomes truthful; the blink clears; the working
state and topology were already correct.

fix(peer-health): default to pulling; auto-promote partner plan to smart

The eager peer-health poll (smart/peering) fans out to every shared cluster on
each peer.json reload (GetAllHealthStatus). With the default 'smart', every
registered repman polls the whole for-sale marketplace it receives — O(N^2)
inbound on seller/aggregator instances, and a single dark peer (behind HAProxy)
strands connections in net/http persistConn read/writeLoop that never reclaim
(observed: ~6900 stuck conns to one peer -> 14k goroutines -> monitor loop
crawls; goroutine + socket-table evidence).

- Flip the shipped default cloud18-peer-health-mode 'smart' -> 'pulling': read
  shared-cluster health from the BO-aggregated peer.json (git-pull cadence, no
  per-peer polling). Correct for regular/client instances.
- Auto-promote to 'smart' only for the 'partner' plan (fleets that benefit from
  direct cross-repman polling) — at InitConfig and on CRM runtime plan sync —
  and only from the default so an explicit mode is preserved.

Direct-polling modes remain available (partner fleets); they're just no longer
the default that hundreds of clients inherit.

fix(peer-health): scope live polling to connected users; stop for-sale fan-out & fix socket leak

Fix 1 (scope): a fresh/browsing repman no longer pings for-sale sellers.
All live polling routes through the connected-users scope
(GetHealthStatusForActiveUsers / relevantURLs):
- BatchUpdateClusters no longer polls (no session context, only flat list)
- reload path calls dispatchPeerHealthPoll after updating data (scoped, instant)
- pulling+smart both scoped; removed unscoped GetHealthStatusForUnknownVersions
- peering kept as the sole opt-in unscoped full-mesh
For-sale clusters are polled only once a connected user enters their sale
workflow (pending/sponsor) or is delegated them, never while browsing.

Fix 2 (leak): legitimate fleet polling can no longer strand connections on a
dark peer:
- bounded transport (MaxConnsPerHost:2 hard ceiling + dial/handshake/response
  deadlines) so one peer can never accumulate ~thousands of sockets
- rate-limit login+health to once per Interval and advance LastUpdate on
  failure, so a dark peer is not re-hit every dispatch
- dispatchPeerHealthPoll self-guards (single-flight) across timer + reload

Docs: doc/implementation/peer/MARKETPLACE.md (invariant, identity rules,
sale-workflow timing, both fixes).

refactor(peer-health): first-in-wins atomic claim instead of single-flight

Replace the whole-poll single-flight guard with a finer-grained per-peer claim:
- new pollPeerHealth helper: under pm.mu, check LastUpdate and advance it in the
  same critical section (claim), then release the lock BEFORE the network call.
  First dispatch to reach a peer wins; overlapping dispatches see the fresh
  timestamp and skip -> exactly one call per peer per Interval, and a failed
  attempt is rate-limited like a success. The lock is never held during I/O, so a
  dark peer blocks only its own poll goroutine (all off the main server loop).
- lock PeerURL/Clients access in both pollers and the PeerClusters update in
  GetHealthStatus, so overlapping timer+reload dispatches can no longer race the
  maps BatchUpdateClusters mutates under the same lock.
- GetAllHealthStatus snapshots URLs under RLock instead of iterating the live map.
- drop dispatchPeerHealthPoll's peerHealthBusy self-guard; restore original timer
  block. Different peers still poll in parallel; only the same peer dedups.

Doc S6 Fix 2 updated to describe first-in-wins.

were landing in GitLab. Root cause: the stamp lived in repman.PushConfigToGit —
dead code (its own comment says 'do not wire back in') — while the live config
sync pushes via ConfigManager's git worker (processGitPush), which stamped
nothing. Same trap would have killed a pull indicator.

fires a SetSyncStampHook on successful push AND pull; the server registers a hook
that sets LastConfigGitPush / LastConfigGitPull. Remove the dead server-side stamp.

(view shows stale sibling), passes with it. Isolated, easily revertable.

fix(build): make log-plugin publishing single-owner + opt-in (fixes stale plugin store)

Log-plugins are distributed to servers from the signed-plugin store at runtime; the store had
gone stale (frozen at an old wire version) so current servers received no compatible plugins.

Root cause: publishing was an emergent side-effect. The Makefile 'plugins' target auto-published
whenever signer credentials were present, so several unrelated build variants published
independently — inconsistently, and racing each other's push to the store. A later attempt to
tame that set PLUGIN_PUSH=OFF on only the two PRO Dockerfiles, which silenced the images that
should define the release set while leaving osc/dev/slim to still auto-publish. Net: no build
reliably published the current wire version's set.

Fix — one owner, opt-in:
- Makefile 'plugins': reduce the publish gate to two states — publish iff PLUGIN_PUSH=ON, else
  skip. Removes the credentials-based auto-publish that caused the scatter and the races.
- build-packages.yml: set PLUGIN_PUSH=ON on the tag-triggered package build only. It already
  compiles every arch (amd64 then arm64) sequentially in one job, so it publishes all arches with
  no concurrent push / no ref race. This is the single publisher.
- All docker/nightly/dev/osc/slim builds leave PLUGIN_PUSH unset -> skip.
- doc/implementation/BUILD_PLUGIN_PUBLISHING.md: documents the rule + why the package build is the
  publisher + the wire-version guard as a recommended follow-up.

Reverted the earlier misdirected attempt to publish from the single-arch PRO docker image (would
have covered amd64 only). A one-time publish of the current wire set unblocks existing servers;
version resolution for non-release builds is a separate back-office change.

fix(cloud18): first-claimant domain ownership + surface real GitLab errors (#1617)

* fix(cloud18): enforce first-claimant domain ownership, surface GitLab errors

Cloud18 registration derived nothing useful from GitLab's error bodies: a
group create that failed because the path was already taken produced the
opaque 'API error: 400 - -' (the code parsed only error/error_description,
but GitLab returns validation errors under message, as a string OR a
field->reasons object). It then recursed into InitGroupAccessLevel on the
same unseeable group.

- Add gitlabErrorMessage() to extract a human message from all three GitLab
  error shapes, falling back to the raw body so nothing is dropped.
- CreateCloud18Domain classifies 'has already been taken' and returns the
  ErrDomainAlreadyOwned sentinel.
- InitGroupAccessLevel: on that sentinel, stop with an actionable message
  ('domain already registered to another account; ask its owner to grant
  access') instead of looping. A genuinely-new domain is still created and
  owned by the registering user — first-claimant ownership, enforced by
  GitLab, which is what makes open self-registration safe under the shared
  GitLab/Mattermost SSO.

This is the repman-side complement to disabling the BO email->domain
auto-membership pipeline.

* fix(config-sync): bootstrap first commit into an empty remote config repo

Regression from the ConfigManager config-sync refactor: cloneRepositoryWith-
Bootstrap only retried on repository-not-found, not ErrEmptyRemoteRepository.
A freshly-created (empty) Cloud18 config project therefore never received its
first commit — git.PlainClone returns ErrEmptyRemoteRepository, the push is
skipped, the repo stays empty, and GWARN002 re-fires every sync. Every repman
created before the refactor worked because the pre-ConfigManager push path
handled empty remotes.

On an empty remote, init a local repo pointed at the same URL on branch master
(matching ResolveCurrentLocalBranch) so the subsequent add/commit/push lands
the first commit and creates the remote's default branch.

fix(backup+config): abort backup on dead-volume stall; persist per-cluster settings across restart (#1622)

* fix(backup): abort logical backup on write-stall (dead/hung output volume)

A logical backup whose output volume disappears mid-run hangs forever: the
dead mount blocks splitdump's writes, back-pressures mariadb-dump and repman's
read loop, and JobBackupMysqldump parks on wg.Wait() with no timeout. The
source's --single-transaction read view stays open (pinning purge), and because
the goroutine never returns, the deferred InLogicalBackup clear never runs — so
the GUI STALLED pill won't clear even after the OS processes are killed.

- Add a write-stall watchdog: track bytes flowing through the read loop and, if
  none flow for backup-write-stall-timeout (default 300s, 0 disables), cancel
  the already-cancellable dumpCtx — killing both the dump and splitdump
  subprocesses so the backup returns a clear stall error instead of hanging.
  This is a stall timeout, not a total-time cap; long healthy dumps are
  unaffected. Returning unwinds the defers, clearing InLogicalBackup and
  releasing the source transaction.
- Stop the unconditional time.Sleep(3s) in JobsCheckFinished from taxing the
  monitoring hot path (Ping -> Refresh -> JobsCheckStates): sleep only when
  there is a finished job to flush.

Watchdog is a standalone, unit-tested helper (stall/progress/disabled cases).
Full root-cause + controllable-mount repro in
doc/implementation/cluster/BACKUP_DEAD_VOLUME_STALL.md.

* fix(config): honor monitoring-save-config flag default at startup load

Custom per-cluster settings (e.g. backup-mysqldump-options with --skip-ssl)
were saved to the datadir <cluster>/<cluster>.toml [saved-<cluster>] and git,
but silently reverted after a full repman restart.

Root cause: a save/load gate asymmetry. The SAVE path is gated on
conf.ConfRewrite (the monitoring-save-config pflag, default true), so saves
happen. The STARTUP load gate read firstRead.GetBool("default.monitoring-save-config")
which returns false when the key is absent from the config file, so InitConfig
skipped loading the datadir saved overlays entirely — the persisted section was
never merged. (Runtime reload via ReconstructLiveClusterConfig is not gated this
way, which is why it preserved the value while a restart did not.)

- monitoringSaveConfigEnabled(): default to the flag value when the key is
  absent, only use the file value when explicitly set. InitConfig uses it, so
  the load gate matches the save gate.
- Cluster.LastConfigSaveToDisk (API lastConfigSaveToDisk): stamped when the
  datadir <cluster>.toml is actually written, so the persistence can be observed
  and tested.

Tests: server_reload_test.go (gate default + saved-option survives reload),
regtest testConfigPersistBackupOption (live save round-trip).
Doc: doc/implementation/config/CONFIG_PERSISTENCE_SAVE_LOAD_GATE.md.

* feat(gui): show 'config last saved to disk' on the Settings page

Surfaces Cluster.LastConfigSaveToDisk (API lastConfigSaveToDisk) at the top of

* fix(backup): bound the post-cancel wait so a D-state hung mount can't hang the backup

Review follow-up (the must-do): the stall watchdog cancels via SIGKILL, but a
subprocess wedged in uninterruptible sleep (D-state) on a hard-hung NFS-style
mount never dies, so wg.Wait()/splitDumpPipeline.wg.Wait() could still hang
indefinitely AFTER cancellation — defeating the fix in exactly the incident's
worst case.

- boundedWait(): after the watchdog fires, wait at most backupStallLeakGrace
  (60s) for the reader/pipeline goroutines to unwind; if they don't, return the
  stall error and leak the stuck goroutine rather than hang. The backup call
  always unwinds now (clears InLogicalBackup, releases the source transaction),
  even when the OS process is unkillable.
- Warn when backup-write-stall-timeout is negative (silent-disable vs typo).
- Add backup-write-stall-timeout to etc/config.toml sample.
- Doc: detection-latency note + best-effort/D-state limitation callout.

fix(monitor): run logical reseed off the tick (unblock monitor during restore) (#1626)

* fix(monitor): run logical reseed off the tick, unblocking the monitor loop

A splitdump/mysqldump reseed was dispatched INLINE from StateProcessing, which
runs inline in tickBody — so the whole cluster monitor loop froze inside the
restore for its entire (multi-minute) duration: no health checks, no failover
(not even if the master died mid-reseed), and concurrent slave reseeds
serialized on the single tick goroutine. Confirmed from a goroutine profile
taken during a restore (Run -> tickBody -> StateProcessing -> ProcessReseedLogical
-> splitdump.Restore on the tick goroutine).

Dispatch the reseed via trackTickGoroutine, mirroring the WARN0111 async reseed
path directly below. The per-server IsReseeding flag (claimed atomically by
ProcessReseedLogical via TrySetInReseedBackup) prevents a later tick from
starting a second reseed for the same server, and rejoin/switchover already
refuse a reseeding server — so unblocking the monitor is a net safety gain:
the master can now fail over during a slave reseed, and two slaves genuinely
reseed in parallel.

Orchestrator hot-path change: validate on the OpenSVC topology matrix before
merge.

* rejoin: async everywhere + reconcile the async-reseed record

Make the topology extra-master caller go-spawned (cluster_topo.go) — the last
synchronous RejoinMaster caller — so every rejoin edge runs off the monitor tick.

Because the logical/physical backup reseed only ARMS WARN0075/WARN0074 and returns
while the restore runs off-tick, finishRejoin was recording success at arm time,
before the restore ran. Defer the record to reseed completion:
- recordOrDeferRejoin(): records now for a synchronous restore (RejoinDirectDump),
  or sets reseedFromRejoin and defers when an async reseed is in flight
- WARN0074/WARN0075 completion handlers reconcile finishRejoin with the real
  ProcessReseed* outcome (finishRejoin then clear, so the one-shot has no gap)
- RejoinMaster holds the one-shot while a reseed is in flight
  (HasAnyReseedingState || reseedFromRejoin)

No retry semantics changed — the record is one-shot either way; it is only made
honest for the async paths. Docs: execution model, full rejoin workflow (triggers/
gates/per-path states), and the WARN0189 reseed-progress coverage gap.

* rejoin: fix async-reseed record — reconcile from observed health at true completion

Review of the previous commit found two real regressions, both because the
reconciliation was hooked to the WARN handler return values, which for most reseed
methods fire before the detached restore goroutine even starts:

- WARN0074 physical: ProcessReseedPhysical arms 'go WaitAndSendSST -> go SSTRunSender'
  and returns nil, so reconciling on its return recorded success at ARM time.
- direct mysqldump: RejoinDirectDump spawns 'go JobRejoinMysqldumpFromSource' and
  returns nil with no WARN state, so reseedFromRejoin was NEVER cleared -> RejoinMaster
  permanently blocked for that server.

The only signal every reseed method shares is clearing IsReseeding on completion, and
none carries a uniform success/fail return. So:
- remove the WARN0074/WARN0075 handler reconciliation (wrong hook);
- add reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds (per tick, before assertRejoinResultStates):
  record finishRejoin from OBSERVED health at IsReseeding-clear — healthy slave of the
  current master = success, else failed (self-corrects to 'recovered' via
  assertRejoinResultStates once it becomes a healthy slave);
- generic WARN0189 'rejoin reseed in progress, started T' (rejoinReseedStart) for
  methods without byte instrumentation, so a rejoin is always visible in the GUI and
  its landing outcome is the proof the reconciliation works.

Docs corrected: the per-method completion table (all async), the observed-health
reconcile, and the generic progress state.

* rejoin: update stale comments to reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds (review #1626)

The guard comment and recordOrDeferRejoin doc still described the removed

splitdump: native Go transactional restore (replace mysql --force) + reseed progress (#1627)

* fix(splitdump): native Go transactional restore, no more mysql --force

Replace the mysql --force subprocess with a native Go loader:
- one dedicated pinned *sqlx.Conn per worker (never the shared pool), so
  session state (USE/FK/UNIQUE) and transaction affinity hold
- INSERT/REPLACE batched into transactions, retried on deadlock (1213) /
  lock-wait-timeout (1205); any other error is returned (fail loud)
- LOCK/UNLOCK TABLES and ALTER..DISABLE/ENABLE KEYS dropped; DELIMITER honored
- binlog on/off follows the master/slave decision via GetConnNoBinlog;
  reset uses version-aware server.ResetMaster()

Fixes silent data loss: --force skipped failing statements and exited 0, so
executeMysqlRestoreContext (which only read stderr on non-zero exit) reported
success while the first shard's rows were dropped under N-way parallel load.

* feat(splitdump): reseed progress (WARN0189) for the native-Go loader

The monolithic mysqldump path reports streamed-bytes progress via WARN0189, but
the splitdump reseed (per-table shard files) showed only a silent 'processing'.

Add beginReseedProgress (stamp the in-flight restore, total = sum of shard sizes)
+ countReseedReader (wrap each shard reader into one accumulating byte counter),
and wire them into restoreSplitdumpWithMysql / restoreSplitdumpFileGo so a
splitdump reload shows the same live '<streamed> out of <total>' line per tick.

* refactor(splitdump): remove dead mysql --force CLI restore path

restoreSplitdumpFileContextWithPreamble, restoreSplitdumpFileContextStripDefiner,
and buildSplitdumpRestorePreamble were the old subprocess (mysql --force) restore
path, fully replaced by the native-Go transactional loader. Production no longer
calls them (only their tests did). Remove the functions and their tests.

* fix(splitdump): honor continueOnError for INSERT batches (mysql.system-all) + parser tests

Review #1627: continueOnError (the old --force tolerance for mysql.system-all seed
rows) only reached execSplitdumpSingle, never execSplitdumpBatch — so system-all
INSERTs went through the transactional batch path and would hard-abort the entire
restore on the first conflicting seed row (pre-existing default account, time_zone).

Refactor the streamer into pure, testable pieces:
- classifySplitdumpStatement (skip/insert/other),
- forEachSplitdumpStatement (DELIMITER-aware segmentation, no DB),
- planAndExecSplitdump (routing) driven by an injectable splitdumpExecutor.

When continueOnError, INSERT/REPLACE now run individually (single, coe=true) so one
bad seed row is skipped instead of rolling back the whole transaction — matching the
old --force. Add parser + continueOnError regression tests (no live DB). Also note
the per-worker *sqlx.DB rationale.

configurator: floor every allocated engine buffer at 128M (fix innodb_buffer_pool_size=0M) (#1656)

GetConfigInnoDBBPSize (and the myisam/aria/tokudb/querycache/s3/rocksdb
siblings) computed a buffer size as (usable_mem * pct / 100), where
usable_mem = prov-db-memory - memReserveMB(2048). For any prov-db-memory <= 2GB
usable clamps to 0, so the buffer emitted 0M. InnoDB with a 16K page size refuses
to start below 6 MiB, so a small/misresolved prov-db-memory (observed: a db
provisioned at 256M) produced innodb_buffer_pool_size=0M and the DB would not boot.

Add a shared engineMemMB() floor: an ENABLED engine (share pct > 0) never gets
less than minEngineMemMB (128M); a DISABLED engine (pct <= 0) stays at 0 so we
never silently turn on a feature meant to be off (e.g. the query cache).

Fixes the test that asserted the broken value (256M -> 0) and adds a guard that a
0%-share engine is not floored.

Note (separate follow-up): ConfigDiscovery() reverse-derives prov-db-memory by
summing the live buffer variables, which can shrink it over restarts; that loop is
why prov-db-memory became 256 and still needs addressing.

fix(jobs): harden API job-state reporting

Fix the dbjobs API-mode terminal callback path when the completion
state is built in the top-level JOBS loop.

- drop the invalid top-level 'local' declaration for api_job_result so
  auditlog/sqlerrorlog and other non-backup jobs don't send an empty
  {jobstate} path segment
- fail fast in report_job_state when the state is empty instead of
  issuing a request that can only 404
- retry job-state callbacks with a larger budget for terminal done/error
  updates, while keeping processing/waiting on the normal retry budget
- document the related HTTP 404 symptom and its root cause alongside the
  startup reconciliation notes

Only the staged files are included in this commit.

fix(jobs): resolve stale SQL-mode log jobs

Address the SQL-mode variant of stale database job state for short-lived
DB log fetch tasks.

This commit makes two targeted changes:

- make dbjobs_new.sh write the final SQL completion update synchronously in
  doneJob() instead of backgrounding it, so the job row is not left at
  state=1/done=0 if the shell exits before the write lands
- extend JobsCheckPending() with a stale-running cleanup path for SQL-mode
  log jobs only (errorlog, slowquery, auditlog, sqlerrorlog), converting
  rows older than one hour from state=1/done=0 to a terminal error state
  and refreshing the UI cache when affected rows are found

The cleanup is deliberately scoped to DB log jobs; backup, reseed, and
flashback tasks are excluded because they can legitimately run much longer
than an hour.

Also update the implementation note to document the SQL-mode stale-running
symptom, the likely missed-final-write cause, and why this fix stays narrow.

fix(server): refresh server-level ServiceRepos from BO-pushed repos.json (#1702)

The GUI DB version dropdown reads repman.ServiceRepos (json:"serviceRepos"),
which was loaded once at startup and never refreshed. The BO-push feature
(fc57e7a8c) only refreshed the per-cluster DockerRepos (json:"-", not
serialized), leaving the comment "ServiceRepos is updated by the caller if
needed" with no caller. So after the back office pushes a fresh
plugins/data/repos.json, new image tags (e.g. mariadb 11.4.12) land in
DockerRepos but never reach the GUI, which keeps showing the startup list.

Add ReplicationManager.ReloadServiceRepos() (reused at startup) and call it
from the -pull git-pull hook alongside cluster.ReloadDockerRepos(), so the
server-level list refreshes when the BO delivers a new repos.json.

chore(build): regenerate embedded repos.json via scripts/updaterepo.sh + `make repos`

The embedded docker image tag catalog (share/repo/repos.json) is the fallback
the GUI/configurator uses when no back-office repos.json has been pushed. It had
gone stale (topped out at 11.4.7, plus malformed tags) because it was a manually
committed file with no regeneration path in the build.

- Move the generator to scripts/updaterepo.sh (was a root script) and mirror the
  back-office generate-docker-repos.sh scrape logic: Docker Hub registry v2,
  paginated for ALL tags, with an invalid-JSON / zero-tag guard so a transient
  API failure can't blank the committed catalog.
- Trim scraped tags to {name}: repman's TagResult only reads the tag name, so
  dropping Docker Hub's per-tag metadata keeps the embedded file ~140KB instead
  of ~17MB.
- Add a `make repos` target that runs it (network + jq; kept OUT of the default
  build, to be run in CI/release like the BO's daily job).
- Regenerate share/repo/repos.json (now includes 11.4.12 and current tags).

Refs #1702 (embedded-fallback-freshness half of the stale version-list bug).

   --user flag value to be lost when using --user=value syntax
2. Empty ConfDirBackup: User lookup failed with empty username, resulting in
   empty backup directory path
3. Inappropriate fatal error: Arbitrator never saves config, doesn't need
   backup directory

- Add WithArbitration compile-time flag to identify arbitrator binary
- Skip ConfDirBackup requirement when WithArbitration="ON"

the arbitrator to start without requiring a config backup directory.

- Add WithArbitration check to PushConfigToBackupDir() early return

MEDIUM:

bytes variable comparison

The staged content adds intelligent value comparison logic for database variables to handle three different types of values:

Key Features Added:
Size Unit Normalization (parseSizeToBytes)

Converts size units (K, M, G, T, KB, MB, GB, TB) to bytes using BigInt
Handles values larger than JavaScript's MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (>9 petabytes)
Supports decimal values like 1.5G
Parses plain numeric strings as bytes
Size Variable Detection (isSizeVariable)

Identifies size-related variables by name patterns
Detects variables ending with: _size, _buffer, _memory, _cache, _length, _limit
Detects variables starting with: max_, min_
Detects InnoDB and buffer/cache related variables
Unified Comparison Logic (areValuesEqual)

Smart comparison that handles:
Boolean variables: ON/OFF, 1/0, TRUE/FALSE are treated as equivalent
Size variables: 4G equals 4294967296 bytes
Regular variables: Standard string comparison
Prevents false positives when comparing different representations of the same value
Impact:
Replaced all manual comparison logic throughout the component (7 locations)
Variables like innodb_buffer_pool_size with value 4G in configurator now correctly matches 4294967296 in runtime
Eliminates incorrect "difference" alerts for semantically equal values

fix: use correct TLS config name in mysql.RegisterTLSConfig

The Go MySQL driver's RegisterTLSConfig expects a plain name (e.g.
"tlsconfig") that matches the value after "tls=" in the DSN. The
constants ConstTLSCurrentConfig and ConstTLSOldConfig contain the
full DSN fragment ("&tls=tlsconfig"), which was incorrectly passed
as the registration name. The driver then looks up "tlsconfig" but
finds nothing registered under that name, silently falling back to
no TLS.

Split the constants into DSN fragments (unchanged) and registration
names (new), and use the registration names in RegisterTLSConfig.

This fixes TLS connections to MySQL 8.4 with caching_sha2_password,
which requires TLS for initial authentication.

fix(app): correct app monitoring debounce semantics

- Per-route debounce: AppErrConsecutiveMap replaces single shared counter.
  Failures are now tracked per route-key per GetMonitoringStatus call,
  preventing counter inflation when multiple routes fail in one tick.
- Isolated counter reset: success on one route no longer clears failure
  history on other routes.
- Immediate config-error emission: no-routes and unsupported protocol
  now emit APPERR immediately without debouncing.
- Temporary TCP dual emission: TCP failures emit both APPERR003 (canonical)
  and APPERR001 (compatibility) after threshold, for migration window.
- Configurable threshold: new cluster-level
  app-error-debounce-threshold (default 3) replaces hardcoded constant.

add cluster-local secret version tracking for encrypted secrets

Introduce per-cluster secret_store.json reconciliation on monitor ticks with bootstrap, atomic persistence, and semantic change detection while storing hash_ values only. Add vault-aware feature-flag defaults and focused tests for config behavior and version-store updates.

trigger immediate secret version reconciliation on API credential changes

Add TrackedSecretCompareSnapshot() to cluster package for change detection.
Hook into setClusterSetting() to trigger ReconcileSecretVersionStore()
when any tracked secret changes via interactive/API path.

This ensures secret_store.json is updated immediately when users
change credentials through the API, rather than waiting for the
next monitor tick.

Tests added:
- TestTrackedSecretCompareSnapshotIncludesOnlyTrackedSecrets
- TestTrackedSecretSnapshotChanged

add manual secret-store pruning utility

Add reusable secret-store pruning helpers in cluster package and a
manual server command to prune per-cluster secret history by keeping
only the last N versions per key.

The command supports dry-run output and reuses the same core logic so
future scheduled pruning can call the same implementation safely.

Tests added for prune behavior, dry-run semantics, and cluster lookup
error handling.

add manual secret-store copy utility with hash dedupe

Introduce a manual secret-store-copy command that exports per-cluster
secret history to {monitoring-confdir}/cluster.d/{cluster}_secret_store.json.

Use raw-byte SHA256 comparison to avoid redundant copies, support dry-run
and overwrite controls, and keep copy/write logic reusable for future
scheduled invocation without duplicating behavior.

Also add tests for copy, dedupe, overwrite gate, dry-run semantics,
and server-side cluster/confdir path resolution.

add secret-store restore utility for cluster config

Add a manual secret-store-restore command that restores selected secrets
(or all store keys) by version or timestamp into
{monitoring-confdir}/cluster.d/{cluster}.toml.

Support config-first restore with dry-run, plus optional --apply-runtime
for a safe runtime subset, and add resolver/listing helpers with tests.

final CLI flag naming: --secret-key and --decrypt-key-path

Rename restore command flags for clarity:
- --key → --secret-key (explicit secrets to restore)
- --key-path → --decrypt-key-path (legacy decrypt key only)

This avoids naming collisions and makes the two key-related
flags semantically distinct and operator-friendly.

Tests updated accordingly.

feat(server): add global alert state machine with cluster heartbeat supervision

Implement a global state machine on ReplicationManager that mirrors the
cluster alert lifecycle, with the first producer being stalled cluster
heartbeat detection.

- Add ProcessAlertStateLifecycle() for open/resolve/preserve lifecycle

- Add MonitorGlobalHeartbeatSupervision and MonitorGlobalHeartbeatStallThreshold config
- Add comprehensive tests for all ACs

Key design:

- Warning resolves automatically when heartbeat advances
- Supervision is configurable and disabled by default (configurable via flag)
- Nil-safe throughout, mutex-protected cluster map iteration

feat(server): add GET /api/global/http-logs endpoint and frontend integration

Adds a new server-level log viewing feature that exposes the ReplicationManager's
in-memory HTTP ring buffer via a protected REST endpoint, with matching React
dashboard integration.

Server changes:
- server/api_global.go: Implement handlerMuxGlobalLogs which copies the repman.Logs
  ring buffer (under mutex lock), filters for general (non-cluster) entries, and
  returns a globalLogsResponse JSON payload. Define globalLogsSnapshot and
  globalLogsResponse types that mirror the cluster log shape so the frontend's
  existing Logs component can render both without modification.
- server/api.go & server/http.go: Register GET /api/global/http-logs route under
  the token-authenticated middleware in both mux configurations.

Frontend changes:
- globalClustersService.js: Add getGlobalLogs() which calls GET /global/http-logs.
- globalClustersSlice.js: Add getGlobalLogs async thunk, initialize globalLogs
  state (mirrors globalMetrics shape), and handle fulfilled/rejected cases.
- Home/index.jsx: Dispatch getGlobalLogs({}) alongside existing globalMetrics
  and globalAlerts polling so global logs stay in sync.
- GlobalItems/index.jsx: Add GlobalLogs sub-component (renders existing Logs
  component with the global log buffer), extract MetricsBody helper, wrap both
  Server Metrics and Global Logs inside AccordionComponent for a cleaner layout.
- GlobalItems/styles.module.scss: Strip unused theme-driven styles and dark/light
  class rules; simplify container to a plain padding wrapper since AccordionComponent
  handles its own theming.

This closes the global log viewing gap: previously only cluster-scoped HTTP logs
were exposed, making server-side debugging tedious in multi-cluster setups.

fix(server/ui): harden global heartbeat supervision and telemetry

Use locked heartbeat tracking with warning/critical global error keys, switch global RSS to real process RSS, and remove unnecessary global polling and duplicate UI helpers.

Note: api.go and http.go are backed by different listeners, so matching route registrations must be maintained in both.

fix(server/ui): reduce global dashboard polling latency and alert duplication

Make global metrics CPU sampling non-blocking and add collapsible global alert previews with an open-in-modal path so the dashboard remains summary-focused while full details stay in AlertModal.

feat(logplugin): add binlog security plugins for cleartext-password and credit-card leak detection

Introduces incremental binlog QUERY event scanning via a persistent
replication.BinlogSyncer kept open on each ServerMonitor.  On every
CheckLogPlugins tick, newly-arrived events are drained (50 ms budget)
into a BinlogEventLog ring buffer and passed to external plugins
through the existing wire protocol.

No double-fetch: reuses server.BinaryLogFile (already refreshed by
CheckBinaryLogs) — no extra GetMasterStatus query.  On binlog
rotation or server failure the syncer is closed and reopened cleanly
via CloseBinlogEventSyncer(), called from SetFailed() and Close().

New config flags:
  log-plugin-binlog-scan              (bool, default false)
  monitoring-binlog-event-log-length  (int,  default 200)

New external plugins:
  plugin-binlog-cleartext-password  WARN0310 — detects IDENTIFIED BY /
    SET PASSWORD literals in binlog QUERY events
  plugin-binlog-creditcard-leak     WARN0311 — detects Luhn-valid PAN
    candidates in binlog QUERY events

Wire protocol (wire.Request / StdioRequest / LogSource) extended with
BinlogEvents []BinlogEvent field; backwards-compatible (empty slice
when scan is disabled).

feat(logplugin): verify Ed25519 signature before loading external plugins

Plugin binaries delivered via git-pull could be tampered with if the pull
repo is compromised. This adds signature verification on load:

- LoadPluginsFromDir now accepts LoadOptions{PubKeyPath, SigDir}.
  When PubKeyPath is set every plugin binary must have a valid Ed25519 .sig
  sidecar in SigDir (<ShareDir>/plugins/). Unsigned or tampered plugins are
  rejected with an ERR log entry and never executed.
  When PubKeyPath is empty verification is skipped (dev/unsigned builds).

- VerifyPluginSignature(binPath, sigDir, pubKeyPath) is exported for use
  in tests and tooling.

- New config option: plugin-signing-public-key (path to raw Ed25519 pub key).
  Default empty = skip verification. Set in production config.toml:
    plugin-signing-public-key = "/etc/replication-manager/plugin-signing.pub"

- .sig files are no longer pushed to the plugin signer repo — they ship
  with the repman package (share/plugins/) as originally intended.
  The signer repo now holds only unsigned plugin binaries.

fix(plugins): fix mutex-copy deadlock in snapshotHttpLog/snapshotSlowLog

snapshotHttpLog(s18log.HttpLog) and snapshotSlowLog(s18log.SlowLog) took
their arguments BY VALUE.  Both structs embed sync.Mutex.  Copying a mutex
is forbidden by the Go memory model: if ErrorLogWatcher (or SlowLogWatcher)
holds server.ErrorLog.L at the exact moment the monitoring loop copies the
struct for the argument, the copy has mutex.state=1 (locked).  The subsequent
log.L.Lock() inside the snapshot function then sleeps on a semaphore that
nobody will ever signal → permanent deadlock in the monitoring goroutine.
This is why cluster.StateMachine.heartbeats stays at 1 on clusters with
plugins enabled: CheckLogPlugins() blocks forever after the first tick.

Fix: change both functions to take *s18log.HttpLog and *s18log.SlowLog
(pointer parameters) and update the three call sites accordingly.

fix(plugins): set WaitDelay on external plugin subprocesses to prevent monitoring loop hang

When a plugin subprocess spawns children that inherit the stdout/stderr
pipes, cmd.Output() blocks forever waiting for pipe EOF even after the
5-second context timeout kills the plugin binary.  This caused the
monitoring loop to freeze at heartbeats=1 on clusters with external plugins.

Set cmd.WaitDelay = 2s so that Go forcibly closes the I/O goroutines 2
seconds after the context fires, guaranteeing cmd.Output() returns within
p.timeout + 2s regardless of orphaned subprocesses.

Also treat exec.ErrWaitDelay the same as DeadlineExceeded so the finding
correctly reports "plugin timed out" in both cases.

fix(plugins): isolate external plugin registry per-cluster to prevent cross-cluster hang

GlobalRegistry was a process-wide singleton shared across all clusters.
When cluster A (belair) loaded 23 external plugins into GlobalRegistry,
every other cluster's CheckLogPlugins() also iterated over those 23
plugins and spawned subprocesses for each of its servers — even clusters
configured with log-plugin=false or with no plugins installed.

Any subprocess that hung (pipe leak, slow binary) froze ALL cluster
monitoring loops, causing heartbeats to stall for every cluster.

Fix: introduce NewRegistry() that clones GlobalRegistry's built-in
plugins into a fresh Registry.  Each cluster now owns a pluginRegistry
populated only with its own external plugins.  ReloadLogPlugins resets
the cluster registry to a fresh built-in clone before scanning the
cluster-specific plugin dir, so removed binaries also disappear on
hot-reload.

fix: change RelayLogSpace from sql.NullInt64 to sql.Null[uint64]

Percona/MySQL 8.4 can return Relay_Log_Space as a large uint64 that exceeds
int64 range, causing SHOW REPLICA STATUS parsing to fail with:
  sql: Scan error on column index 22, name \"Relay_Log_Space\":
  converting driver.Value type uint64 to a int64: value out of range

This scan failure causes the replica to disappear from topology detection,
leading to cascading failures:
- slave seen as StandAlone
- no failover candidates available
- automatic failover can create split-brain

The fix changes the field type to sql.Null[uint64] which safely handles
large unsigned values and preserves NULL semantics.

Also adds comprehensive tests covering:
- NULL, uint64, int64, MaxUint64, negative rejection
- []byte and string numeric inputs
- overflow and non-numeric rejection

Fix /api/clusters/{name}/plugins returning only built-in plugins

The handler was calling logplugin.GlobalRegistry.All() which only contains
the 4 built-in plugins (errorlog, sqlerrorlog, slowlog, auditlog).
External security plugins (plugin-score-auth, plugin-score-passwords, etc.)
are loaded into per-cluster registries via LoadPluginsFromDir and never
appear in GlobalRegistry.

so all plugins — built-in + external — are returned for that cluster.

every plugin; now respects per-plugin config["enabled"] override.

feat: register handler sets Cloud18 config and runs InitGitConfig connect on success

After the CRM API returns 201:
  - Set Cloud18Domain / Cloud18SubDomain / Cloud18SubDomainZone from parsed URI
  - Set Cloud18GitUser (email) and store password in Conf.Secrets
  - Enable Cloud18 = true
  - Call InitGitConfig — the same connect flow triggered by cloud18=true in
    global settings: authenticates with GitLab via basic auth, creates a
    personal access token, idempotently creates main+pull Git projects,
    sets GitUrl/GitUrlPull, and clones the config repo

If InitGitConfig fails, Cloud18 is rolled back to false and the 201 body
is returned with an extra connect_error field so the caller can retry.

Fix cloud18 connect blocking HTTP server by running InitGitConfig async

InitGitConfig makes 5+ sequential HTTP calls to GitLab (OAuth token,
user lookup, group access, PAT rotation/creation). Running it synchronously
in the HTTP handler blocked all other browser requests for 5+ seconds.

Set Cloud18=true optimistically and launch InitGitConfig in a goroutine.
The handler returns 200 immediately. If InitGitConfig fails in the
background, Cloud18 is reverted to false and the UI reflects that on the
next monitor poll. The goroutine calls SaveConfig when done to persist
the final state (PAT + GitUrl on success, Cloud18=false on failure).

This also correctly handles the reconnect-after-days scenario where the
PAT has expired: InitGitConfig always runs and re-authenticates with the
stored email+password credentials.

Force monitor refresh after connect/disconnect so UI updates immediately

After setGlobalSetting returns, config?.cloud18 only updates on the next
getMonitoredData polling cycle, which could be many seconds away. Dispatch
getMonitoredData immediately after connect/disconnect so the button state
(Connect ↔ Disconnect) transitions without waiting for the interval.

Lock URI fields when credentials exist, not just when connected

Disconnect is a temporary deactivation — the CRM is not notified of URI
changes. Editing domain/subdomain/zone after disconnect without going
through Unregister would orphan the old GitLab projects on the server.

URI fields are now read-only whenever hasCredentials is true (connected
or disconnected with stored creds). Only Unregister clears credentials,
which is the correct gate for URI changes.

Track uriUnlocked state after Unregister to gate URI field editing

URI fields (domain/subdomain/zone) must only be editable after an explicit
Unregister call, which is the CRM call that drops both the GitLab projects
and the subscription DB record for the old URI. Disconnect alone is not
enough — the CRM still holds the URI record.

After successful Unregister: uriUnlocked=true, URI fields become editable,
and hasCredentials is forced false so the UI shows Register (not Connect)
since the CRM subscription row is gone and must be recreated.

uriUnlocked resets automatically when isConnected becomes true (new
registration completed).

while still ensuring new wire versions are published automatically.

expected config values.

1. Root cause: hasPrintDefaultsContent() guard in JobFinishReceiveFile
   checks that .tmp has actual --prefixed lines before overwriting
   dummy.cnf or current.cnf. Empty .tmp is skipped with a warning.

2. Delta guard: WriteDeltaVariables skips when server IsDown() or when
   VariablesMap lacks config/deployed data (HasConfigValues/HasDeployedValues).

after ShutdownClean, so the orchestrator transitions to a clean
"stopped" state. The SQL shutdown with innodb_fast_shutdown=0 still
runs first for the InnoDB full purge, then the orchestrator stop
ensures a clean state for the subsequent start.

test(regtest): add testOpenSVCUpgradeWarnRecovery

Reproduces the flacq May 2026 incident: a failed rolling upgrade
leaves OpenSVC in warn state, blocking subsequent starts with 409.

Scenario:
1. Stop slave cleanly
2. Inject broken config.tar.gz (invalid tarball)
3. Start slave — container fails, OpenSVC enters warn state
4. Verify slave is down
5. Restore good config
6. Clear instance state (per-node instance API)
7. Start slave — should succeed
8. Wait for replication sync

Requires OpenSVC orchestrator and at least one slave.

fix(opensvc): optimistic clear before start/restart

— the optimistic clear makes them unnecessary.

For slaves (the normal rolling upgrade path), only innodb_fast_shutdown=0
is set — the orchestrator stop handles the actual shutdown.

The orchestrator stop always follows to ensure clean state transition
and stop ALL containers (db + jobs) so both get the new image on start.

fix(regtest): inject broken delta.cnf instead of broken tarball

container already has valid config on its persistent volume. Breaking

MariaDB to refuse to start with "unknown variable" error.

hardcoded sleep.

- Stop: "OpenSVC V3 stop for..."
- Abort: "Aborting orchestration for..."
- Clear: "Clearing instance state for... on node..."

bypasses the global monitor state check and starts/stops containers

feat(monitoring): implement monitoring-schema-change-script hook

Call the configured script when a table schema change is detected
during MonitorMasterTableSchema(). The script receives:
  $1 cluster name
  $2 server URL (host:port)
  $3 schema name
  $4 table name
  $5 change type ("new" for new tables, "altered" for CRC change)

First-time cache population ("init") is skipped to avoid flooding
the script on startup when the table dictionary is empty.

The config key monitoring-schema-change-script was already registered
but never called — this wires it into the monitoring loop.

feat(monitoring): pass column diff to schema change script via stdin

The monitoring-schema-change-script now receives a unified diff of
column definitions piped to stdin:

  --- schema.table (before)
  +++ schema.table (after)
  - old_col varchar(50) NOT NULL
  + old_col varchar(100) NOT NULL
  + new_col int DEFAULT 0
  - dropped_col text

Covers all change types:
  - "new": all columns shown as additions (old is empty)
  - "altered": before/after diff of changed columns
  - "dropped": would show all columns as removals (if table tracking added)

Args unchanged: $1=cluster $2=server $3=schema $4=table $5=change_type

feat(monitoring): detect dropped tables and call schema change script

After scanning current tables, compare with cached DictTables to find
tables that no longer exist. Call the schema change script with
changeType="dropped" and all old columns as removals in the diff.

All three DDL types now covered:
  - new: table created (all cols as + additions)
  - altered: table changed (before/after column diff)
  - dropped: table removed (all cols as - removals)

fix(pr-review): address schema change script review findings

1. Explicit nil for oldCols when changeType == "new" — avoids relying
   on GetTableFromDict returning an empty-but-non-nil Table.

2. Script timeout: 30s via context.WithTimeout to prevent stalling
   the monitoring loop during active schema migrations.

3. Log output only when len(out) > 0 (avoid noisy empty log lines).

4. Unit tests for columnDiff and formatColumn covering:
   - New table (all additions, no removals)
   - Dropped table (all removals, no additions)
   - Altered table (before/after for changed, new/dropped columns)
   - Empty old and new
   - Identical columns (no diff lines)

Writes to LogDDL from MonitorMasterTableSchema when a table is

not cross-server drift). Compares current Variables with a
PrevVariables snapshot taken on each monitoring cycle.

Script args: $1=cluster $2=server_url
Stdin: unified diff of changed variables:

feat(monitoring): configurable variable change ignore list + dynamic SQL detection

2. MariaDB 10.1+: queries INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SYSTEM_VARIABLES where

fix: add 120s timeout to jobs-upgrade socat listener

The jobs-upgrade socat TCP-LISTEN had no timeout, unlike the config
listener which uses timeout. If repman never connects to push the new
script (network issue, repman restart), the socat blocks forever,
dbjobs never exits, and the launcher never re-execs with the new
version. This caused dbjobs to stay stuck for days (observed: 7 days).

fix: add accept-timeout to backup restore socat listeners

All four backup restore socat listeners (reseed/flashback for
xtrabackup/mariabackup) had no timeout on TCP-LISTEN, causing dbjobs
to block forever if repman never connected to stream the backup.

Use socat accept-timeout=600 instead of timeout wrapper — this only
applies to the LISTEN/accept phase (10min to wait for connection),
once data flows the transfer runs without time limit. This prevents
the stuck-for-days scenario without killing large backup transfers.

fix: remove JWT requirement from needs/{taskname} endpoint

The needs/ endpoint was moved behind validateTokenMiddleware which
broke backward compatibility with old dbjobs scripts (pre-3.1.25)
that use encrypted body auth. This caused a chain failure: jobsCheck
couldn't run → script never sent back → CheckJobsVersion never ran →
config refresh cookie never set → print-defaults never executed →
empty delta tracking.

The handler is read-only (returns true/false for task cookies) so
token protection is unnecessary. Old scripts can now self-upgrade
and resume normal operation.

fix: SST Reseed log level from WARN to INFO

fix: remove JWT middleware from job endpoints that use SecretLoginCheck

receive-jobs-check, send-jobs-upgrade, write-log, receive-task, and
job-state handlers all authenticate via SecretLoginCheck (encrypted
body) internally. The validateTokenMiddleware added for API mode broke
backward compatibility with old dbjobs scripts (pre-3.1.25) that
don't obtain a JWT token. The middleware rejected requests before the
handler's own auth could run.

fix: prevent plugin-push race from failing Docker build

Two issues fixed:

1. plugin-push git push failed when concurrent builds updated the
   signer repo: "cannot lock ref - expected X but got Y". Added
   git fetch + rebase before push so the local clone picks up
   changes from the previous build.

2. plugin-push failure killed the entire Docker build (make pro
   returned error 2). Made plugin-push non-fatal — plugins are
   already built and signed in the image, pushing to the signer
   repo is a distribution step that can be retried.

3. Remove committed .sig files and ephemeral pub key from git —
   these are build artifacts generated by make plugin-sigs, not
   source files. Added to .gitignore. The official pub key and
   sigs are generated at build time from the signer repo keypair.

subsequent Stop() (cluster shutdown, scheduler toggle, re-init) would

fix(arbitration): prevent election race and heartbeat reset

Two bugs caused both repman instances to end up standby:

1. RequestArbitration() used a transaction but SELECT queries lacked
   FOR UPDATE, allowing concurrent elections to both read count==0
   and both lose. Add FOR UPDATE suffix for MySQL/InnoDB to serialize
   concurrent election attempts.

2. WriteHeartbeat() reset elected status 'E' back to 'U' every tick
   when count(distinct master)==1. That condition means both instances
   agree on the same master (split-brain resolved), not that the
   election should be undone. Invert the logic: only reset when
   count>1 (masters diverge, true split-brain).

fix: self-heal missing per-cluster plugins symlink in ReloadLogPlugins

The <cluster>/plugins → ../plugins symlink is created only at startup
and by the git pull sync. When the cluster working dir does not exist
yet at startup (or was wiped by a config restore), symlink creation
fails and is never retried: plugins stay unloaded, or stale registry
entries fork/exec dangling paths producing a WARN0203 storm on every
tick (seen on dev image with belair cluster).

ReloadLogPlugins now recreates the symlink to the shared plugin dir
when the per-cluster path is missing, so plugin loading no longer
depends on startup/pull-sync ordering.

fix: stable secret ciphertext across config saves to stop git churn

Every periodic SaveConfig re-encrypted all secrets from memory with a
fresh random IV (GetEncryptedString -> crypto Encrypt), so saved config
files always differed even when nothing changed. With git config sync
this meant a commit+push every save cycle (~2min), phantom 'config
changed' on every peer/standby pull, and cluster reloads flooding the
state machine (OPENED/RESOLV churn, cookies recreated).

Secret gains a Crypted ciphertext cache, seeded at load from the config
file's own hash_ value. New Config.GetStableEncryptedValue reuses the
existing ciphertext while it still decrypts to the current value and
only re-encrypts (fresh IV, unchanged crypto) when the secret really
changed. EncryptSecretValue mirrors DecryptSecretValue composite
handling (user:hash_..., comma lists). Both GetEncryptedValueFromMemory
implementations (server + cluster) now use it, including credential
composites; empty secrets are no longer encrypted into junk.

feat: role-free standby config sync via isolated .config clone

Per-cluster arbitration elections are incompatible with role-based git
sync (active pushes / standby pulls): with a mixed active/standby
cluster set there is no server-level role to gate on, and the old
PullActiveConfig ran git checkout --force + pull --force directly on
the LIVE working dir — destructive for locally saved state of clusters
active on that node — gated by HasStandbyClusterWithGitSync (any single
standby cluster made a node pull, so after a failover both peers
pulled).

New model, change-driven and role-free:
- pull lands in an isolated clone WorkingDir/.config/ (same principle
  as .pull/), gitignored; the live tree is never force-reset
- files (<name>.toml, overwrite.toml) are copied into the live tree
  only for clusters where this node is standby with
  git-config-sync-standby, and only when bytes actually differ (real
  change detection before the reload)
- PullActiveConfig now runs on both peers whenever arbitration is on;
  HasStandbyClusterWithGitSync removed
- GitPush stays ungated: with stable secret ciphertext, nodes with no
  real edits push nothing

Also documents the per-cluster-election design decision (server-level
election considered and rejected: arbitration protects each cluster's
master, and masters legitimately sit on different sides of a
partition) in HEARTBEAT_AND_ARBITRATION.md.

fix: main loop must never block on network I/O — detach periodic tasks

The %60 block launched git sync (PullActiveConfig + GitPush wait=true),
cloud18 pull-repo sync and peer health polls as goroutines and then
wg.Wait()ed on them inside the main loop. go-git has no timeout: one
hung pull froze the entire loop — observed 2h frozen on dbaas-fr-2-dr
(last log 10:30:38, empty state machine, no heartbeat states, Monitor
0/0) while HTTP kept serving, so supervision died silently.

Tasks now run detached, each guarded by an atomic busy flag: if a round
is still running at the next cycle it is skipped and GWARN013@<task>
opens (git config sync / cloud18 pull-repo sync / peer health poll), so
a hang degrades into a visible Monitor warning instead of killing every
state producer.

fix: bound all go-git network calls, never wait on manager queue in loop

Second freeze found after the detach fix: the git-sync goroutine takes
the ConfigManager gitMutex (WithGitLock) and hangs in a go-git call
(go-git has no network timeout); next %60 cycle the loop's
SaveConfig(wait=true) queues behind the wedged worker and freezes every
state producer BEFORE the GWARN013 guard can fire. Observed on
dbaas-fr-2 five minutes after a fresh boot (last log 10:41:59), empty
state machine, no OPENED/RESOLV lines.

- main loop periodic SaveConfig no longer waits on the manager queue
- CloneConfigFromGit and PushConfigToGit use PlainCloneContext /
  PullContext / PushContext with a 120s gitNetworkTimeout, so a hung
  remote turns into a logged error surfaced by the GWARN002/003 git
  health states instead of a permanent mutex hold

feat: monitor loop ticker exposed and watched by the GUI

A frozen main loop cannot report itself through states — only an
external observer can catch it. The loop now publishes its tick
counter (loopTick in /api/monitor) and the navbar shows a live
'Tick N' pill (global view) that turns into a red blinking

fix: RepMan init race left global state machine nil — no state ever published

Three files' init() guarded RepMan creation with bare
'if RepMan == nil { RepMan = new(ReplicationManager) }'. Go runs file
inits in file-name order, so server_decrypt.go's minimal init won and
server_monitor.go's full block was skipped: MessageChan stayed nil
(send would block forever) and InitAlertStateMachine never ran. Every
repman.SetState was a silent no-op — GWARN/GERR/GINF states never
existed in monitor mode: empty /api/global/alerts, zero OPENED/RESOLV
log lines, Monitor button permanently 0/0, regardless of split brain,
registration or supervision producers running.

Single ensureRepMan() constructor now builds the singleton with all
runtime dependencies; all three inits call it.

fix: preserve slow-cadence global states across lifecycle ticks

The lifecycle clears the global state machine every tick but the
connectivity probes (GWARN004/005/012) only re-assert every %60 ticks,
so once the state machine actually publishes (post init-race fix) they
flapped open/resolved 59 of 60 ticks. Preserve them on skipped ticks —
same pattern as ERR00022 for the throttled arbitrator probe. GWARN013
busy-overrun states are likewise preserved while their task's busy
flag is still set, resolving naturally when the task completes.

fix: raise heartbeat supervision stall threshold to stop GWARN001 flapping

The supervision counts repman loop ticks (2s) with an unchanged
cluster heartbeat; threshold 5 meant 10s — but a busy cluster tick
legitimately takes 10s+ (slow DB connection attempts during a peer
outage), so GWARN001 flapped STALLED/RESUME on every cluster tick
(40 open/close in 4.5min observed on fr-2). A truly stalled cluster
loop stays stalled for minutes: default is now 30 ticks (~60s),
critical at 3x (~3min); still tunable via
monitor-global-heartbeat-stall-threshold.

- WARN0180: node never reported a deployed config — dbjobs never ran
  or config was never applied (diagnose with WARN0170 gates and

- WARN0179: deployed config exists but differs — dbjobs has not

States carry server names only — the full variable diff (potentially

doc: config event log design — peer-symmetric config change replication

Approved design for event-changed.<RRBid>.log: per-instance append-only
log of locally-born config mutations in the shared config git repo,
per-peer cursors persisted with the save and advanced on the SaveConfig
cycle (apply the diff between two saves). Echo suppression, hash_
ciphertext for secrets, timestamp LWW conflicts, rotation with
full-pull fallback, log-everything / apply-allowlist scoping.
Solves mutations stranded on the standby peer (belair external user
case). Doc only — no code.

doc: config event log — drop apply-allowlist, peers re-apply every event

Every logged event is a dynamic cluster-scope setting peers must
converge on (server-scope flags never enter the log); LWW resolves
concurrent writes. Doc only.

doc: config event log — server-scope settings also logged and re-applied

Runtime changes to immutable scope:server settings are lost on restart
anyway, so replaying them on a peer carries no extra risk and peers
converging on the same runtime value is the desired behaviour. Doc only.

doc: config event log — save-diff authoring with provenance subtraction

Events derived from the SaveConfig cycle, not setter hooks (rejected:
call-site churn, future setters could forget to log): replay peer
events first recording provenance, key-diff the new toml against the
previous save, subtract keys whose value came from a replay, append
the rest as own events. Cursors + provenance persist with the save.
Ping-pong impossible by construction: applied events are subtracted
from the diff, cursors are forward-only, per-key LWW with author-id
tie-break gives all peers the same winner. Trade-offs recorded
(save-coarse timestamps, no transient audit, thin attribution). Doc
only.

feat: config event log — peer-symmetric config change replication

Implements doc/implementation/config/CONFIG_EVENT_LOG.md.

Authoring (save-diff, no setter hooks): SaveConfigFile,
SaveImmutableConfig and Overwrite() now build content in memory, write
crash-safe (<file>.new + rename — a kill mid-save can no longer leave
a truncated toml) and key-diff against the previous save. Locally-born
changes append to event-changed.<RRBid>.log (RRBid =
arbitration-external-unique-id); values just replayed from a peer are
subtracted via the provenance table, making ping-pong structurally
impossible. Secrets travel as hash_ ciphertext only. First save is a
baseline and emits nothing. Identical content no longer rewrites the
file (real change detection replaces the md5-at-wrong-offset check).

Transport: config.FetchRemoteRootFiles — bounded fetch + blob read
from the remote-tracking ref; the working tree is never merged into.

Replay (server_eventlog.go): fetch peer logs on the detached git-sync
cycle before the push, apply events past per-log cursors in (ts,
author) order under per-key LWW with author-id tie-break, seed peer
ciphertext into the Secret cache so both peers' saved configs converge
byte-identical, persist cursors+provenance in event-log-state.json
(gitignored, atomic). Unknown-setter keys apply through the same
viper/mapstructure path the config loader uses. A rotated (shrunk)
peer log replays from the start — LWW skips stale events.

(one-directional active→standby sync stranded standby-born mutations,

Third recurrence of the per-cluster header appearing on the cluster

fix: event log transport + phantom event sources

Three issues surfaced by the first live event log run:

- PushConfigToGit never staged event-changed.<id>.log (explicit
  whitelist of <cluster>/*.toml + agents.json + default.toml), so
  events were authored but never committed or pushed — peers fetched a
  remote with no logs. The event log now travels with the config push.
- SaveUserRoles built the role list from map iteration: random order
  made the ACL string flap ('sysops dbops' <-> 'dbops sysops') and emit
  phantom acl-allow-external events on every save. Roles are sorted.
- SetAgentsCpuCoreMem removed: it min()'d agent capacity into
  ImmuableFlagMap — write-only (no reader anywhere, incl. dbaas-portal),
  absent at boot (empty agent list -> unset event) and 0 when agents
  had not reported capacity (set '0' event). Per-agent capacity already
  reaches the BO through agents.json, which the push stages; free-
  capacity publication, if wanted, will be a proper computed field
  there.

fix: event log compares secrets by decrypted value, not ciphertext

Encryption uses a random IV: the same secret re-encrypted (e.g. after
a restart when the ciphertext cache did not seed) produces different
bytes — not a config change, must not emit an event. The save diff now
decrypts both sides for secret keys and skips equal plaintexts, making
the event log immune to ciphertext instability regardless of cause.

Adds boot-seed reproduction tests (config_secret_seed_test.go): the
DecryptSecretsFromConfig -> GetStableEncryptedValue cycle is proven
stable across simulated restarts when the raw hash_ value is present
in the flag maps — so the every-boot re-encryption observed live means
the maps lack the raw values at seed time (boot wiring, under
investigation); the git-churn side of that remains to fix.

fix: instance-local secrets never replicate; config saves gated on init

- Instance-local keys (git-acces-token, vault-role-id/secret-id,
  api-oauth-client-id/secret) are excluded from the config event log:
  never authored, never applied. Each instance derives its own GitLab
  PAT from its own OAuth session (rotated at boot and daily) — a peer
  replaying it would clobber the local credential, and both peers
  rotating the same named PAT would invalidate each other.
- Cluster.Save() refuses to run until InitFromConf completes
  (initConfigDone flag): config saves go through an async queue, and a
  save executing mid-init captured a half-loaded config (missing
  external users, restic paths, ACLs) — emitting transient unset/set
  event pairs (seen on mixr-dev, two saves 100ms apart) that then
  replayed on peers.
doc: config event log — instance-local keys and authoring hygiene

fix: dynamically-created clusters load their saved config at boot

GetClusterConfig gated the saved-<cluster> section load on the STATIC
cluster section existing (cf2 != nil). Clusters created dynamically
(API, marketplace) have no static section — they exist only through
saved-<name>.toml — so every restart discarded their entire persisted
config: api-credentials-external regenerated (AddCloud18GitUser saw no
sysops user and rolled a fresh random password each boot — the
per-boot mixr-dev events), backup-restic-local-repository and ACLs
rebuilt from defaults. Discovery already knew these clusters (it
strips the saved- prefix); only the loader refused their section.
The block only uses cf3 (own nil-check) and the immutable map, so
dropping the cf2 condition is safe for static clusters.

fix: per-instance GitLab PAT name — peers no longer invalidate each other

Both peers authenticate as the same GitLab account and built the same
PAT name (domain-subdomain-zone), and GetGitLabTokenOAuth rotates the
token by name: every boot (and daily ticker) of either instance minted
a new token under the shared name, invalidating the other instance's
copy — its git fetch/push then failed 401 until its own next restart.
Pre-existing bug; the event log's every-cycle fetch made it visible in
minutes (DR could not fetch peer events after main's restarts).

Token name now carries the instance unique id
(GetInstancePATName: <domain>-<subdomain>-<zone>-<RRBid>) in all three
sites (InitGitConfig, daily rotation ticker, SSO login flow). Each
instance owns and rotates its own PAT; the shared-name token falls out
of use.

fix: stage event log in the push implementation actually used

There are two push implementations: repman.PushConfigToGit (legacy,
stages event logs since 4f213c12b, also writes the gitignore lines)
and config.PushConfigToGit used by the ConfigManager queue — the one
every periodic push goes through, staging only <cluster>/*.toml,
agents.json and queryrules.json. The event log staging went into the
wrong one, so event-changed.<id>.log was authored, committed nowhere,
and never reached the remote (diagnosed live: pushes green, file
absent from HEAD, gitignore missing the legacy path's lines proving
that path never runs). Both implementations now stage the logs.

fix: stage event log in the ConfigManager push worker — the real live path

Third push implementation found the hard way: the ConfigManager's own
commit worker (config/manager/manager.go, GitAddTask queue) is what
every periodic push actually runs — proven live by its distinct error
format in the logs and by the instance .gitignore lacking every line
the legacy paths write. The two previous staging fixes (repman and
config package PushConfigToGit) patched dormant code. The worker now
queues event-changed.<id>.log like default.toml.

Push 'object not found' failures observed alongside are the shallow
clone racing the peer's pushes; the worker's existing
classifyRecoverablePushError -> RefreshGitMetadata -> retry already
covers that.

fix: rebase-on-remote before commit in the live push worker

Fetch (bounded 120s) and mixed-reset the local branch onto the
remote-tracking head before staging: working files are kept (local
content wins), only the branch pointer and index move, so every push
is a fast-forward built from objects we hold. Kills the shallow
two-writer race for good: previously the worker committed on top of a
stale graft, the push died with 'object not found' once the peer had
advanced the remote, and the refresh-restage retry (~2min at ~1s per
go-git Add across ~80 files) reliably lost the next race too —
trapping local commits, including the config event log, forever.
