fix: checksum repair DELETE fails on MariaDB < 11.6 (alias syntax)

RepairTableChecksum emitted 'DELETE FROM db.tbl A WHERE <A.-qualified
chunk condition>' — single-table DELETE with a table alias, which
MariaDB only accepts since 11.6.1 (MDEV-33988) and refused to backport
to any LTS line (MDEV-37227 Won't Fix). Checksum repair was therefore
broken with error 1064 on 10.5/10.6/10.11/11.4. The alias cannot be
dropped (the stored chunkRangeCondition references A.), so use the
multi-table form 'DELETE A FROM db.tbl A WHERE ...' which every MySQL
and MariaDB version accepts.

fix(arbitration): restore peace-time election semantics and true heartbeat upsert

Two regressions from late June made peer pairs flap active/passive
(ERR00022 open/resolve every ~2min with 'Arbitrator says: winner'):

1. The election reset was inverted on 2026-06-30 from the original
   2017 semantics. Restored: count(distinct master)==1 — every fresh
   heartbeat reports the identical master, no split brain — clears the
   election, because in peace time the arbitrator must not impose an
   authority: who is active is decided by the peer protocol (an
   instance seeing its peer active with the same master sets itself
   passive, an authority already exists). The Elected flag only takes
   over when the peers disagree on the master (two different masters
   after a partition, or one side seeing none), and is then preserved
   so the first winner holds for the whole partition. The inversion
   made the arbitrator keep a persistent winner in peace time,
   fighting the peer protocol.

2. WriteHeartbeat used REPLACE / INSERT OR REPLACE, which deletes and
   reinserts the row — status falls back to its default 'U', so the
   winner wiped its own Elected flag on its own next heartbeat.
   Restored the original 2016 MySQL semantics (ON DUPLICATE KEY
   UPDATE; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on SQLite): the heartbeat reports
   uuid/master/date/hosts/failed and never touches status.

Also updates TestRequestArbitration_Winner_MySQL_SQL to the SQL shape
introduced by the 2026-06-30 stale-row filter (failing since then).

Arbitrator-side only: rebuild (make arb) and redeploy the arbitrator
service; no repman client changes.

feat(arbitrator): /version endpoint

Reports the running build ({version, fullVersion} JSON). Election
semantics changed across builds and an unversioned arbitrator made it
impossible to verify what was deployed. Exempted from the URI check
like the other observability endpoints.

fix(client): consult the arbitrator only when the master has failed

The /arbitrator endpoint runs an election. The client probed it in
peace time — every tick on active clusters through the false-positive
check chain, plus a periodic ERR00022 status probe — so the arbitrator
minted a transient Elected row on every check; the peer probing
seconds later read it, answered looser, and every cluster flapped
active/passive (ERR00022 blockers) at probe frequency.

The check chain now evaluates ActiveArbitration lazily: pass without
probing while the master is healthy, ask the arbitrator only when
isMasterFailed() and a failover is actually being evaluated — the one
moment the answer is decisive. The peace-time status probe block is
removed; a lingering ERR00022 resolves naturally once no longer
re-asserted, and the split-brain election path (cluster_split) is
unchanged.

Client-side fix on purpose: upgraded repman instances must behave on
OLD arbitrators, which keep the probe-elects behavior forever.

fix(arbitrator): status probes no longer run elections — read-mostly /arbitrator

Companion to 859989b5e (client stops idle probing): protects fleets of
OLD repman clients, which probe /arbitrator in peace time forever.
Decision order in handlerArbitrator:
1. A fresh Elected row exists: answer winner/looser by uid, no write.
2. No Elected row and no fresh heartbeat disagrees with the caller's
   master: peace — every asker is a winner (the arbitrator imposes no
   authority; the peer protocol decides who is active), no write.
3. Masters diverge: real split brain — run the election; the flag
   sticks for the whole partition (heartbeats no longer wipe it) and
   dissolves when agreement returns.

New read-only helpers GetFreshElected and IsMasterAgreed in dbhelper.
Takes effect on arbitrator redeploy; no client changes required.

feat: chaos isolation — per-cluster split-brain simulation + regtest

Simulates, for one cluster on this instance only, the scenario
arbitration protects against: the monitor loses the data plane (every
database connection fails at GetNewDBConn, driving servers to failed
exactly like a real cut) and peer visibility (IsSplitBrain forced in
ArbitratorHandler, engaging the existing election machinery) while the
arbitrator stays reachable.

- Runtime state only, NEVER a config key: config would replicate to
  the peer through the config event log and isolate both sides.
- API: /api/clusters/{name}/actions/chaos-isolate-start
  (?duration=seconds, 120s default, 15min max) and chaos-isolate-stop;
  requires the cluster-test grant. Always auto-restores; WARN0181
  warns every tick while armed with the remaining seconds.

Regtest testChaosIsolationArbitration, three phases (failover mode
forced auto and restored — phases 1-2 alone would pass in manual mode
too and prove nothing):
1. Armed: the isolated side must lose the election, go standby, and
   the failover counter must NOT move.
2. Lifted: split brain resolves, same master, still no failover.
3. The hard part: a REAL master stop under active arbitration must
   still fail over automatically (protection must never block the

Skips as passed when arbitration is not configured.

Failover model (restore 3.0): removed the two !IsActive() gates
(MasterFailover, top of CheckFailed). Failover is gated only by the
arbitrator's per-failover winner check (isActiveArbitration in the
false-positive chain), never by the continuous-election status — which
cannot reliably latch and was deadlocking a healthy standby node out
of a legitimate failover. Status is retained for config sync and the
scheduler but no longer gates failover.

Chaos tool (cluster_chaos.go) reworked to sever links independently so
real split-brain scenarios compose:
- arbitrator (per-cluster): arbitratorElection + isActiveArbitration
  fail -> node cannot confirm authority, fail-safes to standby.
- peer (server-level): /api/heartbeat goes dark AND our
  HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain treats the peer as unreachable.
- db (per-cluster, optional): database connections fail.
Chaos always cuts arbitrator+peer (the constant across both
co-located-master scenarios); db only on ?cut=db (master stays
reachable by default). Split brain is no longer forced — it emerges
from the cuts so the real detection path is exercised. WARN0181 shows
the active cuts every tick; always auto-restores.

Regtest testChaosIsolationArbitration updated: cut the arbitrator link,
assert the isolated node fail-safes to standby without failing over,
recovers on restore, and a real master kill still auto-fails-over with

feat(chaos): independent link cuts + P1/P2 partitions + doc

Each chaos cut (arbitrator, peer, db) is now independently selectable
(?cut=, default arbitrator,peer) so the scenarios compose — including
db-only on the peer to blind it to a master that lives in the other DC.

Regtest testChaosIsolationArbitration now runs the two partitions of an
isolated active node explicitly, each asserting fail-safe (standby, no
failover) + recovery:
- P1 master OK  (cut=arbitrator,peer): live master, can't confirm
  authority -> must step down, not stay a second master.
- P2 master FAILED (cut=arbitrator,peer,db): wants to fail over but

Same rule both times: lost arbitrator => fail-safe, never act alone.

test(arbitration): minority node must not act — split brain + lost arbitration

Rewrites testChaosIsolationArbitration to the correct model: a
split-brained repman is the minority node (its infra lost BOTH peer
and arbitrator, 1 of 3), so the master it sees is not authoritative —
the majority (peer + arbitrator) holds the truth. A minority node must
do nothing: never flip active/passive, never fail over.

Sets up the virtual split brain at both levels at once — server: peer
check failed (IsSplitBrain); cluster: cannot join the arbitrator
(arbitrator link cut) — and asserts status and failover counter never
move, in two cases (local master ok / failed). The earlier assertion
('goes standby') was wrong: a minority node holds its status, it does

fix(chaos): arbitrator cut also stops the arbitrator report

A minority node (arbitrator link cut) must stop refreshing its
arbitrator heartbeat row, not just skip the election — otherwise its
row stays fresh and the majority never wins. SetArbitratorReport now
bails on the arbitrator cut too, so the minority's row goes stale
(~10s) and the majority wins the next per-tick election, exactly as a
real isolated node behaves (it can reach neither the peer nor the
arbitrator, so it reports to neither).

test: rename to testSetMinority with two virtual scenarios

testSetMinority puts a repman into the minority condition (peer +

Two virtual scenarios by master location, exercising different branches

- setMinorityLostMaster: master on the majority side (unreachable) —

Same assertion (status held, no failover), two distinct code paths.
Fencing the minority's live master read-only is a stronger follow-up

A real peer network loss is a timeout, not a fast 503. The peer cut now

(HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain waits MonitoringTicker*4s; the handler sleeps

Restore the outbound timeout in HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain: an isolated

fix(splitbrain): force server split-brain when heartbeat failure simulated

The inbound-only heartbeat cut made the split brain invisible on the node
where it was armed: SimulateHeartbeatFailure only darkens this node's inbound
/api/heartbeat, so its own outbound heartbeat still succeeded and
HeartbeatPeerSplitBrain returned false — repman.SplitBrain never flipped and
nothing propagated to the clusters. Only the peer could detect it, and only if
a remote call landed.

Now, when IsHeartbeatFailureSimulated() is armed, Heartbeat() forces
repman.SplitBrain = true directly (a real cable cut means THIS node cannot
reach its peer). The existing block then fires GWARN006 and pushes IsSplitBrain
down to every cluster — the first observable step — with no peer dependency.
On expiry/restore the next tick recomputes via the real peer heartbeat and
clears it. This also lets the minority tests detect the split locally.

cluster (e.g. belair) without touching others.

fix(arbitration): bound isActiveArbitration HTTP call with a timeout

isActiveArbitration used a bare http.Client{} with no deadline, so a cut
arbitrator link (real split brain or the split-brain simulator's blackhole)
would hang the monitor tick — and shutdown — indefinitely instead of failing
fast. Bound it with ArbitrationReadTimout (default 800ms), matching the intent
already present in SetArbitratorReport (context deadline) and arbitratorElection
(client Timeout). This is also required for split-brain detection to work: the
probe must FAIL on a severed link, not block.

fix(acl): grant cluster-test access to split-brain-simulator endpoints

The simulator routes are /api/clusters/{c}/test/split-brain-simulator/... but
the only test ACL rule was "/tests/" (plural). matchACLRules uses
strings.Contains, so "/tests/" never matches the singular "/test/..." path —
every simulator call (including the remote op3/op4 in testSetMinorityWithMaster,
which POST to these endpoints on the peer) returned 403 "No valid ACL", silently
reducing the 4-op minority orchestration to only the 2 local ops.

Add a rule mapping "/test/split-brain-simulator/" to GrantClusterTest so the
simulate-*-failure and restore endpoints are reachable by cluster-test users.

fix(arbitration): minority fail-safe — set master read-only + yield to standby

When a node is in split brain but cannot reach the arbitrator to confirm
authority, it is (or must assume it is) the minority. Previously arbitratorElection
just returned on arbitrator loss, so a node that was Active with a writable master
FROZE Active and kept accepting writes — risking dual-active and, worse, writes on
the minority master that diverge and block its rejoin once the partition heals.

The 2020 fail-safe (SetReadWrite blocked while IsFailedArbitrator, still present)
only refuses to *enable* writes; it does not demote an already-writable master.

Add arbitratorMinorityFailSafe(), called from both arbitrator-unreachable paths
(simulated cut and real HTTP error):
  1. force the master READ-ONLY so it rejoins the majority's newly-elected master
     as a slave (no divergence), and
  2. yield status to standby so this repman stops driving the cluster.
Idempotent per tick. This is the behavior expected by design; git history confirms
the original fail-safe was read-only-based, never a status yield that was removed.

test(splitbrain): minority must fail-safe (yield to standby), not freeze

minorityDoesNothing asserted the minority's status stays UNCHANGED — but the
correct, data-safe behavior is that the minority yields: drops to standby and
sets its master read-only so it can rejoin the majority. The old assertion would
flag the correct fix as a "FLIPPED" failure.

Rewrite the assertion: for the whole window require no failover (FailoverCtr
unchanged), and require the node to reach standby (yield). Log the master's
read-only state. "does nothing" was really "does nothing destructive" — it must
still fail safe.

fix(splitbrain-sim): master/db cut must fail the Ping health check, not just new conns

simulate-master-failure / simulate-database-failure only hooked GetNewDBConn, but
that is NOT the path that detects a down server: ServerMonitor.Ping() only calls
GetNewDBConn when CheckType == "tcp", and monitoring otherwise reuses the existing
pooled connection. So the simulated master kept pinging fine, was never marked
failed, and the majority never detected a master loss or promoted — "still see the
master as master."

Inject the simulated failure directly in Ping(), after the CheckType switch, so the
server is driven down through the real detection path (FailCount -> stateFailed ->
failover) regardless of CheckType or connection reuse. Covers both the whole-cluster
db cut and the master-only cut.

fix(splitbrain-sim): also fail Refresh() ping so a cut master stays down

Hooking Ping() alone wasn't enough: the health is delegated to the Go driver's
pooled connection, and Refresh() (server.Conn.Ping()) auto-reconnects and keeps
succeeding, flapping the master Suspect->Master so it never reaches MaxFail and
never triggers failover. Gate Refresh()'s ping with the same simulation check so
the cut server stays consistently down and failover fires.

Simulation-only (fires solely when IsMasterFailureSimulated / IsDatabaseFailureSimulated
is armed) — no effect on normal operation. NOTE for after release: the deeper
question is why Refresh() runs at all after Ping() has already failed for a server
in the same tick — that flap could mask real half-broken-master failures too.

fix(splitbrain-sim): simulated master death must defeat false-positive guards

A simulated master failure only cuts repman's view — db->db replication stays
live — so the false-positive guards (isOneSlaveHeartbeatIncreasing sees the slave
still replicating; isExternalOk may still reach the DB) concluded "master not
really dead" and vetoed failover on every tick. FailCount climbed past MaxFail
(observed 21/5) but MasterFailover never fired.

Short-circuit both guards to the "dead" answer when IsMasterFailureSimulated /
IsDatabaseFailureSimulated is armed, so a simulated death is treated as real and
failover triggers at MaxFail (5/5) as expected. Simulation-only; no effect on
real operation.

fix(splitbrain-sim): stop the topology-role heal from resetting a simulated-dead master

The real reason a simulated master death never triggered failover: the ping/refresh
error was fine, but srv.go's active-passive state reconciliation re-marks the master
stateMaster purely from its topology role (PrevState==Suspect + "it's the master"),
ignoring the connection. That heal reset FailCount every tick, so it flapped
Suspect<->Master and never held Failed long enough for CheckFailed to promote.

Skip that re-heal while IsMasterFailureSimulated is armed for this server, so the
death sticks -> FailCount reaches MaxFail -> failover fires. Sim-gated only.

NOTE after release: this same heal ignores the connection for REAL deaths too — worth
verifying against the failover regtest whether it can mask a real active-passive
master failure.

fix(splitbrain-sim): guard the real reheal path (SetMaster) for master-slave

a0f8da31a guarded the ActivePassive branch (srv.go:789), but belair is master-slave,
so that branch never runs — the reheal actually goes through SetMaster() (srv_set.go),
which topology discovery calls every tick to re-designate db1 as master, re-marking it
stateMaster and resetting FailCount -> the flap, no failover.

Revert the wrong-branch guard and instead guard SetMaster(): while a server's failure is
simulated, don't re-mark it stateMaster, so the death sticks -> FailCount holds at MaxFail
-> failover fires. Sim-gated only.

majority told looser every tick, no promotion during a master failure,
then per-cluster dual-standby latched at heal (elections stop when split
clears; the both-Standby recovery trigger compares SERVER-level status so
per-cluster dual-standby is invisible to it).

Path A used to get 'winner' from the agreement branch without electing.

feat(arbitration): authority lease + contest window — fix the coordination root cause

The dual-active relapses observed live today (a standby self-promoting off
a single lost peer poll, twice) are a COORDINATION flaw, not a client bug:
the arbitrator had no memory of who holds authority. Elected rows went
stale 10s after a split ended, so the next asker — whoever, whenever — won
a fresh election against nobody. Blips merely walked through that open
door. Per Stephane: fix the coordination, do not hide the blip.

The Elected row becomes a persistent LEASE, enforced by the arbitrator:

- Lease maintenance (handlerHeartbeat): an instance reporting status
  Active CLAIMS its lease; reporting Standby RELEASES it. Fed by new
  event-driven transition reports from repman (server.go): every
  server-level transition (Active<->Standby, split enter/leave, boot)
  posts one report per arbitrated cluster — steady peacetime stays
  completely silent. Old clients omit status: nothing changes for them.
- decideArbitration (handlerArbitrator): I hold the lease -> winner;
  another holds it FRESH -> looser (base-cut: incumbent keeps driving);
  another holds it STALE -> the challenger must persist through a 10s
  CONTEST WINDOW before the election runs and the lease transfers
  (in-memory contest map, single-instance arbitrator, no protocol or
  schema change). A blip heals long before the window closes; split brain
  stays fully visible (WARN0079) but can no longer steal authority.
- dbhelper: ClaimElected / ReleaseElected / GetElectedAny /
  DemoteOtherElected + lease lifecycle test.
- cluster/prx.go: authority gate — only the Active repman injects the
  heartbeat/traffic DDL into the master (a yielded minority stays silent:
  this was the self-inflicted divergent DDL tail at every rejoin).
- The client-side blip mitigations prototyped earlier today (peace-time
  presence, DB-marker liveness, standby silence gate) are all REMOVED —
  coordination lives at the coordinator.

Scenario matrix: blip -> contest absorbs it, incumbent undisturbed;
base cut -> fresh holder wins, first-winner-holds; corner cut -> silent
holder loses after one window, majority fails over (+10s, acceptable);
manual relocate -> yield releases, takeover claims: lease follows.

fix(arbitration): restore the 2.x/3.0 anti-blip grace at split-brain entry

heals inside the grace, so no election traffic is ever generated for it —
including against pre-lease arbitrators (mixed-version safety).

feat(inject): default traffic/pseudo-GTID marker to flashback-able DML, keep DDL opt-in

The pseudo_gtid_v traffic marker was a CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW — DDL, which
flashback can never reverse. On a live minority test the old master's whole
divergent tail was 13 of these self-inflicted heartbeat DDLs, making an
otherwise-recoverable divergence reseed-only. repman's own monitoring could
thus poison a client's recoverability before any client transaction.

New inject-traffic-mode (default 'dml'): a single-row REPLACE INTO

reverse; pseudo_gtid_v becomes a view over that row so GetLastPseudoGTID is

the reseed path and for non-GTID positional rejoin (whose binlog search
greps the UUID as plain text — a row image is not greppable). Both markers
stay available; the default can no longer break clients.

feat(arbitration): true minority-master freeze via held FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK (opt-in)

read_only does not bind repman's own SUPER connection, and MariaDB has no
super_read_only (confirmed live: db1 read_only=ON still committed 13 DDLs).
FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK is the only server-side lock that blocks even
SUPER — so it is the only way to truly stop a minority/old master from
diverging during a split.

- ServerMonitor.FreezeWithReadLock: opens a DEDICATED single-session conn
  (SetMaxOpenConns(1)) and holds FTWRL on it. The lock lives exactly as
  long as that conn stays open, so a repman crash releases it — a client
  master can never be left frozen forever. UnfreezeReadLock closes it;
  IsFrozen reports state. Idempotent.
- Wired into arbitratorMinorityFailSafe (gated on new opt-in flag
  arbitration-minority-freeze, default false), released when the split
  resolves (ArbitratorHandler) and defensively at rejoin start (recovery
  must write). Pairs with the authority gate: the gate stops repman's own
  writes, the freeze blocks everyone else's.

Off by default — it is a global write freeze, opt-in per deployment.

fix(inject): dml marker table created once via the proxy — no state machine

The dml traffic marker broke replication because I created the marker table
OUT-OF-BAND (directly and empty on each node): the master's in-place REPLACE

1032 HA_ERR_KEY_NOT_FOUND.

The fix is simply to create the table the SAME way the marker is written —
via the PROXY, once, when traffic starts. That CREATE lands on the master,
is binlogged, and flows to every slave in the SAME binlog stream BEFORE any
REPLACE that follows it. Binlog ordering guarantees a slave applies the
CREATE before the REPLACE (no 1032), and a reseeded node gets the table in
its snapshot. So there is NOTHING to check — no CanInjectTraffic state, no
per-node presence probe, no DictTables/SHOW CREATE lookup, no new-node
tracking. One idempotent create-once guard (injectTrafficTableReady).

fix(arbitration): fire per-cluster reports concurrently every split-tick (keep leases in sync)

on different sides of the split (belair/crm/curepipe on DR, flacq stuck on the
main) because their arbitrator leases were refreshed on staggered per-cluster
ticks: a lagging cluster's lease passed the freshness timeout, the arbitrator
dropped it, and its next election won against nobody → self-promote → split
ownership / dual-active summary / colliding git pushes.

  split brain is set (not only on transition), fired concurrently per cluster,
  so all leases stay fresh IN SYNC and none starves.
- SetArbitratorReport reads its topology inputs (hosts/failed/master/status)
  under the cluster lock before the network POST — cluster.Servers is
  reassigned (make/append/delete) under that same lock during TopologyDiscover,
  so firing the report concurrently from the server loop without it could tear
  the slice and panic. Lock held only for the quick reads; POST runs unlocked.

per-repman lease (drop cluster from the arbitrator heartbeat primary key) so
there is nothing per-cluster to starve — arbitrator-side, tracked separately.

topology: re-designate stale master after a minority sat out split-brain

that sat out a split-brain as the minority froze its last-known master pointer.
When it goes Active/calm again it lands in the extra-master branch (Case A) whose

the old master even though that node is now a slave of the real (majority-elected)
master. Symptom: node shows db1=Master while db1 is actually a wedged slave of db2,
ERR00063 open every tick, proxies never follow.

Fix: in the master-slave extra-master case, if our own cluster.master pointer is
itself a slave now (IsSlave), it is stale — re-designate to the real master
(the non-slave others follow) rather than treating the live master as an extra to
demote (which would enslave it). Guarded to TopoMasterSlave and IsActive only, so
the minority never re-designates from an untrusted view and multi-master is
untouched. Repair of the stale old master (standalone->slave) is a separate step.

At freeze time the minority should demote its master's OWN slaves too, so the
whole minority branch is fenced for the split and resolve-time recovery only
re-points them onto the winner. Add fenceMinoritySubtreeSlaves for that, but
leave the caller in arbitratorMinorityFailSafe COMMENTED OUT: it must be
DC/side-scoped first. Under the app-level split simulation every DB stays
reachable, so cl.slaves also contains the majority's promotable slave (master+
Slave1 in DC1 minority, Slave2 in DC2), and a plain loop would demote the very
node the majority is about to promote. Parked until the simple lone-old-master
case is validated and per-server DC membership drives the scope.

arbitration: minority fetches real master from peer on split-resolve (cluster-scoped)

After a split resolves, the formerly-minority node was stuck holding a stale
cluster.master (its frozen old master, now a slave of the majority-elected one)
because the extra-master reconcile was dead and the arbitrator's winner-master
was unreliable to it. Fix: in the IsActive() master-slave extra-master branch,
fetch the REAL master from the arbitration PEER (the winner) via its crash
(ElectedMasterURL) and re-designate to it, then existing RejoinFixRelay walks the
slaves on. Local heuristic (our pointer is now a slave -> the local non-slave is
master) is the fallback when there is no peer / it is unreachable.

fetchMasterFromPeer is CLUSTER-scoped and self-contained: it uses this cluster's
own ArbitrationPeerHosts + cluster-test credential, never the server layer, so a
single-repman / no-auto-failover cluster has no peer, gets "" back, and relies on
its own local crash — nothing to depend on that doesn't exist. Guarded to
TopoMasterSlave + IsActive; multi-master untouched. Only the Active node runs
this, so exactly one node drives the rejoin (the loser, co-located with the old
master); the winner just serves its crash.

arbitration: peer-login must prefer admin, not a random cluster-test-grant user

getClusterTestCredentials iterated cl.APIUsers (a Go map = random order) and
returned whichever grant-holder came first. On belair TWO users hold the
cluster-test grant: admin (stable) and sysops-cloud18 (the git-sync service
account, which locks out after failed auth). So each peer login was a coin flip:
land on admin -> works -> peer cuts arm / peer-fetch succeeds; land on
sysops-cloud18 -> 401 -> master-cut never arms / peer-fetch fails. That is the
intermittent 'worked before, not now' 401 that made every minority test flaky and
would have flapped the new peer-fetch too.

Prefer admin deterministically (fall back to any other grant-holder only if admin
lacks the grant). Fixed in both copies: server getClusterTestCredentials (test
peer cuts) and the cluster-level one added for fetchMasterFromPeer.

arbitration: peer-fetch pulls the peer's DURABLE failoverHistory crash + materializes it

fetchMasterFromPeer queried the peer's LIVE crash list (/topology/crashes), which
the retention purges once the peer thinks the DBs are up — exactly when a
record-less minority needs it — so it returned null and node1 got no crash. Read
the peer's cluster JSON failoverHistory instead (StoreLastN, durable, keeps the
anchors), take the last entry, and MATERIALIZE it into cl.Crashes (dropping the
peer-local delta paths) so getCrashFromJoiner returns it and the old master's
rejoin has FailoverIOGtid/positions.

Guard it with SplitBrainStartTs: stamp the calm->split edge (ArbitratorHandler)
and reject a last-crash whose UnixTimestamp predates this split brain, so a stale

-> caller falls back to local.

When a master-slave node loses the arbitrator (IsFailedArbitrator = the isolated
minority under the always-up arbitrator design), TopologyDiscover fell through the
extra-master branch and did nothing — freezing its pre-split view with the old
master still cluster.master. That old master stayed the proxy target and, at
resolve, the rejoin re-slaved it off its own diverged GTID (collision, no delta).

Add the missing minority else: fence the old master read-only (opt-in FTWRL
freeze), SetState(stateUnconn) (standalone) and cluster.master = nil — via the
loop's own server handle (sv), re-applied every discover tick, so nil-ing
cluster.master never loses the fencing handle. Position PRESERVED (no RESET
MASTER); the rejoin turns it into a slave later.

Guarded by Conf.Arbitration + TopoMasterSlave (multi-master/ring/wsrep/grouprep
untouched) + IsFailedArbitrator (majority never affected).

arbitration: resurrect the 3.0 topology dual-master rejoin, guarded by the election verdict; drop the latch

restart') because topology could not tell a split-brain LOSER from a server

discriminator: rejoin the extra master only when the materialized crash says

(5f7f2fea5) is removed — it treated standby as transient, but DR is standby

never rejoin — the arbitration verdict makes the Active winner the sole
owner of recovery. rejoinFromElection stays for the no-master case at
resolve on the former minority.

only ever touches servers that were part of an election — new nodes match no

while the real loser's capture never ran (empty Last Divergence in the GUI).

crash: disk-truth crash history — one crash = one crash-bin dir, synchronized

The crash history and the on-disk archives had drifted (10 failover.json vs 3
crash-bin dirs): finishRejoin wrote an accumulating failover.<now>.json per
rejoin (same crash printed X times), while archives pruned to keep-3, so
LoadFailoverHistory read dead links after restart and the last crash's binlog
delta vanished.

Redesign (Stephane): the crash list IS the real crashes archived on disk.
- Crash.ArchiveDir: each crash's own crash-bin-<eventTs> dir.
- ensureCrashArchive: create the dir + write crash.json the MOMENT the crash is
  known (option B), prune to keep-N as a unit.
- Majority failover (cluster_fail.go, both paths) and minority peer-materialize
  (fetchMasterFromPeer) both call ensureCrashArchive -> local disk reflects the
  crash immediately, synchronized before any rejoin.
- saveBinlog fills the binlog INTO the crash's existing ArchiveDir (no new dir);
  finishRejoin stamps the result into the same crash.json. No more
  failover.<ts>.json, no append.
- LoadFailoverHistory scans crash-bin-* dirs (crash.json each) => history is a
  pure reflection of disk: deduped, restart-safe, delta always present, pruned
  with the archives.

Peer->local flow revisited for the new model: the minority writes its own
crash-bin dir on materialize, so both nodes hold their own synchronized record
of the same event.

The point of manual rejoin is to EXERCISE the same code auto-rejoin uses, so a client
can trust turning auto-rejoin on. Re-coding it was a double mistake: reinvention bugs +
it validates nothing about auto. Aligning rejoinWithMethod to the auto path:

- Remove the blanket trailing attachAsReadOnlySlave. It duplicated (and conflicted with)
  every self-attaching method — flashback does its own slave_pos CHANGE MASTER, my attach
  re-issued current_pos, and the naive attach dropped SSL/delay/channel/multi-source.
  Now attach runs ONLY on the failure branch, exactly like the auto path (its line 214).
- flashback/logical-dump/logical-backup/physical-backup: call the real auto functions,

- reset-master-reslave: = the server menu, ResetMaster + StartSlave (resumes the existing

- ignore-delta-force: RESET MASTER + SetReplicationGTIDSlavePosFromServer (full config) +

Auto-rejoin function bodies untouched; only RejoinScript (returns error, auto ignores) and

fix(rejoin): pin failed-over master to Failed at crash materialization

A minority-side failover left the old master stranded StandAlone with no auto-rejoin.
Root cause (proven from logs): the only auto-rejoin trigger is a Failed->up edge, but
the winning repman yields active (calm-yield) before that edge lands, and the new
active never witnessed the failure (its DB link to the master survived), so neither
auto path fires — DR log showed 'Rejoin ... not triggered (active=false)'.

Fix: when the active node fetches/materializes the peer's crash for the old master
(fetchMasterFromPeer — runs only on the active node), set that server to Failed. The
node that drives the rejoin is then guaranteed to hold the Failed->up edge; the server
is reachable so it recovers to StandAlone next tick with PrevState=Failed and the
existing RejoinMaster fires. Guarded !IsMaster so the elected new master is never demoted.

fix(rejoin): keep operator-armed crash out of the DBs-up purge

The manual rejoin API returned {"rejoin":"armed"} (ACL OK, crash queued with the
chosen method) but never executed: hasUnresolvedCrash only protected a crash whose
server was SlaveErr/Failed, so for a StandAlone old master the DBs-up purge
(cluster_topo.go) deleted the armed crash before ProcessArmedRejoins could run it.
Treat an armed crash (RejoinMethod set, RejoinResult empty) as unresolved so it
survives the purge and the queued rejoin actually runs.

shutdown-timing hunt surfaced):

  it did) — the final git push on SIGINT could stall the whole stop. Use
  r.PushContext with a 120s deadline.
- server_peer.go PeerRequest/RequestForwarder: client := &http.Client{} had no
  Timeout — an unreachable peer hangs the forward (and the O(N^2) peer poll).
  Add a 30s Timeout.

Restic exec/FUSE-unmount are also unbounded but NOT touched here: a blanket
timeout would kill legitimately long backups — that waits on the shutdown
instrumentation to confirm restic is the phase before choosing a safe bound.

The support-chat/meet integration talks to an (embedded, already-slow) Mattermost
with unbounded clients:

  server blocks the caller forever. Set HTTPClient.Timeout = 30s.
- the GitLab-SSO login client (&http.Client{Jar: jar}) had no Timeout. Add 30s.

chore(shutdown): fast-fail the final git push at 5s (safety net)

Git push time is always seconds in practice (tracked in the log), so this is not
the slow-stop cause — it's a guard: if gitlab is unreachable during a stop, the
unbounded PushContext(120s) would drag the shutdown. Bound the shutdown push to
5s and abandon on overrun (config is already synced by the dirty-gated push).

fix(shutdown): force/lazy restic unmount on stop — kills the 40-68s stall

UnmountRepo waits up to 5 MINUTES for CanUnmount() (all mount refs released) —
correct in normal operation, but on SHUTDOWN it holds the whole stop hostage to a
lingering mount reference. That wait (not git, not peers, not the worker) was the
observed 40s/68s graceful-stop (peers+marketplace disabled made it 68s, proving
it's the unmount).

Add ForceUnmountRepo: SIGTERM the mount process, lazy-unmount the path
(fusermount -uz / umount -l detaches a busy mount immediately, no user-wait),
short grace then SIGKILL, clear state. cluster.Stop() now calls it; the restic-job
callers keep the safe UnmountRepo with the 5-min wait.

fix(restic): plug the mount-ref leak on physical reseed early-returns

Root cause of the 'fast before, slow now' stop: the guarded ReleaseMountRef defer
was registered ONLY for non-physical reseeds, so the physical path's early-return
errors (ctx.Done, no candidates, no source paths, invalid/escaping path, snapshot
verification) returned WITHOUT releasing the mount ref. The leaked ref then made
UnmountRepo wait its full 5-minute CanUnmount() timeout for a phantom user — the
40-68s (up to 5min) graceful stop.

Register the defer for ALL methods. The physical success path already sets
refOwned=false when it hands the ref to the async cleanup
(registerResticReseedCleanup), so the defer skips it there; the refOwned guard
also prevents double-release with the existing manual releases. Logical was
already safe. Complements ForceUnmountRepo (which protects the stop regardless).

  same critical section (claim), then release the lock BEFORE the network call.
  First dispatch to reach a peer wins; overlapping dispatches see the fresh
  timestamp and skip -> exactly one call per peer per Interval, and a failed
  attempt is rate-limited like a success. The lock is never held during I/O, so a
  dark peer blocks only its own poll goroutine (all off the main server loop).

  maps BatchUpdateClusters mutates under the same lock.

fix(build): make log-plugin publishing single-owner + opt-in (fixes stale plugin store)

Log-plugins are distributed to servers from the signed-plugin store at runtime; the store had
gone stale (frozen at an old wire version) so current servers received no compatible plugins.

Root cause: publishing was an emergent side-effect. The Makefile 'plugins' target auto-published
whenever signer credentials were present, so several unrelated build variants published
independently — inconsistently, and racing each other's push to the store. A later attempt to
tame that set PLUGIN_PUSH=OFF on only the two PRO Dockerfiles, which silenced the images that
should define the release set while leaving osc/dev/slim to still auto-publish. Net: no build
reliably published the current wire version's set.

Fix — one owner, opt-in:
- Makefile 'plugins': reduce the publish gate to two states — publish iff PLUGIN_PUSH=ON, else
  skip. Removes the credentials-based auto-publish that caused the scatter and the races.
- build-packages.yml: set PLUGIN_PUSH=ON on the tag-triggered package build only. It already
  compiles every arch (amd64 then arm64) sequentially in one job, so it publishes all arches with
  no concurrent push / no ref race. This is the single publisher.
- All docker/nightly/dev/osc/slim builds leave PLUGIN_PUSH unset -> skip.
- doc/implementation/BUILD_PLUGIN_PUBLISHING.md: documents the rule + why the package build is the
  publisher + the wire-version guard as a recommended follow-up.

Reverted the earlier misdirected attempt to publish from the single-arch PRO docker image (would
have covered amd64 only). A one-time publish of the current wire set unblocks existing servers;
version resolution for non-release builds is a separate back-office change.

* build: strip v/V from tags and refuse to package non-digit versions

A capital-V tag (V3.1.35) slipped through 'sed s/^v//' and produced debs
with a dpkg-invalid Version field, poisoning the apt repo. Strip either
case and fail the build early if the derived version does not start with
a digit.

fix(cloud18): first-claimant domain ownership + surface real GitLab errors (#1617)

* fix(cloud18): enforce first-claimant domain ownership, surface GitLab errors

Cloud18 registration derived nothing useful from GitLab's error bodies: a
group create that failed because the path was already taken produced the
opaque 'API error: 400 - -' (the code parsed only error/error_description,
but GitLab returns validation errors under message, as a string OR a
field->reasons object). It then recursed into InitGroupAccessLevel on the
same unseeable group.

- Add gitlabErrorMessage() to extract a human message from all three GitLab
  error shapes, falling back to the raw body so nothing is dropped.
- CreateCloud18Domain classifies 'has already been taken' and returns the
  ErrDomainAlreadyOwned sentinel.
- InitGroupAccessLevel: on that sentinel, stop with an actionable message
  ('domain already registered to another account; ask its owner to grant
  access') instead of looping. A genuinely-new domain is still created and
  owned by the registering user — first-claimant ownership, enforced by
  GitLab, which is what makes open self-registration safe under the shared
  GitLab/Mattermost SSO.

This is the repman-side complement to disabling the BO email->domain
auto-membership pipeline.

* fix(config-sync): bootstrap first commit into an empty remote config repo

Regression from the ConfigManager config-sync refactor: cloneRepositoryWith-
Bootstrap only retried on repository-not-found, not ErrEmptyRemoteRepository.
A freshly-created (empty) Cloud18 config project therefore never received its
first commit — git.PlainClone returns ErrEmptyRemoteRepository, the push is
skipped, the repo stays empty, and GWARN002 re-fires every sync. Every repman
created before the refactor worked because the pre-ConfigManager push path
handled empty remotes.

On an empty remote, init a local repo pointed at the same URL on branch master
(matching ResolveCurrentLocalBranch) so the subsequent add/commit/push lands
the first commit and creates the remote's default branch.

Test: initRepositoryForEmptyRemote sets origin + master HEAD and is idempotent.

* harden(auth): bind API auth method to password presence

Make the API auth model explicit: an account with a password is LOCAL
(password auth only, SSO refused); an account with no password is an SSO
identity (OIDC only, local password refused). The registering owner
(Cloud18GitUser) is the single SSO account allowed to carry a credential.

- IsValidACL: OIDC refuses a password-protected account (except the owner);
  the password path refuses an empty stored or submitted password. GetAPIUser

stops an empty-password (SSO-provisioned or hand-written passwordless) entry
from being authenticated on the local password door.

by email only (no password). Default admin:repman and password-protected
accounts are unaffected.

fix(backup+config): abort backup on dead-volume stall; persist per-cluster settings across restart (#1622)

* fix(backup): abort logical backup on write-stall (dead/hung output volume)

A logical backup whose output volume disappears mid-run hangs forever: the
dead mount blocks splitdump's writes, back-pressures mariadb-dump and repman's
read loop, and JobBackupMysqldump parks on wg.Wait() with no timeout. The
source's --single-transaction read view stays open (pinning purge), and because
the goroutine never returns, the deferred InLogicalBackup clear never runs — so
the GUI STALLED pill won't clear even after the OS processes are killed.

- Add a write-stall watchdog: track bytes flowing through the read loop and, if
  none flow for backup-write-stall-timeout (default 300s, 0 disables), cancel
  the already-cancellable dumpCtx — killing both the dump and splitdump
  subprocesses so the backup returns a clear stall error instead of hanging.
  This is a stall timeout, not a total-time cap; long healthy dumps are
  unaffected. Returning unwinds the defers, clearing InLogicalBackup and
  releasing the source transaction.
- Stop the unconditional time.Sleep(3s) in JobsCheckFinished from taxing the
  monitoring hot path (Ping -> Refresh -> JobsCheckStates): sleep only when
  there is a finished job to flush.

Watchdog is a standalone, unit-tested helper (stall/progress/disabled cases).
Full root-cause + controllable-mount repro in
doc/implementation/cluster/BACKUP_DEAD_VOLUME_STALL.md.

* fix(config): honor monitoring-save-config flag default at startup load

Custom per-cluster settings (e.g. backup-mysqldump-options with --skip-ssl)
were saved to the datadir <cluster>/<cluster>.toml [saved-<cluster>] and git,
but silently reverted after a full repman restart.

Root cause: a save/load gate asymmetry. The SAVE path is gated on
conf.ConfRewrite (the monitoring-save-config pflag, default true), so saves
happen. The STARTUP load gate read firstRead.GetBool("default.monitoring-save-config")
which returns false when the key is absent from the config file, so InitConfig
skipped loading the datadir saved overlays entirely — the persisted section was
never merged. (Runtime reload via ReconstructLiveClusterConfig is not gated this
way, which is why it preserved the value while a restart did not.)

- monitoringSaveConfigEnabled(): default to the flag value when the key is
  absent, only use the file value when explicitly set. InitConfig uses it, so
  the load gate matches the save gate.
- Cluster.LastConfigSaveToDisk (API lastConfigSaveToDisk): stamped when the
  datadir <cluster>.toml is actually written, so the persistence can be observed
  and tested.

Tests: server_reload_test.go (gate default + saved-option survives reload),
regtest testConfigPersistBackupOption (live save round-trip).
Doc: doc/implementation/config/CONFIG_PERSISTENCE_SAVE_LOAD_GATE.md.

* feat(gui): show 'config last saved to disk' on the Settings page

Surfaces Cluster.LastConfigSaveToDisk (API lastConfigSaveToDisk) at the top of
the Settings page so operators can see whether/when a config change was actually
persisted to the datadir <cluster>.toml — the observability half of the
config-persistence fix. Real 'npm run build' passes.

* fix(backup): bound the post-cancel wait so a D-state hung mount can't hang the backup

Review follow-up (the must-do): the stall watchdog cancels via SIGKILL, but a
subprocess wedged in uninterruptible sleep (D-state) on a hard-hung NFS-style
mount never dies, so wg.Wait()/splitDumpPipeline.wg.Wait() could still hang
indefinitely AFTER cancellation — defeating the fix in exactly the incident's
worst case.

- boundedWait(): after the watchdog fires, wait at most backupStallLeakGrace
  (60s) for the reader/pipeline goroutines to unwind; if they don't, return the
  stall error and leak the stuck goroutine rather than hang. The backup call
  always unwinds now (clears InLogicalBackup, releases the source transaction),
  even when the OS process is unkillable.
- Warn when backup-write-stall-timeout is negative (silent-disable vs typo).
- Add backup-write-stall-timeout to etc/config.toml sample.
- Doc: detection-latency note + best-effort/D-state limitation callout.

Test: TestBoundedWait_LeaksStuckGoroutineAfterStall.

fix(monitor): run logical reseed off the tick (unblock monitor during restore) (#1626)

* fix(monitor): run logical reseed off the tick, unblocking the monitor loop

A splitdump/mysqldump reseed was dispatched INLINE from StateProcessing, which
runs inline in tickBody — so the whole cluster monitor loop froze inside the
restore for its entire (multi-minute) duration: no health checks, no failover
(not even if the master died mid-reseed), and concurrent slave reseeds
serialized on the single tick goroutine. Confirmed from a goroutine profile
taken during a restore (Run -> tickBody -> StateProcessing -> ProcessReseedLogical
-> splitdump.Restore on the tick goroutine).

Dispatch the reseed via trackTickGoroutine, mirroring the WARN0111 async reseed
path directly below. The per-server IsReseeding flag (claimed atomically by
ProcessReseedLogical via TrySetInReseedBackup) prevents a later tick from
starting a second reseed for the same server, and rejoin/switchover already
refuse a reseeding server — so unblocking the monitor is a net safety gain:
the master can now fail over during a slave reseed, and two slaves genuinely
reseed in parallel.

Orchestrator hot-path change: validate on the OpenSVC topology matrix before
merge.

* rejoin: async everywhere + reconcile the async-reseed record

Make the topology extra-master caller go-spawned (cluster_topo.go) — the last
synchronous RejoinMaster caller — so every rejoin edge runs off the monitor tick.

Because the logical/physical backup reseed only ARMS WARN0075/WARN0074 and returns
while the restore runs off-tick, finishRejoin was recording success at arm time,
before the restore ran. Defer the record to reseed completion:
- recordOrDeferRejoin(): records now for a synchronous restore (RejoinDirectDump),
  or sets reseedFromRejoin and defers when an async reseed is in flight
- WARN0074/WARN0075 completion handlers reconcile finishRejoin with the real
  ProcessReseed* outcome (finishRejoin then clear, so the one-shot has no gap)
- RejoinMaster holds the one-shot while a reseed is in flight
  (HasAnyReseedingState || reseedFromRejoin)

No retry semantics changed — the record is one-shot either way; it is only made
honest for the async paths. Docs: execution model, full rejoin workflow (triggers/
gates/per-path states), and the WARN0189 reseed-progress coverage gap.

* rejoin: fix async-reseed record — reconcile from observed health at true completion

Review of the previous commit found two real regressions, both because the
reconciliation was hooked to the WARN handler return values, which for most reseed
methods fire before the detached restore goroutine even starts:

- WARN0074 physical: ProcessReseedPhysical arms 'go WaitAndSendSST -> go SSTRunSender'
  and returns nil, so reconciling on its return recorded success at ARM time.
- direct mysqldump: RejoinDirectDump spawns 'go JobRejoinMysqldumpFromSource' and
  returns nil with no WARN state, so reseedFromRejoin was NEVER cleared -> RejoinMaster
  permanently blocked for that server.

The only signal every reseed method shares is clearing IsReseeding on completion, and
none carries a uniform success/fail return. So:
- remove the WARN0074/WARN0075 handler reconciliation (wrong hook);
- add reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds (per tick, before assertRejoinResultStates):
  record finishRejoin from OBSERVED health at IsReseeding-clear — healthy slave of the
  current master = success, else failed (self-corrects to 'recovered' via
  assertRejoinResultStates once it becomes a healthy slave);
- generic WARN0189 'rejoin reseed in progress, started T' (rejoinReseedStart) for
  methods without byte instrumentation, so a rejoin is always visible in the GUI and
  its landing outcome is the proof the reconciliation works.

Docs corrected: the per-method completion table (all async), the observed-health
reconcile, and the generic progress state.

* rejoin: update stale comments to reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds (review #1626)

The guard comment and recordOrDeferRejoin doc still described the removed
WARN0074/WARN0075 handler reconcile; point them at the observed-health
reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds. Comment-only.

* gui: live reseed/rejoin progress panel + per-server reseedProgress API

Backend: ServerMonitor.GetReseedProgress() snapshots the in-flight restore
(bytes/total/percent + generic rejoin timer from rejoinReseedStart), attached to
GET /topology/servers as server.reseedProgress (nil when idle).

Frontend: a Navbar 'Reseed' pill appears while any server restores and opens a
ReseedProgressModal showing per-server Chakra Progress bars (byte-instrumented
methods) or an indeterminate timer + 'started T' line (methods without byte
counting). crashPill now excludes WARN0189 (in-progress reseed is informational,
shown by the Reseed pill) so a normal reseed no longer red-blinks the crash pill.
Pure logic extracted to utility/reseedProgress.js with node tests.

The panel showing a rejoin start -> stream -> land its true outcome is the visible
proof the reconcileDeferredRejoinReseeds fix works.

splitdump: native Go transactional restore (replace mysql --force) + reseed progress (#1627)

* fix(splitdump): native Go transactional restore, no more mysql --force

Replace the mysql --force subprocess with a native Go loader:
- one dedicated pinned *sqlx.Conn per worker (never the shared pool), so
  session state (USE/FK/UNIQUE) and transaction affinity hold
- INSERT/REPLACE batched into transactions, retried on deadlock (1213) /
  lock-wait-timeout (1205); any other error is returned (fail loud)
- LOCK/UNLOCK TABLES and ALTER..DISABLE/ENABLE KEYS dropped; DELIMITER honored
- binlog on/off follows the master/slave decision via GetConnNoBinlog;
  reset uses version-aware server.ResetMaster()

Fixes silent data loss: --force skipped failing statements and exited 0, so
executeMysqlRestoreContext (which only read stderr on non-zero exit) reported
success while the first shard's rows were dropped under N-way parallel load.

* test(splitdump): synthetic manifest-completeness guard for multi-shard split

* feat(splitdump): reseed progress (WARN0189) for the native-Go loader

The monolithic mysqldump path reports streamed-bytes progress via WARN0189, but
the splitdump reseed (per-table shard files) showed only a silent 'processing'.

Add beginReseedProgress (stamp the in-flight restore, total = sum of shard sizes)
+ countReseedReader (wrap each shard reader into one accumulating byte counter),
and wire them into restoreSplitdumpWithMysql / restoreSplitdumpFileGo so a
splitdump reload shows the same live '<streamed> out of <total>' line per tick.

* refactor(splitdump): remove dead mysql --force CLI restore path

restoreSplitdumpFileContextWithPreamble, restoreSplitdumpFileContextStripDefiner,
and buildSplitdumpRestorePreamble were the old subprocess (mysql --force) restore
path, fully replaced by the native-Go transactional loader. Production no longer
calls them (only their tests did). Remove the functions and their tests.

* fix(splitdump): honor continueOnError for INSERT batches (mysql.system-all) + parser tests

Review #1627: continueOnError (the old --force tolerance for mysql.system-all seed
rows) only reached execSplitdumpSingle, never execSplitdumpBatch — so system-all
INSERTs went through the transactional batch path and would hard-abort the entire
restore on the first conflicting seed row (pre-existing default account, time_zone).

Refactor the streamer into pure, testable pieces:
- classifySplitdumpStatement (skip/insert/other),
- forEachSplitdumpStatement (DELIMITER-aware segmentation, no DB),
- planAndExecSplitdump (routing) driven by an injectable splitdumpExecutor.

When continueOnError, INSERT/REPLACE now run individually (single, coe=true) so one
bad seed row is skipped instead of rolling back the whole transaction — matching the
old --force. Add parser + continueOnError regression tests (no live DB). Also note
the per-worker *sqlx.DB rationale.

* docs(splitdump): fix orphaned comment — doc the streamSplitdumpStatements wrapper (review #1627)

The old function doc was left above type splitdumpStmtKind after the refactor;
move a concise version onto the wrapper and drop the orphan. Comment-only.

Nightly images sign their own dev plugins with the official key but never
published them, so the BO fell back to the stale release wire-vN set — whose
binaries don't match the image's dev .sig -> WARN0206 (signature mismatch).

Add a PLUGIN_CHANNEL=nightly publish path:
- Makefile: nightly publishes binaries to plugins/<platform>/nightly/<FULLVERSION>/
  and creates symlink replication-manager-<FULLVERSION> -> that dir (keyed on the

replication-manager-<repmgr_version> exactly, falling back to highest wire only
when the symlink is absent. Release path unchanged (PLUGIN_CHANNEL defaults to
release). Same build produces the image .sig and the published binary -> match.

configurator: floor every allocated engine buffer at 128M (fix innodb_buffer_pool_size=0M) (#1656)

GetConfigInnoDBBPSize (and the myisam/aria/tokudb/querycache/s3/rocksdb
siblings) computed a buffer size as (usable_mem * pct / 100), where
usable_mem = prov-db-memory - memReserveMB(2048). For any prov-db-memory <= 2GB
usable clamps to 0, so the buffer emitted 0M. InnoDB with a 16K page size refuses
to start below 6 MiB, so a small/misresolved prov-db-memory (observed: a db
provisioned at 256M) produced innodb_buffer_pool_size=0M and the DB would not boot.

Add a shared engineMemMB() floor: an ENABLED engine (share pct > 0) never gets
less than minEngineMemMB (128M); a DISABLED engine (pct <= 0) stays at 0 so we
never silently turn on a feature meant to be off (e.g. the query cache).

Fixes the test that asserted the broken value (256M -> 0) and adds a guard that a
0%-share engine is not floored.

Note (separate follow-up): ConfigDiscovery() reverse-derives prov-db-memory by
summing the live buffer variables, which can shrink it over restarts; that loop is
why prov-db-memory became 256 and still needs addressing.

fix(gitsync): exclude runtime data dirs from git so push stops walking the WorkingDir (#1712)

The git config WorkingDir doubles as the runtime data dir, so it can hold tens
of GB of untracked bulk (backups/, per-cluster backup/, graphite/, *.log,
goroutine.txt, caches, certs). go-git's add/status walks and hashes every
untracked file not covered by .gitignore, so each config push spent minutes
hashing bulk data before committing a few KB of config — while the pull stayed
~1s to the same remote. As backups accumulate the push overruns the sync cycle
and GWARN013@gitsync flaps every cycle, risking starvation of the monitor.

Add AddDataDirsToGitignore (wired into PushAllConfigsToGit next to the existing
AddPullToGitignore / AddTempDirToGitignore / AddConfigSyncToGitignore) to exclude
that bulk, keeping go-git's worktree scan cheap. Non-destructive — nothing is
deleted, only left out of the sync; cert/key material must not be in the config

fix(prov): serialize errorChan provisioning ops with a per-cluster mutex

Phase 1 mitigation for #1769. The shared, unbuffered cluster.errorChan is
used by ~10 provision/unprovision receivers (prov.go + srv.go Uprovision)

cross-talk on it: one receiver reads the other op's result and the other
blocks forever, deadlocking orchestration and leaving a server stuck in
maintenance with no log.

covers every channel user) while preserving fan-out parallelism (per-server
goroutines still run in parallel under one hold), cross-cluster parallelism,

e.g. OpenSVCGetDBEnvSection) is left to the Phase 2 per-operation-channel

fix(prov): guarantee the reseed on rolling reprovision (#1771)

RollingReprov destroys each replica's data (UnprovisionDatabaseService) then
recreates an empty service. The reseed that repopulates it is delegated to the
autoseed rejoin path (RejoinMaster -> ReseedMasterSST), which fires only when
Conf.Autorejoin AND Conf.Autoseed are on -- and ReseedMasterSST itself needs a
reseed METHOD armed (autorejoin-mysqldump / backup-load-script /
autorejoin-logical-backup / autorejoin-physical-backup), otherwise it logs
"No SST reseed method found" and leaves the replica empty. With the defaults
(autoseed off, no method), a reprov left the replicas destroyed and empty --
silent data loss.

Guarantee the reseed before destroying anything:
- refuse to run if autorejoin is disabled (srv.go gates the rejoin trigger on
  it; forcing it globally would change failover for every other server, so we
  abort with a clear error instead of piloting it);
- pilot autoseed on for the duration, and if the operator has armed no reseed
  method, pilot autorejoin-mysqldump on (a direct dump from the master, always
  available, no pre-existing backup needed); a method the operator did choose
  is kept. All piloted values are restored afterwards.

Validated live on a dev OpenSVC cluster: without the method pilot the reprov
logged "No SST reseed method found" and left the replicas empty; with it each
reprovisioned replica is reseeded from the master.

fix(prov): guard RollingReprov against concurrent runs (reentrancy)

Addresses review point 1 on #1772. RollingReprov pilots the shared
Conf.Autoseed / Conf.AutorejoinMysqldump flags for its duration and restores

fix(rm): memory occupancy is not a scaling signal -- drop mem axis from scale states

A healthy InnoDB buffer pool is always ~full (clean+dirty pages, adaptive hash index,
change buffer), so dbu_mem (cgroup memory.current occupancy) is pinned near the cap
regardless of load. It never legitimately means "grow" (always saturated -> CINF0007
fired on idle) and never means "shrink" (memory is sticky, the pool does not release
on idle). So CheckResourceConsumed now excludes the mem axis (dropMem) from all four
consumed-vs-reference states.

Growth is driven by the DEMAND axes -- CPU usage and IO saturation (+ disk usage), which
ARE mean-rate/usage sensors. Real memory NEED surfaces AS IO (a too-small buffer pool
causes Innodb_buffer_pool_reads misses -> disk reads, seen on the io axis). Memory shrink
is the deliberate reclaim path, never an occupancy trigger.

Follow-up: a pressure-based mem grow signal (Innodb_buffer_pool_reads/wait_free/hit-ratio,
already emitted to graphite) to split an io-saturation trigger into grow-iops vs grow-memory.

git-sync: self-heal corrupt-pack push failure + git-push/git-repair API

A gitlab failover that emptied the config repos left repman unable to push:
go-git builds a full pack that includes corrupt/dangling local objects, the
remote's receive-side fsck (transfer.fsckObjects=true) rejects it
("unpack error: unpack-objects abnormal exit" client-side, "fatal: object of
unexpected type" in gitaly), and it looped forever as a persistent GERR002.

The self-heal scaffold already existed (classifyRecoverablePushError ->
RefreshGitMetadata reclone -> retry once) but did not classify this error, so
it never fired. RefreshGitMetadata re-inits the local .git from the remote
(cloneRepositoryWithBootstrap bootstraps a fresh empty repo for an empty
remote), shedding the dangling objects, so the retry pushes a clean pack.

 - classifyRecoverablePushError: classify "unpack error" / "unpack-objects" /
   "abnormal exit" / "object of unexpected type" as recoverable -> the existing
   reclone+retry now fires (bounded to one per cycle; degrades, never loops).
 - RepairAndPush: explicit reclone-then-push for the on-demand API action.

Also adds the missing operability/testability flow (there was no API to push
or repair git; it only ever fired dirty-gated in the sync loop):
 - POST /api/clusters/{name}/settings/actions/git-push   -> force push now
 - POST /api/clusters/{name}/settings/actions/git-repair  -> reclone + push
Both serialized with the sync worker via the git lock; server-level (one repo),
routed per-cluster for ACL.

configurator: clamp innodb read/write io threads to MariaDB max (64)

GetConfigInnoDBWriteIoThreads (Little's-law: iopsLatency*iops) and
GetConfigInnoDBReadIoThreads (=ProvCores) had no upper bound, so a large plan
produced a value above MariaDB's hard maximum of 64 for innodb_read_io_threads /
innodb_write_io_threads -- e.g. > 32 DBU of IOPS, or a > 64-core config -- and the
live SET GLOBAL from the io/cpu resize would then fail out of range, exactly at the
large plans where the resize matters most. Both now clamp to [1, 64]
(clampInnoDBIoThreads); read-threads also parses defensively.

auth: reconcile stale `system` service-account password on every user load

The `system` API-key account is created once and persisted, but a user created by
an older binary (before AddUser honoured an explicit password, e6c6df4ca) got a
RANDOM password, and EnsureSystemServiceUser skips an existing user -- so the drift
was never corrected and the compute sensor's derived-key login failed with "invalid
credentials" (observed on dev3). A SecretKey change would drift it the same way.

Fix: reconcileSystemServicePassword() forces the in-memory `system` credential to the
current derived key (GetSystemAPIKey) at the end of LoadAPIUsers, so every load path
(startup + each dynamic config reload) repairs it. Auth compares this in-memory map
(IsValidACL), so this is the reliable fix -- no fragile per-value secret rewrite, and
recursion-safe (unlike EnsureSystemServiceUser, which may AddUser -> LoadAPIUsers).

fix: resolve WriteBackupMetadata self-deadlock + JobsCheckStates api-mode 1146 storm

Two independent backup/job bugs found while investigating belair/db2 stuck
in reseed for a day after a failover during a demo.

1) WriteBackupMetadata self-deadlock (cluster/srv_job_backup.go)
   The function held server.backupMetaMutex for its whole body, including
   two unbounded `for { time.Sleep(time.Second) }` poll loops waiting on
   task.State and lastmeta.BinLogFileName. But BinLogFileName is set by the
   writelog API path *under the same mutex*, so the waiter blocked forever
   on a value only settable by acquiring the lock it was holding. Any later
   backup-meta op (including the flashback auto-rejoin's
   snapshotLogicalBackupMeta and the manual logical rejoin) then wedged
   behind it -- db2 never actually reseeded.
   Fix: release backupMetaMutex around each poll loop and re-acquire before
   mutating; all metadata mutations stay guarded.

2) JobsCheckStates missing api-mode guard (cluster/srv_job.go)
   JobsCheckStates polled the SQL jobs table unconditionally; in
   scheduler-jobs-mode=api that table does not exist, producing an
   ERROR 1146 storm every tick. Mirror JobsCheckRunning's guard and return
   early when SchedulerJobsMode == "api".

WaitObjectConfigSettledV3 compared the target node's loaded csum with the
md5 of GET /object/.../config/file -- a read the API node proxies to an
instance node, which for a service living elsewhere still holds the OLD
file for ~250 ms after the PUT. md5(old) == csum(old), the wait returned at
once and the pg update applied the previous quota: every live cpu/memory
resize (and the rolling-restart template push) landed one push behind on
nodes other than opensvc-host (dev3: db1/db2 one step late on three
consecutive pushes; om3 journals in #1795).

The reference is now the API node's own file, GET /node/name/_/instance/
path/.../config/file -- the route om3 peers use to fetch a fresh foreign
config -- with the proxied read as fallback once the API node dropped its
foreign copy (by then the peers have it). Regression test with an httptest
om3 that serves old on the proxied route and new on the node route: the
wait must not return before the loaded csum reaches the new md5.

monitor: replication parallelism signal -- binlog group commit size vs parallel workers, per server, emitted to Graphite and graphed

Group commit size = Binlog_commits / Binlog_group_commits deltas per tick:
transactions committed in the same group are known conflict-free, so this
is the commit concurrency a slave can apply in parallel on this master's
binlog (conservative mode floor). Tracked as server.ReplicationGroupCommitSize
next to QPS, with server.ReplicationParallelThreads (slave_parallel_threads /
slave_parallel_workers as the server runs it). Both emitted to Graphite as
mysql.<host>.replication_group_commit_size / replication_parallel_threads
(direct, like the slave status metrics), and graphed on the cluster Graphs
page as 'Replication parallelism' after the replication delay chart. Basis
for the workers tuner (decision 2026-09-16: workers are concurrency, not
cores) -- the number to look at before fixing 32.

Review on #1808: UNIQUE(a) was reported as covered by UNIQUE(a,b), and
dropping it would change the data-integrity semantics (UNIQUE(a,b) allows two

duplicate, whatever the covering index. Same rule for FULLTEXT/SPATIAL:

not covered. The finding text now carries the BTREE/HASH caveat the package
doc promised. Tests for all three.

switchover: wait for long writes to complete (bounded by switchover-wait-trx) instead of refusing at once; never kill them

The long-write guard in MasterFailover runs before anything is frozen or locked on the
master, so waiting there costs the application nothing. Instead of refusing on the first
count it now re-checks every 2 s for at most switchover-wait-trx seconds and proceeds as
soon as the long writes are gone. Still there at the deadline: refuse, with one log line
per offending session (id, user, host, running time, transaction age, rows modified and
locked, query). They are never killed: the rollback of a killed transaction runs unbounded
on the server about to be demoted, and nothing can stop or shorten it.

  the switchover-wait-write-query row renamed "Switchover Long Write Threshold"

switchover: WARN0217 open state while the long-write guard waits (tracked fact, asserted per tick)

While waitLongRunningWrites waits for the long writes, the GUI only showed ERR00001
("monitor freeze") with no hint of what the switchover was doing. The wait is now a
tracked fact on the cluster (SwitchoverLongWriteWait: server, count, since, deadline,
exposed in the cluster JSON), set for the duration of the wait and cleared after, and
CheckFailed asserts WARN0217 from it on every tick, next to ERR00001, so the state opens
when the wait starts and resolves when it ends. Never re-derived from logs.

switchover: WARN0217 set from the guard itself with the wait's outcome (no tick runs during a switchover)

The per-tick assertion never fired: the switchover runs on the monitor goroutine
(cluster.Run's select on switchoverChan), so there is no tick, no state processing
and no alert until MasterFailover returns. Same limitation as ERR00100, which is why
it is set from inside the switchover and opens at the first tick after. WARN0217 now
does the same: set when the wait starts, rewritten with the outcome before the guard
returns ("completed after Ns, switchover proceeding" or "still running after
switchover-wait-trx=Ns, switchover cancelled"), so the alert that opens tells what
happened. The live signal during the wait is the cluster JSON fact
switchoverLongWriteWait, served directly from memory (verified on dev3).

Fed by the cluster object's switchoverLongWriteWait (present for the duration of the wait,

switchover: its crash record ends "no-divergence" (stamped by the switchover, by pointer); rejoin one-shot guard scoped to the current event; Crashes modal renders the outcome

A switchover appended its record to the working set (cluster.Crashes) and never
finished it: the old master is re-slaved by the switchover itself, never by the
rejoin path that stamps outcomes. The record sat forever with no result and no
delta, and the Crashes modal could only show "not analyzed" + Lost Events for an
event that has no divergent tail by construction (old master frozen under FTWRL,
candidate caught up before promotion).

- MasterFailover: once CHANGE MASTER and START SLAVE succeeded on the old master,
  finishCrashRecord(crash, RejoinResultNoDivergence): out of the working set, crash.json
  rewritten, history reloaded. A failed demotion leaves the record as before.
- finishCrashRecord ends ONE record by pointer (finishRejoin still resolves by URL;
  both share finishCrash), so a stale working crash of the same URL is never mistaken.
- rejoinAlreadyAttempted: an outcome older than the newest working crash for that URL
  no longer blocks (it predates the current event). Without this the stamped switchover
  would swallow the ex-master's next real automatic rejoin; a "success" outcome already
  did, so this also fixes that pre-existing one-shot over-reach. Unit tests.
- CrashesModal: rejoinResult "no-divergence" with nothing analyzed renders a green
  "none" badge and no Lost Events button; captured deltas keep their verdict badges.
